This study systematically investigates the transport and retention behaviour of polyethylene (PE; ρ = 0.92 g cm⁻³) and polystyrene (PS; ρ = 1.10 g cm⁻³) MPs through fine gravel under controlled hydrodynamic regimes using six large-scale columns (110 cm × 24 cm). Continuous, pulsed, and single-pulse infiltration conditions were applied to simulate contrasting recharge scenarios. Effluent and pore-water MP were collected over 503 h at multiple depths (20-80 cm), and sediment subsets were analysed post-experiment to quantify MP retention and recovery. Results demonstrated strong flow-dependent MP transport. Continuous infiltration produced earlier breakthrough, whereas pulsed flow generated episodic MP concentration peaks associated with rewetting events and enhanced pore-water velocities. Pulsed infiltration also increased the first temporal moment of both polymer types, indicating sustained particle transport and prolonged recovery at the column outlet. Contrarily, single-pulse infiltration resulted in limited MP downward transport. PS-MPs showed earlier breakthrough, while polymer-specific transport differences generally decreased with increasing transport depth. MPs <45 µm preferentially showed early transport, while particles >50 µm were mobilised later. MP recoveries ranged from 104% to 126% with 51% to 67% of the particles retained within the upper 10 cm of the sediment profile. Our findings demonstrate that hydrodynamic conditions, particle size, and polymer-specific properties influence MP transport and retention in subsurface sediments, highlighting the importance of transient conditions in regulating MP mobility and potential groundwater contamination.

tag.summary: Hydrodynamic controls on vertical microplastic transport in subsurface sediments; an environmental fate study.

paper.title: Microplastic pollution in Greek seas: Abundance, spatio-temporal dynamics, potential sources and post-storm amplification.
paper.abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution represents an increasing threat to coastal and marine ecosystems, yet data from Greek waters remain scarce. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of MP abundance, spatial distribution, polymer composition, and seasonal variability in surface waters and sediments collected from 27 coastal sites in Greece between 2021 and 2024. Sampling was combined with Fourier - Transform Infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy polymer identification and satellite-derived Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM) data, available for a subset of sites, to explore hydrodynamic influences on MP distribution and the effects of extreme events. The impact of Storm Daniel on the Pagasitikos Gulf was particularly notable, with a sharp and sustained increase in both SPM and MP concentrations persisting for over a year following coastal flooding. Seasonal analysis showed higher MP levels during winter and early spring, coinciding with elevated SPM and with periods that are climatologically associated with increased precipitation and runoff in Greece. Polymer analysis indicated that polyolefins (PE and PP) comprised approximately half of the detected MPs in both matrices, followed by PS in sediments and cellulose and PET in seawater. Morphologically, fragments and films were the most common MP types, particularly in highly impacted locations. MP concentrations exhibited strong spatial variability, ranging from 0 to 240.8 items/m2 in sediments and 0.0008 to 0.1637 items/m3 in surface waters. Overall, the results indicate that storm-driven runoff and hydrodynamic conditions can play an important role in mobilising MPs from terrestrial sources to coastal environments, particularly in semi-enclosed gulfs. This study provides new evidence linking extreme weather events, SPM dynamics, and MP transport in parts of the Greek coastal environment, offering insights for pollution monitoring and management strategies.

tag.summary: Microplastic abundance and post-storm amplification measured in Greek seas; an environmental survey.

paper.title: Plastiome in seagrass meadows: higher health risk of plastisphere beneath leaf canopy than that in root sediment.
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) act as vectors for disseminating antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) across ecosystems, posing potential threats to environmental and public health. Seagrass meadows serve as vital ecotones between land and sea, where MPs pollution is widely recognized. However, plastisphere resistome (plastiome) in this ecosystem and its modulation by native phyllosphere and rhizosphere microbiomes remain poorly understood. Herein, MPs were in-situ exposed to seagrass meadows to investigate differences in resistome profiles of phyllosphere-associated (SL-MPs) vs. rhizosphere-associated plastisphere (SR-MPs). The potential health risk was evaluated by profiling ARGs, virulence factor genes (VFGs)-associated pathogenicity and mobile genetic elements (MGEs)-mediated motility. Results showed that SL‑MPs harbored more abundant putative pathogens, ARGs and VFGs than SR-MPs. Specifically, SL-MPs were dominated by WHO critical-priority pathogens Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae, and enriched ARGs conferring multidrug resistance. Additionally, SL‑MPs exhibited greater potential health risks and more abundant high-risk ARGs (e.g., bacA and floR). These traits appeared to be primarily associated with the dense biofilms, high cell motility, pronounced reactive oxygen species response, DNA recombination and distinct membrane features of plastisphere beneath leaf canopy. Since phyllosphere-associated plastisphere can be readily dispersed by waves to other coastal ecosystems, it is necessary to integrate ecological connectivity into "One Health" frameworks.

tag.summary: Antibiotic resistance genes compared between seagrass canopy and sediment plastispheres; an environmental microbiology study.

paper.title: Physics-Guided Active Learning Enables Energy-Filtering Flexible Thermoelectric Composites for Self-Powered Wound Bioelectronics.
paper.abstract: Thermoelectric stimulation offers a self-powered intervention for accelerated wound healing by converting physiological thermal gradients into sustained micro-electric fields. However, the development of flexible thermoelectric materials is constrained by the coupled dependence of electrical conductivity and the Seebeck coefficient, which empirical screening alone is inefficient for exploring the large number of possible interfaces. We developed a small-data, literature-derived, physics-guided screening and design framework that integrates Bayesian optimization with eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) regression and subsequent experimental validation. Using 18 physics-informed descriptors selected by recursive feature elimination, the framework predicts interfacial energy barriers within the literature-derived data domain with a test R2 of 0.87, enabling targeted barrier engineering that partially decouples the thermoelectric parameters. The model and practical screening criteria were used to select five composite systems for synthesis and experimental evaluation, supporting the applicability of the algorithm. Among the experimentally validated systems, poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene): poly(styrene sulfonate)/eutectic gallium-indium (PEDOT:PSS/EGaIn) flexible composite exhibited a measured interfacial energy barrier of 0.24 eV, close to the predicted effective filtering range, and achieved a Seebeck coefficient of 40.0 µV K-1. Under a mild physiological-to-ambient temperature gradient of 25 K, the flexible thermoelectric device generated an open-circuit voltage of 8.80 mV. In the scratch assay, the stimulated group showed 34.5% closure compared with 13.9% in the untreated control. In the rat wound model, the thermoelectric group reached near-complete closure approximately two days earlier than the sham and untreated groups. This data-driven approach provides a physical framework for screening energy-filtering composites and evaluating their potential in self-powered bioelectronic therapeutics.

tag.summary: Active learning used to design flexible thermoelectric composites for wound bioelectronics; a materials paper.

paper.title: Microplastics in freshwater environments across the high altitude region of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.
paper.abstract: Microplastics are increasingly recognized as pervasive contaminants in remote mountain freshwater ecosystems, yet evidence from high-altitude regions remains limited. This study investigated microplastics occurrence and characteristics in surface water, sediments, and fish from the Braldu-Shigar-Skardu freshwater system in Gilgit-Baltistan, northern Pakistan. Samples were collected from remote headwaters, tributaries, main river channels, and the Satpara Lake-Dam system. Fish originated from wild populations, farming facilities, and local markets to provide a broader assessment of microplastic exposure. Matrix-specific extraction protocols were applied, followed by stereomicroscope sorting and polymer identification by µFT-IR spectroscopy. Microplastics were detected in nearly all sites and matrices, with concentrations ranging from 1 to 17 MPs L-1 in water, 55-537 MPs kg-1 in sediments, and 1-11 MPs individual-1 in fish gastrointestinal tracts. Notably, highest frequency of microplastics occurrence was measured in farmed individuals (78%-83%), suggesting that aquaculture-related practices may represent an additional source of microplastics. Wild fish showed the lowest occurrence (25%), whereas those obtained from local markets revealed intermediate values (62%), indicating variable exposure across different pathways. Surface waters were dominated by small fragments and polypropylene, indicative of recent inputs and origin from fragmentation. Sediments showed a broader size distribution, and greater polymer diversity, consistent with their role as long-term sinks. The highest polymer diversity was highlighted in fish, indicating multiple exposure pathways. Spatial patterns did not show a geographical downstream increase, but rather a patchy distribution shaped by local anthropogenic input, hydrological connectivity, and depositional dynamics. Glacier-fed rivers primarily act as transport corridors, whereas low-energy environments such as Satpara Lake function as sinks promoting microplastics accumulation. Overall, the study provides the first integrated multi-compartment baseline for microplastics in Gilgit-Baltistan and supports future monitoring and management actions for these high altitude critical freshwater resources.

tag.summary: Microplastics measured in high-altitude freshwater systems in Pakistan; an environmental survey.

paper.title: Microplastic contamination in Ramsar wetlands: a systematic review of global sources, ecological impacts, and policy implications.
paper.mesh: Wetlands; Environmental Monitoring; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Microplastics; Environmental Policy; Geologic Sediments; Ecosystem
paper.abstract: Ramsar wetlands, globally recognized for their ecological, hydrological, and socio-economic significance, are increasingly threatened by microplastic (MP) contamination. Despite mounting evidence of MPs in freshwater and coastal environments, no global synthesis has focused on MP contamination in Ramsar-designated wetlands. This study presents the first systematic global review of MP contamination in Ramsar wetlands by compiling peer-reviewed studies (April 2012-May 2025). This review addresses MP sources, transport pathways, contamination levels in surface water, sediment, and biota especially in threatened species, ecosystem impacts, and mitigation efforts. Key findings from quartile analysis and descriptive statistics reveal that MPs are ubiquitous across Ramsar wetland compartments, with spatial patterns showing higher contamination in Asia, North and South America, and lower levels in Europe and Australia. Certain countries' Ramsar wetlands consistently emerged as hotspots across all three environmental compartments, surface water, sediments, and biota, including Ecuador, China, India, and Ghana. Temporal trends indicate rising MP loads over the past decade, and seasonal peaks linked to runoff in some regions. Polyethylene and polypropylene were the most common polymers (> 80%), with fibres and fragments as the predominant morphotypes. Sediments generally harboured the highest MP concentrations, while biota exhibited variable uptake. These results underscore an urgent need for standardized monitoring methods and more geographically balanced research, especially in under-studied regions such as Africa and South America, to enable robust global comparisons. We recommend prioritizing plastic source reduction, enhancing international collaboration, and integrating MP pollution control into wetland conservation policies to safeguard the ecological integrity of Ramsar wetlands.

tag.summary: Systematic review of microplastic contamination in Ramsar wetlands with policy implications; an ecology review.

paper.title: Photoinduced weathering of plastics and implications for spectral inclusion into matching database for laser direct infrared spectroscopy identification.
paper.abstract: Microplastics are a ubiquitous environmental contaminant that can be found virtually every habitat and water source around the world. Therefore, there is great interest in developing efficient and reliable methodologies for the identification and enumeration of microplastics from environmental media. Laser direct infrared spectroscopy (LDIR) utilizes the fingerprint region of infrared (IR) spectra to make identification of plastics and other materials during analysis. However, only pristine spectra of plastics are currently used in the identification process. It has been well documented that the IR spectra of plastics changes considerably upon photochemical weathering, bringing into question whether databases may lead to misidentification of certain polymer types. To test if weathering influences identification of microplastics by LDIR, nine different plastics were irradiated to simulate weathering from 3 to 13 years in the sun. The physical and chemical changes of the plastic were measured by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) respectively. The weathered polymers were analyzed by LDIR-transflectance spectroscopy and resulting spectra were loaded into the LDIR matching database. This updated database was used to analyze samples from a local wastewater treatment plant with and without the inclusion of weathered spectra. This manuscript shows the inclusion of weathered transflectance spectra into the LDIR matching database can increase polymer identifications by 9.6 - 10.2% in wastewater samples on average. It also reveals that not all polymers are increased in identification uniformly, as PC and PA show the most sizeable increased spectral matches. However, most polymers tested were able to show increased medium and high-quality matches of weathered polymers using this approach.

tag.summary: Photoinduced weathering of plastics assessed for spectral database matching; a method paper.

paper.title: Microplastics in freshwater aquaculture: Evidence of sediment-fish transfer and associated ecological risks in Bangladesh.
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in aquaculture systems in Bangladesh threaten ecosystem health and food safety. This study examined MPs in surface sediments and farmed fish from 25 aquaculture ponds in Trishal Upazila, Mymensingh. Most sites were moderately to highly polluted, with a pollution load index (PLI) ranging from 1.0 to 4.5, while mean sediment MPs concentrations were 11.04 ± 3.75 particles kg-1. For fish, a total of 90 MPs were detected, with a mean abundance of 0.60 ± 1.16 MPs fish-1. Demersal fish (52%) demonstrated the greatest ingestion rates, followed by benthopelagic (35%) and pelagic species (13%). The major polymers detected were PE and PP, showing ubiquitous plastic origins in aquaculture and household activities. Frequency of occurrence (FO%) ranging from 16% to 40% revealed uneven fish species MPs ingestion rate. Fulton's condition factor (K: 0.35-2.27) varied among species, with lower values observed in Catla catla and Pangasius pangasius, which also showed relatively higher MPs ingestion. Higher bioconcentration (BCF) values in Cirrhinus cirrhosus, Cyprinus carpio and Pangasius pangasius indicating MPs magnification through the food chain. Overall, the widespread ingestion of MP by cultured fish highlights their potential ecological impacts within Bangladesh's aquaculture systems and underscores the urgent need for targeted monitoring and sustainable management strategies to mitigate MP contamination.

tag.summary: Sediment to fish transfer of microplastics documented in Bangladeshi aquaculture; an occurrence survey.

paper.title: A versatile Bacillus esterase reveals a carboxylesterase blueprint for PET intermediate degradation.
paper.mesh: Bacillus; Polyethylene Terephthalates; Carboxylesterase; Hydrogen-Ion Concentration; Substrate Specificity; Carboxylic Ester Hydrolases; Temperature; Kinetics; Biodegradation, Environmental; Esterases; Enzyme Stability; Bacterial Proteins; Burkholderiales
paper.abstract: The biodegradation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and its derived intermediate breakdown products, represents a core focus of multidisciplinary research. While Ideonella sakaiensis PETase (IsPETase) and leaf-compost cutinase (LCC) efficiently depolymerize PET, many other PET-active hydrolases display stronger activity toward soluble PET intermediates such as bis- and mono(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET and MHET). Here, we describe a versatile carboxylesterase derived from Bacillus halotolerans (BhEstB). BhEstB is structurally related to BsEstB from B. subtilis but divergent from canonical PETases and most characterized MHETases, including IsMHETase, while clustering more closely with carboxylesterases such as TfCa. BhEstB displayed broad esterase activity toward pNP-esters, with maximum activity at pH 8 and 20-30 °C. Although it showed modest overall activity on the bulk polymer, BhEstB significantly outperformed the engineered variant LCCICCG and the recently published archaeal feruloyl esterase PET46 in turning over BHET and MHET. BhEstB exhibits remarkably high activity toward BHET and MHET, achieving complete conversion of 50 mM BHET within 1 h at 30 °C (kcat = 15.57 ± 1.25 s⁻1, Km = 6.54 ± 1.01 mM, corresponding to a catalytic efficiency of 2.38 × 103 M⁻1 s⁻1) and subsequent efficient turnover of 39.8 mM MHET (77% (± 0.7%)) into terephthalic acid (TPA) within 24 h. These results identify BhEstB as one of the most efficient BHET-hydrolyzing enzymes characterized to date. Collectively, these findings establish BhEstB as a versatile BHET/MHET active Bacillus carboxylesterase with modest activity toward commercial semi-crystalline PET powder, contributing to the expanding diversity of PET-intermediate-degrading enzymes. KEYPOINTS: • BhEstB exhibits structural divergence from canonical PET esterases. • BhEstB efficiently degrades significant amounts of BHET and MHET at 30 °C. • BhEstB demonstrates moderate activity on PET powder at elevated temperatures.

tag.summary: A Bacillus carboxylesterase characterised for PET intermediate degradation; an enzymology paper.

paper.title: Environmental Aging Enhances Hydrodynamic Driven Microplastics Piezoelectric Catalytic Decomposition of Organic Pollutants.
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are recognized as emerging environmental pollutants. However, their potential role in degrading pollutants under hydrodynamic conditions after environmental aging is frequently overlooked. In this study, three common MPs including polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polystyrene (PS) were investigated for their ability to enhance atrazine (ATZ) degradation after UV aging and under ultrasonic hydrodynamic treatment. Our findings demonstrate that environmental aging significantly boosts the piezoelectric catalytic activity of MPs, consequently accelerating pollutant degradation. UV-aged polypropylene (PP-8) exhibited the highest performance, achieving a piezoelectric catalytic degradation rate constant (k ═ 0.246 min-1), which is 22.36-fold higher than that of pristine PP (k ═ 0.011 min-1). Mechanistic studies revealed that polar carbonyl (C ═ O) functional groups formed during aging play a pivotal role for improving the piezoelectric properties of MPs. This enhancement promotes hydroxyl radicals (·OH) generation from water molecules, which drives pollutant degradation. Furthermore, this effect was found to be general as it was consistently observed in systems using MPs aged by different environmental processes (high temperature, mechanical wear, and Fenton oxidation) and exposed to various hydrodynamic conditions (oscillation and cavitation). This study provides new insights into the self-purification mechanisms of organic pollutants in natural environments.

tag.summary: Environmental ageing shown to enhance piezoelectric catalytic decomposition of pollutants by microplastics; a chemistry paper.

paper.title: Seasonality and maximum wind gusts correlate with microplastic concentrations in a freshwater stream system.
paper.mesh: Microplastics; Environmental Monitoring; Rivers; Seasons; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Wind; Pennsylvania
paper.abstract: We evaluate how meteorological and environmental variables relate to stream microplastic concentrations using regression-based models. Forty-nine water column samples were collected bimonthly over an annual cycle (September 2024-September 2025) from a stream in southeastern Pennsylvania, USA. Microplastic particles were isolated and quantified by light microscopy, and polymer types were characterized using scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Results from three separate multiple linear regression models (stepwise selection, LASSO, and elastic net) demonstrate high variability in microplastic counts, including pronounced seasonal variability (mean = 7.6 particles L⁻1, n = 49, 1σ = 4.9 particles L⁻1). All regression approaches identified colder temperatures and stronger wind gusts as important predictors of elevated microplastic concentrations. Repeated tenfold cross-validation indicated that models incorporating these variables explained approximately 80% of the variability in microplastic concentrations within this relatively small dataset (n = 49), highlighting their importance as the dominant environmental controls on microplastic abundance in Plum Run. When scaled by riparian area, the wind-sensitive component of the stream plastic flux is consistent with physically plausible atmospheric deposition rates. These results provide an indirect inference that environmental factors enhance transport of microplastics into waterways. Qualitative data from EDS and FTIR spectra indicate that polyester fibers comprise the majority of microplastic pollution in Plum Run. From this, we infer that increased laundering and shedding of synthetic clothing during winter may be a primary driver of higher pollution in winter months.

tag.summary: Seasonality and wind gusts correlated with stream microplastic concentrations; an environmental survey.

paper.title: Microalgae-mediated aggregation facilitates the vertical transport of microplastics: the role of Cylindrotheca closterium under simulated conditions.
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) released from aquaculture infrastructure represent a growing source of pollution in coastal environments, yet their fate in the presence of periphytic diatoms remains underexplored. This study investigates how the periphytic diatom Cylindrotheca closterium interacts with polyethylene (PE) MPs of two size classes (10-20 μm and 100-200 μm) under controlled laboratory conditions. Using 36-day time-series experiments, we examined cell attachment, aggregate formation, and sinking dynamics. C. closterium rapidly reached high biomass (>1.50 × 106 cells mL-1) and formed visible aggregates as early as day 11. Aggregation pathways differed by MP size: small particles became embedded within branched internal matrices, whereas large particles developed into dense, spherical flocs with external coatings of diatom cells. Large MPs served as nucleation cores, enabling higher MP incorporation per aggregate (mean 1.68-2.44 MPs) and generating attachment ratios exceeding 8.00 × 103 cells per particle in some treatments. Aggregate areas surpassed 1.7 × 105 μm2 in large-PE groups, and sinking velocities reached up to 3.70 mm s-1. Aggregate formation and downward transport occurred across all treatments, with distinct morphologies and performance depending on particle size and concentration. These results suggest that C. closterium promotes a robust pathway for MP aggregation and sedimentation through surface-mediated attachment rather than extensive extracellular matrix production. The size-dependent structural strategies highlight functional plasticity in capturing and retaining MPs. Overall, this study underscores the significant role of periphytic diatoms in regulating the environmental fate of aquaculture-derived MPs, providing new insight into biologically mediated removal processes in coastal ecosystems.

tag.summary: Microalgal aggregation shown to speed vertical transport of microplastics; an environmental fate study.

paper.title: Effects of dry-wet alternation patterns on PFAS fate in sediments amended with microplastics.
paper.abstract: The accumulation of PFASs in sediments is influenced by both dry-wet alternation (ADW) patterns and microplastic (MP) pollution, yet their combined effects on PFAS fate in water-sediment systems remain unclear. In this study, we investigated PFAS accumulation in sediments under three ADW patterns (1ADW, 2ADW, 3ADW) and continuous submergence (CS), combined with or without polypropylene (PP) MPs (1% w/w). The results showed that, relative to CS, ADW generally inhibited the accumulation of PFOA & substitutes, whereas its effect on PFOS & substitutes was pattern-dependent, with 3ADW even showing elevated accumulation. For individual compounds, HFPO-TA and PFHxS varied most across ADW treatments; Gen-X and PFBS least. MPs presence altered this trend: MPs promoted PFAS accumulation under ADW (with the highest increment of 44.68 μg/kg for PFOS & substitutes under 1ADW), but exhibited inhibition (for PFOA & substitutes) or weak (for PFOS & substitutes) effects under CS, indicating that the direction of MP-mediated regulation is highly dependent on hydrological conditions. Based on sediment physicochemical property differences and multiple linear regression (MLR) model results, compared to CS, ADW primarily inhibited PFAS accumulation by disrupting sediment flocculent structures and altering the role of DOM, whereas MPs presence enhanced PFAS retention by intensifying surface fragmentation, modulating key parameters (e.g., Zeta potential, BIX, and DOC), and serving as an additional sorption phase, thereby altering the original inhibition pattern imposed by ADW.

tag.summary: Dry-wet alternation and microplastics studied for their joint effect on PFAS fate in sediment; a geochemistry study.

paper.title: Precise identification and validation of microplastics using deep learning models in the Yellow River.
paper.abstract: Investigating the spatial distribution and seasonal variations of riverine microplastics (MPs) is vital to aquatic ecological research. Mass suspended sediment within the Yellow River introduces severe background noise, which impedes conventional deep learning models from accurately extracting fine edge features of microplastics. Based on water samples collected from the Zhengzhou reach of the Yellow River, this study systematically evaluates a matrix of 24 hybrid encoder-decoder segmentation architectures covering six backbones (ResNet and ResNeXt series) and four decoders (FPN, DeepLabV3+, UNet, UNet++). The objective is to identify the optimal single model configuration (including network depth, topological layout, and feature fusion strategy) capable of accurately extracting fine edge features of microplastics under severe sediment interference.. Beyond standard segmentation metrics, three dedicated indices including Counting Error (CE), Background Complexity (BC) and 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95) are proposed to quantify the anti-noise robustness of each model. Grad-CAM visualization is adopted to interpret model spatial feature activation and target focus patterns, and micro-Fourier transform infrared (μ-FTIR) spectroscopy is utilized to cross-validate segmentation outputs. The ResNeXt-101 + UNet++ hybrid network delivers optimal performance. Equipped with grouped convolution and nested dense skip connections, this architecture bridges the information gap between shallow spatial details and deep semantic features, achieving a precision of 0.9534, a recall of 0.9991 and a mean absolute counting error (MAE) of 0.242. Microplastic abundances predicted by the model show excellent consistency with μ-FTIR measurements, addressing the common disconnection between image segmentation and spectroscopic identification in existing studies. This work develops an accurate intelligent pipeline for microplastic detection and quantification, facilitating routine surveillance and ecological risk assessment within the Yellow River Basin, while providing a methodological framework that warrants further validation in other sediment-laden aquatic environments.

tag.summary: Deep learning models used to identify microplastics in the Yellow River; a method paper.

paper.title: Construction of Polydopamine@Crosslinked Polystyrene Core/Shell Polymeric Support for the Immobilization of Silver Nano-cluster: Adsorption and Selective Reduction of p-Chloronitrobenzene.
paper.abstract: Polymers are promising catalyst supports because of their tunable composition and facile functionality. In this work, a core/shell polydopamine@crosslinked polystyrene support (XP-PDA) was first constructed, and silver nano-clusters were subsequently immobilized via in situ reduction to yield Ag@XP-PDA. Adsorption kinetic and temperature-dependent isotherm tests were conducted to compare the adsorption capacity of the catalysts toward the reactant p-chloronitrobenzene (P-CNB) and its corresponding hydrogenation product p-chloroaniline (P-CAN). At 298 K, Ag@XP-PDA reached adsorption equilibrium within 180 min, with distinct capacities of 38.5 mg g-1 for P-CNB, whereas only 9.2 mg g-1 for P-CAN. Increasing the temperature from 298 to 318 K enhanced the adsorption capacity for P-CNB (from 50.3 to 54.1 mg g-1) while suppressing that for P-CAN (from 15.3 to 11.6 mg g-1). This distinct temperature-dependent adsorption behavior indicates the chemisorption of P-CNB for substrate enrichment. Improved substrate adsorption and product desorption endow Ag@XP-PDA with over 90% P-CAN chemoselectivity at 318 K. Hence, the XP-PDA support enables both the stabilization of Ag nano-clusters and enrichment of the substrate, affording an efficient catalytic system for the selective reduction of P-CNB to P-CAN.

tag.summary: A polydopamine and polystyrene core-shell support built to immobilise silver nanoclusters; a catalysis paper.

paper.title: Tracing Industrial Microplastics Footprint in Fiji's Marine Environment.
paper.mesh: Microplastics; Fiji; Environmental Monitoring; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Seawater
paper.abstract: This study investigated the presence of microplastics (MP) in drainage channels that carry stormwater and greywater runoffs from areas surrounding the industrial sites on Viti Levu, Fiji's main island. Water samples were collected, digested with hydrogen peroxide, separated by density separation and filtered through an aluminum oxide Anodisc membrane filter (0.2 μm pore size) for particle recovery. The filter membranes were observed under a microscope for the presence, size and morphology of MP. 93.4% of particles ≥ 100 μm were confirmed as MP by ATR-FTIR. Across all sampling locations, an average MP concentration of 2.23 ± 0.78 MP L⁻¹ was observed, with the highest MP abundance (3.08 MP L- 1) at Site 5 and the lowest (1.26 MP L- 1) at Site 2. Fragments accounted for the largest number of MP (48.08%), followed by fibers (47.83%) and films (4.09%). Most of the MP (52.30%) were smaller than 500 μm. Polyethylene (PE, 46.29%) and polystyrene (PS, 33.76%) were the most prevalent polymers, reflecting their extensive use in packaging materials. These findings highlight the substantial role of industrial activities in MP contamination of the marine ecosystems. In Fiji, PS has been completely banned as a single use plastic, while PE is restricted under certain conditions. It is important to extend this ban to include PE and PS packaging materials to accelerate the elimination of these plastics from Fiji's environment.

tag.summary: Industrial microplastics traced in Fijian drainage channels and marine environment; an environmental survey.

paper.title: Silver nanoparticles supported on DABCO-based ionic liquid-functionalized magnetic polystyrene for the efficient reduction of 4-nitrophenol.
paper.abstract: The efficient conversion of nitrobenzene to aminophenols, typically achieved with metal catalysts or metal oxides, provides significant environmental benefits. In this study, a novel nanocatalyst was synthesized by immobilizing silver metal on DABCO-based ionic liquids supported on magnetic polystyrene. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized by XRD, TGA, EDS & EDS mapping, FT-IR, and ICP and subsequently evaluated as solid-phase catalysts for the reduction of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) with excess NaBH4 using UV-vis spectroscopy, which maintained good catalytic activity after six recycling cycles. The synthesized nanocatalyst was cost-effective and demonstrated excellent efficiency (⁓80% conversion) within 6 min, 15 mg of nanocatalyst, 25 mL of NaBH4 (2.5 mM), as well as straightforward separation during the reduction process. Additionally, kinetic analysis shows that the reduction of 4-NP follows a pseudo-first-order model with Kapp= 0.20 min- 1.

tag.summary: Silver nanoparticles on functionalised magnetic polystyrene used to reduce 4-nitrophenol; a catalysis paper.

paper.title: Hospital wastewater as a significant source of microplastics in Northern Iran: Abundance, polymer composition, and environmental risk assessment.
paper.mesh: Microplastics; Iran; Wastewater; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Risk Assessment; Environmental Monitoring; Hospitals; Humans; Polymers
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous contaminants increasingly detected in aquatic environments and wastewater systems, raising concerns regarding ecosystem and human health. Hospital wastewater has been identified as a source of MPs entering municipal systems; however, data on their occurrence, characteristics, and associated risks remain limited. This study aimed to characterize MP contamination in hospital wastewater and assess the associated environmental and health risks. METHODS: Wastewater samples were collected from the influent and effluent of a hospital wastewater treatment plant in northern Iran. MPs were isolated using stainless-steel sieving followed by hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) digestion. Abundance, morphology, and size distribution were determined through microscopic examination, and chemical composition was analyzed using Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy Dispersive X-ray (SEM-EDX) and micro-Raman spectroscopy. The Pollution Load Index (PLI) and Hazard Index (HI) were calculated to evaluate contamination levels and associated risks. RESULTS: The analysis showed mean MP concentrations of 21.13 ± 12.8 particles L-1 in the influent and 1.45 ± 0.89 particles L-1 in the effluent, reflecting a removal efficiency of 93.13%. Morphologically, fibrous particles predominated (92-96%), with black as the most common color and sizes below 250 µm being the most prevalent. Identified polymer compositions included polyamide (PA), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyurethane (PU). Based on the calculated indices, the hospital wastewater reached a PLI of 1.86 and an HI of 1416.45, which corresponds to hazard level IV, primarily attributed to the high hazard score of PVC (5001) due to its carcinogenic monomer and additive leaching. CONCLUSIONS: Hospital wastewater is a significant source of MPs, particularly hazardous polymers such as PVC and PU. These findings highlight the need for targeted mitigation strategies, including advanced treatment processes and reduced use of toxic polymers in healthcare settings, to minimize MP discharge and protect environmental and public health.

tag.summary: Hospital wastewater characterised as a source of microplastics in northern Iran; an environmental survey.

paper.title: Toxic cascade from oxidative stress to metabolic imbalance in Manila clams exposed to polyethylene terephthalate microplastics.
paper.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is one of the most abundant plastic pollutants in marine environments. However, compared with other polymers, research on PET microplastics (MPs)-particularly their impact on benthic organisms in sediment environments-remains relatively scarce. In this study, we exposed Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum) to PET MPs in fragments and fibers of five sizes at concentrations of 0.8, 8, and 80 mg/kg dry weight (dw) of sediment for 21 days using a water-sediment exposure system. Mortality in Manila clams exposed to PET MPs remained unchanged, and each MP group accumulated in the digestive glands and gills. Chronic exposure to PET MPs increased reactive oxygen species production and SOD, IL-1β, and CASP8 levels in the gill and digestive gland tissues of clams. Integrated biomarker response analysis showed stronger correlations for fragments than for fibers, and for larger than smaller sizes, in both gill and digestive gland tissues. Furthermore, omics analysis confirmed a strong response in inflammation-related factors to fragment MPs, suggesting that PET MPs induce oxidative stress, inflammation, and cellular responses that lead to digestive and secretory dysfunction, which may cause morphological and metabolic changes in clams and ultimately adversely affect their health and survival. This study contributes to our understanding of the toxic mechanisms of PET MPs, focusing on their size and shape, and ultimately raises awareness of their harmful effects in the environment.

tag.summary: PET microplastics drove a cascade from oxidative stress to metabolic imbalance in Manila clams, a polymer less studied than polystyrene.

paper.title: Using Weibull-derived λ-α parameters to diagnose physical processes controlling microplastic size dynamics in estuarine-coastal waters: A five-year study in Tianjin, Bohai Bay.
paper.abstract: To elucidate the spatiotemporal evolution of microplastic particle size distributions and their controlling mechanisms in estuarine-coastal regions, this study conducted continuous monitoring in Tianjin coastal waters from 2021 to 2025. By coupling microplastic abundance and particle size analysis with Weibull distribution fitting to extract the rate parameter λ and shape parameter α, the impacts of sedimentation, fragmentation, and riverine input were investigated. The results showed a significant decline in both λ and α at all sites during 2021-2022, coinciding with extreme rainfall (978.4 mm) in Tianjin in 2021, indicating a pronounced riverine input pulse. After 2022, sites exhibited regional differentiation: northern nearshore sites showed sustained concurrent declines in λ and α (continuous input dominance); central sites exhibited stable low-level fluctuations (input-sedimentation balance); and certain sites displayed transient concurrent increases (episodic sedimentation dominance). Spatially, the multi-year mean λ increased with water depth, reflecting preferential settling of large particles. Notably, the concurrent decline in λ and α was accompanied by decreasing abundance at most sites, indicating that input particles became larger while total input flux decreased. This pattern may reflect the initial effectiveness of regional plastic control measures. This study demonstrates that the λ-α dual-parameter combination can effectively distinguish physical processes controlling microplastic size distributions, providing a new diagnostic tool for source identification and process attribution of microplastics in coastal waters.

tag.summary: Weibull parameters used to diagnose processes controlling microplastic size distributions in Bohai Bay; an environmental study.

paper.title: Sustainable synthesis of a Zr-based UiO-66 MOF from PET waste for UV-assisted degradation of organic contaminants.
paper.abstract: The coexistence of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste and persistent organic pollutants in aquatic environments requires comprehensive circular-economy strategies to valorize PET waste into functional materials for water treatment. In this study, post-consumer PET was converted to terephthalic acid (TPA) via a neutral hydrothermal depolymerization process and was used as an organic linker for the synthesis of a Zr-based UiO-66. The recovered linker and synthesized UiO-66 were characterized by FTIR, PXRD, TEM/SAED, nitrogen adsorption-desorption, UV-vis spectroscopy, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and Mott-Schottky analysis. PXRD confirmed UiO-66 crystallinity, while TEM revealed nano-sized polyhedral particles with an average size of approximately 120 nm. The material exhibited a BET surface area of 822.2 m2 g-1, total pore volume of 0.379 cm3 g-1, and average pore diameter of 2.93 nm. Optical and electrochemical analyses showed a band gap of about 3.51 eV, n-type semiconducting behavior, and a flat-band potential of -0.68 V vs. Ag/AgCl. The photocatalytic activity of PET-derived UiO-66 was evaluated using methylene blue (MB) under UV light irradiation. Under optimized conditions, the catalyst achieved about 97.3% degradation with an apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.024 min-1, which was about 12 times higher than that of direct photolysis. Radical scavengers' experiments showed that hydroxyl radicals (˙OH) acted as major reactive species, followed by superoxide radicals (˙O2 -) and photogenerated holes (h+). The catalyst showed good recyclability with about 86% activity retained after five cycles. These results offer an environmentally sustainable approach to recycle PET waste into a useful photocatalyst for water treatment.

tag.summary: A zirconium metal-organic framework synthesised from PET waste for photodegradation of pollutants; a chemistry paper.

paper.title: Microplastics and toxic elements in small freshwater lakes and ponds in coastal Norway.
paper.abstract: This study examined the occurrence of microplastics (MPs) and toxic elements in small freshwater lakes and ponds on islands in the Froan archipelago, Central Norway, evaluating marine plastic as a local contributor to environmental contamination. MP polymers and concentrations, along with toxic elements (As, Cd, Cu, Cr, Hg, Ni, Pb, Zn), were analyzed across freshwater, sediment, marine macroplastics, and adjacent soils across 12 waterbodies on seven islands, using Py-GC/MS (MPs) and ICP-MS (toxic elements). Polyethylene, polypropylene, and polystyrene were the predominant MP polymers, indicating secondary fragmentation. In freshwater, Cd and Zn reached Class V (very bad) status under Environmental Quality Standards, with concentrations up to 4.7 µg L⁻¹ and 260 µg L⁻¹, respectively. Marine macroplastics harbored extreme contaminant burdens from both legacy production additives and environmental adsorption, including Cd up to 415 µg g⁻¹ dw, Pb up to 800 µg g⁻¹ dw, Cr up to 186 µg g⁻¹ dw, and Zn up to 407 µg g⁻¹ dw. There were significant positive correlations for Zn concentrations in plastics, water, and sediments, alongside elevated element levels in shoreline soils (<0.3 m). This strongly indicates that plastic litter acts as a dynamic source and vector transferring toxic elements across compartments, accelerated by acidic conditions (pH < 7) triggering metal desorption. Notably, pollution levels differed greatly, even between ponds on the same island (e.g., a 270-fold difference in water Cd), highlighting the role of local topography on litter retention. These findings underline the role of marine plastic in amplifying contaminant burdens in coastal ecosystems.

tag.summary: Microplastics and toxic elements surveyed in small Norwegian lakes and ponds; an environmental survey.

paper.title: Fabrication of gold nanostars for SERS detection of microplastics in water.
paper.journal: Spectrochim Acta A Mol Biomol Spectrosc
paper.abstract: Environmental contamination by microplastic particles has become a globally recognized issue, attracting increasing scientific and regulatory attention. In this study, a rapid and efficient method for detecting microplastics was developed using surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) combined with highly active substrates, enabling real-time monitoring and fast analysis. Gold nanostars (Au NSs) with sharp multi-branched structures were controllably synthesized using chloroauric acid (HAuCl₄), silver nitrate (AgNO₃), and ascorbic acid (AA). Their formation was achieved by regulating the anisotropic growth of gold via the underpotential deposition (UPD) of silver ions. The resulting Au NS colloid was then uniformly deposited onto a PVDF membrane through vacuum filtration, producing an Au NSs-PVDF substrate capable of both enriching and enhancing the SERS signal of microplastic particles. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations using a trimer model of Au NSs confirmed that the observed Raman signal enhancement originates from abundant electromagnetic "hot spots" generated by the sharp branches and the high specific surface area of the nanostars. SERS measurements demonstrated that rapid analysis of both single-component and binary mixtures of polystyrene (PS), polyethylene (PE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyamide (PA) microplastics in aqueous environments can be completed within 10 min. Furthermore, the minimum detectable concentrations for single-component PET, PS, PE, and PA in lake water were 0.2 g·L-1, 0.4 g·L-1, 0.4 g·L-1, and 0.4 g·L-1 respectively, representing a significant improvement in detection efficiency.

tag.summary: Gold nanostars fabricated for surface-enhanced Raman detection of microplastics; a method paper.

paper.title: Cellular toxicity and apoptosis-related responses to individual and combined exposure to microplastics and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) in Hediste diversicolor coelomocytes.
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are emerging contaminants of increasing concern in marine ecosystems due to their widespread occurrence and ability to adsorb and transport hazardous chemicals such as perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS). PFOS is a persistent per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) with high environmental stability, bioaccumulative potential, and well-documented toxicity to aquatic organisms. However, the combined effects of MPs and PFOS on marine invertebrates remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of environmentally relevant concentrations of MPs (50 mg kg-1 sediment) and PFOS (0.1, 0.5, and 1 μg kg-1 sediment) on the coelomic fluid of the benthic polychaete Hediste diversicolor after 7 days of sediment exposure. The MPs consisted of particles <30 μm composed of PVC, PET, PS, HDPE, LDPE, and PE with heterogeneous morphologies. PFOS accumulated in the coelomic fluid in a dose-dependent manner, with higher concentrations observed under co-exposure, suggesting that the presence of MPs may influence PFOS bioavailability and uptake. This increased accumulation was accompanied by pronounced cytotoxic and genotoxic effects, including lysosomal membrane destabilization, increased micronucleus frequency, and DNA fragmentation. Co-exposure also upregulated the pro-apoptotic genes p53, Bax, and Casp-3, while downregulating the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl-2, indicating activation of apoptotic pathways. Overall, the effects of combined exposure varied according to the endpoint and PFOS concentration, with co-exposure producing greater responses for some endpoints but not consistently across all treatments. These findings highlight the increased hazard posed by the co-occurrence of MPs and PFOS and emphasize the need to consider contaminant mixtures in marine environmental risk assessment.

tag.summary: Microplastics alone and with perfluorooctane sulfonic acid caused cytotoxicity and apoptotic responses in ragworm coelomocytes.

paper.title: Synthesis of ultra-large Ti3C2T x MXene nanoflakes: enabling high-performance flexible transparent conductive coatings.
paper.abstract: Flexible transparent conductive electrodes (FTCEs) are critical components in next-generation wearable electronics and display technologies. However, achieving low sheet resistance without compromising optical transparency remains a significant challenge due to percolation limitations in thin conductive films. MXenes, a rapidly expanding class of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal carbides and nitrides, offer remarkable potential as transparent conducting electrodes (TCEs) owing to their exceptional electrical conductivity, mechanical flexibility, and intrinsically hydrophilic nature. In this work, a modified orbital shaker-assisted Minimally Intensive Layer Delamination (Orbital-MILD) etching method is introduced, yielding ultra-large Ti3C2T x MXene nanoflakes with an average lateral size of ∼30 µm (optical-microscopy statistics over 168 individual flakes) and individual flakes reaching up to 48 µm - among the largest reported to date for solution-processed MXenes. The gentle orbital mixing action prevents flake fragmentation during both the etching and delamination stages, preserving the large lateral dimensions of the parent MAX phase particles. These large-flake inks were formulated into aqueous colloids and deposited onto flexible polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrates using slot-die coating - a scalable, alignment-promoting deposition technique. The resultant FTCEs demonstrated an electrical conductivity of 22 777 S cm-1 with a record figure of merit (FoMe) of 39, effectively eliminating the percolation bottleneck common in sparse nanomaterial networks. This work not only addresses a key limitation in MXene-based FTCE fabrication but also opens avenues for extending the method to other MXene systems, enabling scalable production of high-performance flexible electrodes.

tag.summary: Ultra-large MXene nanoflakes synthesised for transparent conductive coatings; a materials paper.

paper.title: Large Seasonal Variation in Microplastic Concentration from the Truckee River, United States.
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous in riverine environments worldwide, but arid river systems, characterized by large seasonal variations in discharge, remain understudied. Using a peristaltic pump, we collected samples for MP surface concentration analysis along the Truckee River in the western United States. Samples were collected using a 100 μm filter during fall 2022 and spring 2023 across 6 and 8 sites, respectively. The samples were analyzed with microscope-enabled Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy, and the resulting MP concentrations were compared to land use and river discharge. MP concentrations were higher in spring (mean 3.7 MP/L) than in fall (mean 0.4 MP/L), coinciding with an increase in river discharge. Statistical analyses revealed significant seasonal differences in polymer composition because of increased concentrations of poly-(ethylene terephthalate), polyethylene, and rubber in spring. These patterns likely reflect increased spring discharge mobilizing MPs from the surrounding landscape and riverbed sediments. These findings underscore the complexity of MP sources and transport and highlight the importance of seasonal sampling across discharge and land-use types. Additionally, polypropylene, poly-(ethylene terephthalate), and polyethylene were the dominant polymer types overall, demonstrating that reducing single-use plastic in the Truckee River Basin is important for protecting the river's water quality.

tag.summary: Large seasonal variation measured in microplastic concentration in an arid United States river; an environmental survey.

paper.title: Airborne microplastics and associated heavy metal contamination in indoor and outdoor environments: Pollution levels and health risks in Metro Manila, Philippines.
paper.mesh: Metals, Heavy; Philippines; Environmental Monitoring; Air Pollutants; Microplastics; Humans; Air Pollution, Indoor; Risk Assessment; Environmental Exposure
paper.abstract: Airborne microplastics (MPs) have emerged as environmental pollutants that can co-occur with hazardous contaminants; however, evidence of heavy-metal associations with atmospheric MPs remains limited. This study investigated the abundance, characteristics, metal loadings, and health risks of airborne MPs in Metro Manila, Philippines. Air samples were collected from classroom, laboratory, dining room, office, living room, and store environments, followed by polymer identification via μFTIR and metal quantification using ICP-MS. MP concentrations ranged from 0.074 to 0.595 MP/m3 indoors (mean: 0.297 ± 0.20 MP/m3) and from 0.057 to 0.262 MP/m3 outdoors (mean: 0.173 ± 0.07 MP/m3), with no statistically significant difference. Fibers dominated the MP assemblage (52.38%), followed by fragments and films. PP, PET, and PE were the most prevalent polymers. Heavy metal concentrations ranged from 0.35 to 27521.66 mg/kg indoors and from 0.11 to 30556 mg/kg outdoors, with notable contributions from Zn, Cu, Ba, Pb, and Ag. These showed site-specific variations associated with room function and anthropogenic activity, with elevated Cu and Zn in high-activity indoor spaces. Pollution indices (PLI, MPI) indicated moderate pollution levels, while the ecological risk index indicated moderate ecological risk. Spearman analysis showed strong positive correlations between MPI-HM and As, Fe, and Zn (r = 0.70, p < 0.05), while PCA and HCA differentiated sampling sites by metal- and MP-related profiles. Inhalation risk assessment indicated low-to-moderate non-carcinogenic risk; however, the co-occurrence of toxic metals with respirable MPs highlights the occurrence of hazardous substances within the recovered airborne MP fraction. This study provides one of the first assessments of heavy metals associated with airborne MPs in indoor-outdoor urban environments.

tag.summary: Airborne microplastics and associated heavy metals measured indoors and outdoors in Metro Manila; an exposure survey.

paper.title: Microplastic Contamination in Four Carnivorous Cultrinae Fish in Dianshan Lake, China.
paper.mesh: Animals; China; Lakes; Microplastics; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Environmental Monitoring; Food Chain; Fishes
paper.abstract: Microplastic (MPs) contamination in freshwater ecosystems threatens aquatic biodiversity. We investigated MPs ingestion in four sympatric Cultrinae fish species from Dianshan Lake, China, using gastrointestinal tract and stable isotope analyses. MPs were widespread, but abundance was low (1.25 ± 2.36 items/ind.). Fibers dominated and consisted mainly of polyethylene terephthalate and polyester, likely derived from fishing gear and domestic laundry. Cultrichthys erythropterus showed the broadest trophic niche and highest MPs diversity, suggesting that opportunistic feeding increases exposure to diverse polymers. MPs abundance was not related to trophic position (Cultrichthys erythropterus: P = 0.24; Culter dabryi: P = 0.07; Culter mongolicus: P = 0.09; Culter alburnus: P = 0.77), providing no evidence of biomagnification among the examined Cultrinae species. However, MPs abundance was negatively correlated with condition index in three species, but not in Culter alburnus. These findings suggest that trophic niche width may be more closely associated with MPs exposure than trophic position within the examined fish assemblage.

tag.summary: Microplastic ingestion compared across four carnivorous fish species in a Chinese lake; an occurrence survey.

paper.title: Biomonitoring microplastic pollution and polymer hazards using the Asian green mussel (Perna viridis): a baseline assessment from Santubong River, Sarawak, Malaysia.
paper.mesh: Animals; Microplastics; Rivers; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Environmental Monitoring; Malaysia; Perna; Polymers
paper.abstract: Microplastic contamination in aquatic organisms is a growing concern due to its ubiquity and potential toxicity. Currently, data on microplastic contamination and polymer hazards in green mussels (Perna viridis) from the Santubong River, Sarawak, is unavailable. In this study, green mussels from the Santubong estuary were analyzed, revealing a 100% occurrence rate and a mean abundance of 5.51 items/individual. Fibers (54.7%) and fragments (30.9%) were dominant, with transparent (40.9%), white (26.1%), and blue (23.8%) being the most prevalent colors. Most particles (83.6%) were < 1000 µm in size. Statistical analysis showed a moderate negative correlation (r = -0.40, p < 0.05) between microplastic abundance and soft tissue weight, suggesting potential impacts on the physiological condition of the mussels. Attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy identified polyamide (60%), polypropylene (23.3%), and polystyrene (10%) as the primary polymers. The prevalence of polyamide is linked to local aquaculture and fishing gear, such as nylon ropes. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) imaging confirmed extensive surface weathering, including cracks, pits, and fractures. The polymer hazard index (PHI) was calculated to be 3143.3, indicating a Level IV (high hazard) status. This study establishes a critical baseline for microplastic pollution management in P. viridis and environmental health assessments in Malaysian Borneo.

tag.summary: Green mussels used to biomonitor microplastic pollution in a Malaysian river; a baseline survey.

paper.title: Enzymatic PET depolymerization: a review of engineering biocatalysts and systems for efficient plastic deconstruction.
paper.abstract: The ever-increasing accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste poses a severe threat to global ecosystems and human health. Biological upcycling (integrating enzymatic depolymerization with microbial conversion of the resulting monomers) has emerged as a promising approach to overcome the limitations of traditional mechanical and chemical recycling. This review provides a systematic and critical synthesis of recent advances in PET bio-upcycling, covering the period from 2016 to 2026. We first discuss the discovery, classification, structural features, and catalytic mechanisms of PET-hydrolyzing enzymes, highlighting the rate-limiting constraints imposed by glass transition temperature, substrate crystallinity, interfacial interactions, and product inhibition. We then evaluate protein engineering strategies that have dramatically enhanced thermostability, substrate binding, and multi-enzyme synergy, yielding benchmark variants capable of near-complete depolymerization of post-consumer PET within hours to days. Concurrent innovations in whole-cell biocatalysis, enzyme immobilization, surface display, and microbial consortia are examined, with emphasis on how metabolic division of labor and substrate channeling can alleviate product inhibition and process mixed plastic waste. We also summarize metabolic engineering efforts that have enabled conversion of PET-derived terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG) into more than 25 value-added products, including biopolymers, platform chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and specialty compounds. Finally, we discuss remaining technological barriers, economic feasibility, and future frontiers (including computational enzyme design, synthetic consortia, tandem chemo-biological processes, and industrial-scale demonstration) and propose a phased roadmap for industrial translation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive resource for advancing PET bio-upcycling from laboratory innovation toward practical implementation in a circular plastics economy.

tag.summary: Review of engineered biocatalysts and systems for enzymatic PET depolymerisation; a biotechnology review.

paper.title: Electrospun Co3O4/CeO2 hollow nanotubes for photocatalytic degradation of PET plastics with peroxymonosulfate activation: Performance and DFT insight.
paper.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics cause significant environmental harm. Traditional treatment methods, such as landfilling and incineration, can cause secondary pollution. Here, an efficient synergistic photocatalytic system is presented, based on Co3O4/CeO2 hollow nanotubes prepared by electrospinning, to activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and promote the degradation of PET plastics. The results show that the as-prepared Co3O4/CeO2 composite catalyst exhibits the best performance under illumination; the weight loss rate of PET can reach ∼82.7 ± 4.5% in the presence of a 3 mM PMS solution (pH 7). The effects of parameters (e.g., PMS dose and coexisting anions) on PET degradation were systematically investigated. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and free radical quenching experiments confirm that the •OH, 1O2, and SO4•- active species contribute the most to the degradation of PET plastics. Density Functional Theory analysis shows that Co-d-pDOS and Ce-f-pDOS modulations in Co3O4/CeO2 synergistically enhance the PET photocatalytic decomposition efficiency. Finally, we discuss the mechanism by which the catalyst/light/PMS system degrades PET in water.

tag.summary: Hollow oxide nanotubes used to photocatalytically degrade PET plastics; a catalysis paper.

paper.title: Depolymerization of PET and Polyamide 66 Wastes Using an Iron(III) Recoverable Lewis-Brønsted Aqueous System.
paper.abstract: The accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyamide 66 (PA66) in municipal and industrial waste streams represents a major challenge to global sustainability efforts. In this work, we report the development and optimization of a low-cost, iron-recoverable, and reconstitutable Lewis-Brønsted aqueous solution (LBAS) system for the selective depolymerization of post-consumer PET and PA66 wastes. The method employs a recyclable reaction medium and operates under mild conditions (150 °C, 2 h), achieving high monomer yields with excellent selectivity. The resulting terephthalic acid, adipic acid, and hexamethylenediammonium chloride were efficiently recovered and purified using straightforward separation techniques, whereas ethylene glycol was recovered as a stream suitable for purification by conventional industrial methods. A proof-of-concept experiment confirmed that PET and PA66 can also be depolymerized in the same medium, even though cross reactions between adipic acid and ethylene glycol prevent the quantitative monomer recovery. Therefore, mixed PET/PA66 feeds require prior separation to recover the individual monomers effectively. Overall, results demonstrate a scalable and environmentally benign approach for the chemical recycling of PET and PA66, contributing to a more sustainable plastic lifecycle and circular materials economy.

tag.summary: An iron-based aqueous system used to depolymerise PET and nylon waste; a recycling chemistry paper.

paper.title: Detection, characterization, and quantification of microplastics in human biological matrices: a systematic review.
paper.mesh: Female; Humans; Environmental Monitoring; Microplastics; Male
paper.abstract: The presence of microplastics (MPs) in the environment represents an emerging risk to human health, with growing evidence of detection in human biological matrices. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the detection, quantification, and characterization of MPs in human biological matrices. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus databases. Original research articles published in English up to 2025 that involved human participants were included, specifically selecting observational studies. The 40 included studies confirmed MPs in multiple human biological matrices, including blood, urine, feces, placenta, breast milk, semen, lung, and heart tissue. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) was used to assess the quality and risk of bias of the individual studies. Substantial methodological heterogeneity was observed in analytical techniques, including Fourier-transform infrared microspectroscopy (μFTIR), micro-Raman spectroscopy (μ-Raman), laser direct infrared spectroscopy (LDIR), and pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS), as well as in the reporting units and limits of detection. Most studies reported fragments and fibers, with a predominance of polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), and polyethylene terephthalate (PET). NOS assessment showed that 52.5% of studies were of moderate quality, indicating that while the frequent detection of these particles suggests widespread human contact, significant methodological shortcomings and potential analytical overestimations limit the accurate quantification of systemic exposure and the strength of causal inferences. The widespread detection of MPs raises public health concerns regarding chronic exposure and potential health implications. However, current evidence remains insufficient to establish causal relationships, underscoring the urgent need for rigorous epidemiological studies.

tag.summary: Systematic review of the detection, characterisation and quantification of microplastics reported across human biological matrices.

paper.title: Chemical Degradation of Waste Polyethylene Terephthalate and Its Application in Developing Asphalt Additives.
paper.abstract: To address the low resource-recovery efficiency of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and the shortage of high-performance eco-friendly asphalt modifiers, PET-derived functional additives were fabricated in this work via zinc-acetate-catalyzed alcoholysis of waste PET followed by repolymerization of the obtained degradation fragments. Owing to the diverse origins of waste PET feedstock, noticeable fluctuations in molecular-weight parameters are commonly encountered. Nevertheless, waste PET can be effectively depolymerized into relatively low-molecular-weight derivatives under the proposed catalytic alcoholysis conditions. This study systematically investigated the effects of different PET degradation pathways on the molecular architecture, molecular-weight distribution, and thermal stability of as-prepared PET-derived asphalt additives. It further uncovers the intrinsic structure-performance relationships between molecular characteristics and critical asphalt properties, including rheological behavior, interfacial adhesion, high-temperature rutting resistance, and low-temperature elastic recovery. Homogeneous alcoholysis conducted at 220 °C enables efficient depolymerization of waste PET to yield derivatives with tailorable molecular weights. The resultant amphiphilic alcoholysis products can reduce asphalt viscosity and ameliorate water stability, rendering them promising warm-mix anti-stripping additives. By contrast, repolymerized PET derivatives are capable of constructing cross-linked networks within asphalt matrix, which substantially boost the high-temperature modulus and fatigue resistance of modified asphalt. Distinct from conventional physical blending approaches that are plagued by inferior interfacial compatibility and marginal performance improvement, this chemical modification strategy affords PET-based additives with tunable functions for different engineering scenarios. These findings provide technical support for high-value recycling of waste PET and the development of sustainable low-carbon asphalt materials.

tag.summary: Chemically degraded waste PET developed into asphalt additives; a materials paper.

paper.title: Molecular-Level Structure Regulation via Sequential Pre-Crosslinking and Friedel-Crafts Hypercrosslinking: Fabrication of Bimetallic Doped Porous Carbon Electrocatalysts.
paper.abstract: Owing to high surface inertness and insufficient active sites, traditional carbons cannot anchor and disperse metal species evenly, restricting catalytic activity. Via polymer precursor design, the components, functional groups and pore architecture can be tailored molecularly and preserved upon carbonization, thus regulating carbon microstructure, surface properties and active centers efficiently. This work focuses on the synthesis and structural tuning of polystyrene-based precursors using a three-step procedure of pre-crosslinking, Friedel-Crafts hypercrosslinking, and activation. The materials possess abundant mesopores ranging from 7 to 30 nm, which serve as an ideal platform for the efficient anchoring of metal ions and mass transfer during the subsequent carbonization and functionalization processes. Based on the strong adsorption and exchange ability of sulfonic acid groups, transition metal ions such as Co, Ni and Fe were uniformly doped on the surface of nanoparticles and carbonized at 300-600 °C in an air atmosphere to realize the conversion of the polymer skeleton to a carbon matrix and the in situ formation of metal species into oxide nanoparticles. At the application performance level, the prepared Co/Ni bimetallic-carbon-doped material exhibits excellent electrocatalytic activity in the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction. The overpotential is only 0.3478 V at a current density of 10 mA cm-2. After 50 cycles of cyclic voltammetry, the voltage fluctuation is only 0.026 V.

tag.summary: Hypercrosslinked porous carbon electrocatalysts fabricated with bimetallic doping; a materials paper.

paper.title: Effects of Storage Temperature and Packaging Type on the Postharvest Quality of Finger Lime (Citrus australasica).
paper.abstract: Finger lime (Citrus australasica F.Muell.) is a native Australian citrus species with increasing commercial value because of its unique sensory, visual and nutritional properties. However, like other citrus species, it is highly perishable and susceptible to postharvest quality deterioration. Despite its growing importance, limited research has examined how commercial packaging and storage temperature affect its quality. Therefore, this study investigated the combined effects of three commonly used types of packaging (net bags, recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) punnets and moulded cardboard clamshells) and three storage temperatures (room temperature (RT; ~25 °C), 8 °C and 4 °C) on finger lime quality over eight weeks. The quality parameters examined included weight loss, firmness, colour, visual appearance and overall marketability, as well as nutritional properties, including total phenolic content, total flavonoid content and antioxidant capacity. Packaging and temperature both significantly affected fruit marketability. Fruit stored at RT quickly lost quality in all packaging types. Fruit stored at 4 °C retained firmness, colour, total phenolic content, flavonoid content and antioxidant capacity better than fruit stored at 25 °C or 8 °C; however, chilling injury and fungal growth developed at 4 °C, with approximately 20% of the fruit in each packaging treatment deemed unsaleable by Week 8. At 8 °C, no chilling injury, visible fungal growth or shrivelling was observed. Although approximately 60% of fruit in cardboard clamshells and net bags were classified as unsaleable because of loss of freshness, approximately 80% of fruit in punnets remained saleable until the end of the trial. Overall, storage at 8 °C in rPET punnets provided the best balance between quality retention and marketability among the combinations of packaging type and storage temperature examined in this study.

tag.summary: Storage temperature and packaging type tested on postharvest quality of finger lime; a food science paper.

paper.title: Recycled PET/Sepiolite Composite Adsorbent for Methylene Blue Removal: Formulation, RSM Optimisation, Reusability, and Adsorption Mechanism.
paper.mesh: Methylene Blue; Adsorption; Magnesium Silicates; Polyethylene Terephthalates; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Hydrogen-Ion Concentration; Temperature; Water Purification; Kinetics; Recycling
paper.abstract: This study explores the valorisation of post-industrial recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) via incorporation of sepiolite clay to develop a composite adsorbent for methylene blue (MB) dye removal. The composite formulation was evaluated by varying the rPET concentration, TFA:DCM solvent ratio, sepiolite content, and blending time. The selected formulation had an average particle size of 267.10 nm, a specific surface area of 0.67 m2/g, and a pore volume of 0.003925 cm3/g. Adsorption conditions were then optimised using a five-factor, three-level Box-Behnken design, considering contact time, MB concentration, adsorbent dosage, pH, and temperature. The resulting quadratic model was statistically significant (F = 114.18, p < 0.0001), with R2 = 0.9892, adjusted R2 = 0.9805, and predicted R2 = 0.9568; however, the lack-of-fit was also significant (F = 90.90, p < 0.0001), indicating that model predictions should be interpreted within the investigated factor ranges. At the selected conditions of 62.5 min, 25.5 mg/L MB, 2.55 g/50 mL adsorbent, pH 7, and 55 °C, the model predicted an MB removal efficiency of 99.03%. The adsorbent retained at least 93% reusability efficiency after six adsorption-washing-reuse cycles. The kinetic data were described more closely by the pseudo-second-order model, whereas the Freundlich model provided a better representation of the equilibrium data (R2 = 0.9976). Thermodynamic results indicated that adsorption was favourable and exothermic within the investigated temperature range. Overall, the results show that post-industrial PET can be converted into a value-added sepiolite-containing adsorbent for MB removal.

tag.summary: Recycled PET and sepiolite composite developed as a dye adsorbent; a materials paper.

paper.title: In-Situ Catalytic Pyrolysis of Polystyrene with Sewage Sludge-Derived Catalysts: Sewage Sludge Ash, Sewage Sludge Char, and Fe-Impregnated Acid-Leached Sewage Sludge Char.
paper.abstract: Sewage sludge (SS)-derived materials were investigated as low-cost heterogeneous catalytic materials for polystyrene (PS) pyrolysis, focusing on the effects of thermal treatment, HCl leaching, and Fe impregnation. Sewage sludge ash (SSA), sewage sludge char (SSC), and HCl-leached Fe-impregnated sewage sludge char (Fe-LSSC) were evaluated as in-situ catalytic materials. Catalyst-to-PS ratios of 1:1-1:10 were investigated in a horizontal semi-batch tubular reactor operated in an in-situ catalyst-polymer contact mode at 800 °C. Thermal pyrolysis produced 63.9 wt.% PyOil and 12.6 wt.% PyGas. SSA increased the PyOil yield to 78.0 wt.% at 1:10 and promoted lighter aromatics; at 1:1, light aromatics increased to 66.8 wt.%, BTEX from 5.8 to 24.58 wt.%, and PAHs decreased to 11.8 wt.%. SSC showed a weaker, non-monotonic effect, with PyOil decreasing to 54.4 wt.% and PyChar increasing to 4.7 wt.% at 1:2. Fe-LSSC produced the strongest changes, increasing PyGas to 28.0 wt.% at 1:1 and H2 to 75.3 vol.% at 1:2. The gasoline-range fraction reached 82.1 wt.% at 1:2, while PAHs decreased to 8.79 wt.% at 1:1. Catalyst reuse altered gas composition, whereas thermal regeneration partially restored catalytic behavior. Overall, SS-derived materials exhibited distinct, loading-dependent catalytic functions, while HCl leaching and Fe impregnation enhanced the conversion of PS pyrolysis vapors toward lighter aromatic and gaseous products.

tag.summary: Sewage sludge-derived catalysts tested for polystyrene pyrolysis; a process chemistry paper.

paper.title: Selective Upcycling of Waste PET into Di(2-ethylhexyl) Terephthalate via a Hybrid Organometallic Catalytic Strategy for PVC Plasticizer Applications.
paper.abstract: The selective conversion of post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into value-added plasticizers offers a promising pathway for advancing polymer circularity within the scope of the circular economy approach. Herein, waste PET bottles were directly upcycled into di(2-ethylhexyl) terephthalate (DOTP) via degradative alcoholysis/transesterification with 2-ethylhexanol using four organometallic catalyst systems: butylstannic acid (F), monobutyltin tris(2-ethylhexanoate) (TK), titanium tetraisopropoxide (T), and a hybrid organotin-titanium system (TKT). PET conversion ranged from 84 to 94%, with the T catalyst affording the highest conversion (94%). Notably, the hybrid TKT catalyst provided the most favorable overall performance, achieving an 81% isolated yield and 85.4% selectivity. GC-FID analysis revealed that DOTP-TKT achieved a 92.0% chromatographic area, while GPC confirmed that this product had the lowest proportion of residual oligomers (15.13%) among all PET-derived samples. FTIR and 1H-NMR spectroscopy further confirmed efficient PET-to-DOTP transformation, with DOTP-TKT displaying the closest structural correspondence to commercial DOTP. Amongst the PET-derived products, DOTP-TKT exhibited the most favorable thermal behavior, with a principal maximum degradation temperature (Tmax) of approximately 283.5 °C. When incorporated into PVC, PET-derived DOTP-TKT showed enhanced tensile strength, elastic modulus, and elongation at break compared with commercial DOTP. These findings demonstrate that the combined Ti-Sn catalyst system simultaneously promotes selective PET depolymerization and product formation while limiting oligomeric residues, providing an effective route for converting post-consumer PET into functional, high-value PVC plasticizers within a circular polymer economy.

tag.summary: Waste PET upcycled into a terephthalate plasticiser for PVC; a recycling chemistry paper.

paper.title: Juncus Acutus fiber-recycled expanded polystyrene composites for lower-impact insulation: experimental characterization and numerical thermal analysis.
paper.abstract: In response to the growing demand for lower-impact building insulation materials, this study investigates composites combining Juncus Acutus (JA) fibers with recycled expanded polystyrene (EPS) as a strategy for valorizing biomass and polymeric waste. Three JA/EPS formulations (70/30, 60/40, and 50/50) were experimentally characterized in terms of density, thermal properties, and compressive strength, followed by life-cycle assessment and transient numerical analysis. Increasing the JA content from 50 to 70% reduced the bulk density from 371.6 to 289.9 kg·m⁻3 and thermal conductivity from 0.117 to 0.096 W·m⁻1·K⁻1, while thermal diffusivity decreased by approximately 15% and specific heat capacity increased by about 10%. Despite the reduction in compressive strength with increasing fiber content, the JA70 formulation reached 0.16 MPa, indicating adequate mechanical integrity for handling and use in non-structural insulation applications. Among the investigated formulations, JA70 provided the most favorable balance between thermal and mechanical properties.
