paper.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To assess the diagnostic accuracy of novel imaging modalities in working up invasive bladder cancer prior to surgical management and their potential role in guiding treatment decisions. RECENT FINDINGS: Multiple new imaging modalities, including VI-RADS and Biparametric MRI have been developed to better guide management of invasive bladder cancer. There lacks a comprehensive review of these modalities and their diagnostic performance. We performed a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through 2025. Studies reporting sensitivity and specificity of novel imaging for muscle invasion detection or nodal staging were included. Quality assessment used the QUADAS 2 tool. Thirty three studies encompassing 4,689 patients were included. Twenty three studies evaluated the Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System for muscle invasion detection, achieving median sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 82% at a threshold of three or greater and 84% and 92%, respectively, at four or greater. Nine studies assessed positron emission tomography for nodal staging, with fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography demonstrating superior sensitivity (23 to 81%) compared to conventional computed tomography (13 to 47%). Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor tracers showed the highest sensitivity (82 to 100%) with specificity of 82 to 90%. One radiomics study achieved 73% sensitivity and 84% specificity for lymph node detection. Novel imaging modalities demonstrate promising diagnostic accuracy for bladder cancer staging. The Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System provides reliable muscle invasion assessment with threshold dependent performance. Positron emission tomography with fibroblast activation protein inhibitor tracers substantially improves nodal staging over conventional computed tomography. Integration of these modalities may optimize patient management, including use or omission of neoadjuvant therapy and consideration for organ sparing approaches. Prospective multicenter validation is needed.

tag.summary: Systematic review of novel imaging before surgery for invasive bladder cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Outcomes of gastrointestinal bleeding events after first-line chemotherapy in gastrointestinal-diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a propensity-score matched analysis.
paper.mesh: Humans; Female; Lymphoma, Large B-Cell, Diffuse; Male; Gastrointestinal Hemorrhage; Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols; Gastrointestinal Neoplasms; Middle Aged; Propensity Score; Aged; Vincristine; Doxorubicin; Cyclophosphamide; Prednisone; Adult; Treatment Outcome; Rituximab; Retrospective Studies; Prognosis
paper.abstract: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) is a life-threatening complication of first-line chemotherapy in gastrointestinal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (GI-DLBCL), yet its prognostic significance remains poorly defined. This propensity score-matched study (1:2) included 79 patients with GI-DLBCL, comparing 9 with post-chemotherapy GIB to controls without GIB. Matching was based on gender, clinical stage, Hans classification, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status. Patients with GIB had worse overall survival (OS, P = 0.006) and progression-free survival(PFS, P = 0.011), with markedly lower complete (11.11% vs. 66.67%, P = 0.013) and objective (66.67% vs. 100.00%, P = 0.029) response rates. Higher baseline PET-CT parameters including gastrointestinal-metabolic tumor volume (GI-MTV, P = 0.002) and gastrointestinal-total lesion glycolysis (GI-TLG, P = 0.004) indicated GIB occurrence. In the survival analysis, high ECOG (P = 0.032), whole-body metabolic tumor volume (Wb-MTV, P = 0.012), and total lesion glycolysis (Wb-TLG, P = 0.038) might be associated with poor OS, while high ECOG (P = 0.008) and international prognostic index (IPI, P =0.027) were associated with poor PFS. GIB was successfully managed with conservative medical therapy in the majority of cases (77.78%), with the remainder (22.22%) requiring endoscopic hemostasis. Post-chemotherapy GIB in GI-DLBCL is associated with a poor prognosis, particularly in patients with elevated baseline PET/CT metabolic parameters indicative of high tumor burden.

tag.summary: Outcomes of gastrointestinal bleeding after chemotherapy in lymphoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Preclinical Evaluation of 89Zr-Labeled Anti-Nectin-4 Antibody for Enhanced PET Imaging in Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma.
paper.mesh: Animals; Humans; Zirconium; Urinary Bladder Neoplasms; Mice; Antibodies, Monoclonal; Radioisotopes; Cell Adhesion Molecules; Positron-Emission Tomography; Female; Radiopharmaceuticals; Cell Line, Tumor; Tissue Distribution; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Mice, Nude
paper.abstract: This study evaluated the preclinical performance of a novel 89Zr-labeled anti-Nectin-4 monoclonal antibody, [89Zr]Zr-DFO-MW282, for PET imaging of bladder urothelial carcinoma (BUC). [89Zr]Zr-DFO-MW282 was prepared via p-isothiocyanatobenzyl-desferrioxamine (p-NCS-Bn-DFO) conjugation, achieving a radiolabeling yield exceeding 70%, radiochemical purity ≥95% post-purification, and specific activity of 36.10-63.72 GBq/μmol. [89Zr]Zr-DFO-MW282 selectively accumulated in Nectin-4-positive cells and tumors, with uptake blocked by the unlabeled MW282 antibody. Small-animal PET/CT imaging revealed sustained tumor uptake in SW780 xenografts, with a high SUVmean value of 4.46 ± 0.02 at 120 h p.i. Owing to hepatobiliary clearance, the kidney and bladder uptake was minimal, yielding excellent imaging contrast. The probe demonstrated high specificity, prolonged tumor retention, and negligible bladder background, making it a promising immuno-PET probe for precise imaging of BUC and warranting further clinical translation.

tag.summary: Preclinical evaluation of a zirconium-labelled antibody for bladder cancer imaging. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: High-Affinity Y1 Receptor Theranostics: First-in-Class Stabilized Nonapeptides for Breast Cancer Imaging and Therapy.
paper.mesh: Humans; Breast Neoplasms; Animals; Female; Receptors, Neuropeptide Y; Mice; Tissue Distribution; Radiopharmaceuticals; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; HEK293 Cells; Oligopeptides; MCF-7 Cells; Theranostic Nanomedicine
paper.abstract: Theranostic agents integrate diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities into a single molecular platform, offering an advanced approach to personalized medicine. The neuropeptide Y1 receptor (Y1R) is a promising target for breast cancer theranostics given its overexpression across multiple disease stages. Building on the Y1R-selective antagonist [Lys2, Arg4]BVD-15, we report the systematic development of stabilized nonapeptide analogues through strategic modifications. Lead candidates were radiolabeled in >95% radiochemical purity and showed Y1R binding affinities up to 60-fold higher than the parent peptide, no detectable plasma degradation over 90 min, and half-lives of 42-55 min in liver and kidney homogenates. PET-CT imaging in HEK-Y1R and MCF-7 tumor models demonstrated selective tumor uptake, peaking at 19.2% ID/g in HEK-Y1R tumors, with biodistribution studies confirming specific tumor accumulation and progressive clearance over 48 h. Therapeutic evaluation of lead candidate [177Lu]Lu-31 in HEK-Y1R tumor-bearing mice showed dose-dependent tumor growth inhibition, supporting this peptide class as Y1R-targeted radionuclide therapeutics.

tag.summary: Stabilised nonapeptides developed for breast cancer imaging and therapy. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Maleimide-Thiol Conjugation Enables the Optimization of 68Ga-Labeled CAIX Targeting PET Probes.
paper.mesh: Animals; Gallium Radioisotopes; Humans; Mice; Positron-Emission Tomography; Maleimides; Carbonic Anhydrase IX; Sulfhydryl Compounds; Tissue Distribution; Radiopharmaceuticals; Antigens, Neoplasm
paper.abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a well-established biomarker of tumor hypoxia and an attractive target for molecular imaging. Despite the development of small-molecule CAIX-targeting positron emission tomography (PET) probes, most exhibit high normal-organ uptake and suboptimal tumor-to-background contrast. Moreover, their application in hypoxic tumors remains insufficiently explored. Herein, we reported four 68Ga-labeled CAIX-targeting probes based on the acetazolamide (AAZ) scaffold, employing distinct conjugation strategies, including amide coupling and maleimide-thiol ligation. All probes demonstrated detectable tumor uptake in vivo. Among them, [68Ga]Ga-SMIC-2607 displayed the highest tumor uptake (14.67 ± 3.06 %ID/g) and tumor-to-kidney ratio (1.69 ± 0.41) at 1 h in subcutaneous OS-RC-2-bearing mice, along with high tumor uptake in HT-29-bearing mice (2.98 ± 0.28 %ID/g at 1 h). Overall, [68Ga]Ga-SMIC-2607 demonstrates favorable imaging characteristics, with high tumor uptake and high tumor-to-normal organ ratios, representing a promising candidate for imaging CAIX-overexpressing tumors and supporting clinical translation.

tag.summary: Conjugation chemistry used to optimise gallium-labelled carbonic anhydrase IX probes. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Evaluation of 68Ga Labeling Strategies and Thermostability of HER2-Targeted Nanobody NB46.
paper.mesh: Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases; Animals; Single-Domain Antibodies; Humans; Mice; Gallium Radioisotopes; Tissue Distribution; Temperature; Female; Cell Line, Tumor; Radiopharmaceuticals
paper.abstract: The HER2-targeted nanobody NB46 was evaluated for labeling strategy flexibility and thermostability. Random and site-specific 68Ga labeling strategies were compared. Both conjugates exhibited high HER2 affinity, comparable to unmodified NB46. Cellular uptake, pharmacokinetics, micro-PET/CT imaging, and biodistribution in HER2-positive and HER2-negative tumor-bearing mice revealed no significant differences between the two strategies. NB46 retained HER2 affinity at temperatures up to 90 °C, demonstrating exceptional thermostability. Both conjugates achieved >95% radiochemical yields at all tested temperatures. Micro-PET/CT imaging showed sustained high tumor uptake with renal clearance as the primary elimination pathway. Blocking studies confirmed that NB46 and trastuzumab competitively bind to HER2. Elevated labeling temperatures did not compromise tumor targeting but resulted in a mild increase in renal uptake, notably for the random conjugate at 90 °C. These findings suggest that random labeling may represent a simpler, equally effective alternative for 68Ga-NB46 preparation, and confirm the excellent thermostability of this nanobody scaffold.

tag.summary: Labelling strategies and thermostability assessed for a HER2-targeted nanobody. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET.
paper.abstract: Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl-carboxyl C-C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C-C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity. The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

tag.summary: Consecutive decarboxylation used to contract the skeleton of waste PET into benzene; a catalysis paper.

paper.title: Sarcoid-like Reaction With Pleural Involvement After Neoadjuvant Chemo-immunotherapy For Lung Cancer: A Rare Mimic of Disease Progression.
paper.abstract: We report a patient with stage IIA (cT2bN0M0) lung adenocarcinoma who developed new diffuse pleural, pulmonary, and nodal FDG uptake on 18FDG-PET/CT after three cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus cisplatin-pemetrexed, with slight regression of the primary tumour. These findings raised the diagnostic dilemma between disease progression and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-related sarcoid-like reaction (SLR). Rapid clinical and metabolic improvement after corticosteroid therapy supported SLR, which was subsequently confirmed histologically by noncaseating granulomas without viable tumour at surgery. This case highlights pleural involvement in SLR as a rare and diagnostically challenging immune-related adverse event.

tag.summary: Case report of a sarcoid-like reaction after chemo-immunotherapy for lung cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: [18F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Incidental Detection of a Benign Phyllodes Tumor in a Patient With Prior Colon Cancer.
paper.abstract: We present [18F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT findings of an incidentally detected benign phyllodes tumor in a 68-year-old woman with prior colon cancer. Routine contrast-enhanced CT revealed a right breast nodule with moderate enhancement, and subsequent PET/CT demonstrated intense focal FAPI uptake (SUVmax: 6.63). Histology confirmed the presence of a benign phyllodes tumor. This case highlights that FAPI-avid lesions in cancer survivors may represent benign entities with fibroblast-rich stroma, underscoring the importance of considering benign diagnoses and obtaining histologic confirmation to avoid unnecessary treatment.

tag.summary: Incidental detection of a benign phyllodes tumour on tracer imaging. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: FAPI PET/CT Outperforms MRI and FDG PET/CT in Tumor Delineation for Low-grade Nasopharyngeal Papillary Adenocarcinoma.
paper.abstract: Low-grade nasopharyngeal papillary adenocarcinoma (LGNPPA) is a rare entity. We report a 27-year-old man with a 1-year history of bloody postnasal drip. MRI revealed a protuberance on the roof and posterior wall of the nasopharynx with contrast enhancement. 18F-FDG PET/CT showed mild uptake with poorly defined lesion extent, whereas 18F-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated intense uptake confined to the tumor with clear boundaries. No metastases were detected. Postoperative pathology confirmed LGNPPA, and the tumor boundary delineated on FAPI PET/CT precisely matched the pathologic extent. This case suggests that FAPI PET/CT may be superior to FDG PET/CT and MRI for tumor delineation in LGNPPA.

tag.summary: Tracer imaging compared with magnetic resonance for nasopharyngeal adenocarcinoma delineation. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Rectosigmoid Intussusception Secondary to Colorectal Carcinoma Imaged With 18F-FDG PET/CT.
paper.abstract: Intussusception of bowel in adults is relatively rare and most commonly secondary to gastrointestinal malignancies. We present the case of an 80-year-old man with rectosigmoid adenocarcinoma evaluated via 18F-FDG PET/CT. Imaging revealed rectosigmoid intussusception with a characteristic "target sign" on both PET and CT images involving the invaginated bowel, alongside synchronous FDG-avid lung metastases. Subsequent MRI confirmed the anatomical findings. This case highlights the unique utility of hybrid 18F-FDG PET/CT in simultaneously delineating both malignant and nonmalignant metabolic and anatomical changes and providing critical whole-body staging to guide clinical management.

tag.summary: Case report of rectosigmoid intussusception secondary to colorectal carcinoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Not Every PSMA-Expressing Bone Lesion Is Prostate Cancer: Incidental Detection of Metastatic Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma on Staging 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT.
paper.abstract: 68Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT is widely used for staging prostate cancer but may also detect nonprostatic malignancies owing to prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) expression in tumor neovasculature. Here, we report a case of a newly diagnosed high-risk prostate adenocarcinoma that underwent staging 68Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT. In addition to the primary prostatic lesion, PSMA-expressing lesions were identified in the sternum and right thyroid lobe. While skeletal involvement was initially presumed metastatic prostate cancer, further evaluation revealed follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma. This case highlights an important diagnostic pitfall and demonstrates the value of PSMA-PET/CT in uncovering clinically occult synchronous malignancies.

tag.summary: Incidental thyroid carcinoma detected on prostate-specific membrane antigen imaging. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: FDG Uptake Extending From the Dorsal Root Ganglion to the Sciatic Nerve After Herpes Zoster.
paper.abstract: A woman in her 50s receiving paclitaxel, carboplatin, and pembrolizumab for recurrent cervical cancer developed herpes zoster and received antiviral therapy. 18F-FDG PET/CT performed 22 days after zoster onset, when the skin lesions had crusted, demonstrated continuous uptake extending from the left L5 dorsal root ganglion to the sciatic nerve. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of FDG PET findings indicating ganglioneuritis extending from the dorsal root ganglion to a peripheral nerve after herpes zoster. Recognition of this pattern is important in patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy because it may mimic immune-related neuritis or perineural tumor spread.

tag.summary: Case report of tracer uptake along the sciatic nerve after herpes zoster. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: A Favorable Partial Response in Patients With Glioblastoma Multiforme Following Combined [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 and Chemotherapy.
paper.abstract: This report highlights the potential role of [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 PET/CT in the early detection of active tumor recurrence in a 64-year-old woman with glioblastoma multiforme (IDH-wild type, WHO grade IV), preceding definitive radiologic evidence of disease progression. Following confirmation of recurrence, the patient underwent combined chemotherapy and [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 radioligand therapy, resulting in a favorable partial molecular and anatomic response as demonstrated by serial PET/CT and MRI examinations. This case illustrates the potential theranostic value of FAP-targeted imaging and radionuclide therapy in the management of recurrent glioblastoma.

tag.summary: Partial response in glioblastoma after combined radioligand therapy and chemotherapy. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: A Head-to-Head Comparison of Detection Rate and Tumor Uptake of FAPI, PSMA, and FDG PET/CT in Newly Diagnosed High-risk Prostate Cancer.
paper.abstract: PURPOSE: This study was designed to investigate the detection rate and tumor uptake of 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET/CT in newly diagnosed high-risk prostate cancer (PCa), compared with 68Ga-PSMA-11 and 18F-FDG PET/CT. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study enrolled 48 patients with biopsy-diagnosed, treatment-naive high-risk PCa who underwent 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, 68Ga-PSMA-11, and 18F-FDG PET/CT between April and December 2024. A head-to-head comparison of detection rate and tumor uptake was performed among the 3 tracers. In addition, 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68Ga-PSMA-11 dual-tracer PET was used to characterize the imaging phenotypes of each lesion and interlesional heterogeneity. RESULTS: A total of 477 lesions were detected by the 3 PET tracers. 68Ga-PSMA-11 exhibited the highest overall detection rate (96.4%), followed by 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI (81.1%) and 18F-FDG (66.0%). A total of 17 68Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions were identified in 8 patients, all of which were detected by 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, whereas only 12 were detected by 18F-FDG. Combined 68Ga-PSMA-11 and 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET identified all lesions detected by triple-tracer PET. Based on relative tracer dominance of dual-tracer PET, patients were classified as PSMA-dominant (n=23), FAPI-dominant (n=5), or mixed phenotype (n=20). The mixed phenotype with marked interlesional heterogeneity might be associated with more advanced clinical characteristics, with a higher proportion of metastatic disease and a greater metastatic burden. CONCLUSIONS: 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI is a promising PET tracer for newly diagnosed high-risk PCa. It may improve the detection rate of 68Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions and provide complementary information that could reflect interlesional heterogeneity. The clinical value of combining 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET requires further validation in larger prospective cohorts.

tag.summary: Head-to-head comparison of three tracers in newly diagnosed prostate cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: A Tale of 3 Tracers: Contrasting Uptake Patterns of 18F-FDG, 68Ga-DOTATATE, and 18F-MFBG in a Pediatric Neuroblastoma Patient.
paper.abstract: A 5-year-old boy underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT before the histopathologic diagnosis of neuroblastoma, revealing a metabolically active left adrenal primary tumor with metastases to the liver. Following resection and chemotherapy, sequential 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and 18F-MFBG demonstrated tracer-specific uptake patterns: 18F-MFBG identified a solitary hepatic metastasis undetected by 68Ga-DOTATATE. This case underscores the complementary diagnostic value of multimodal molecular imaging in pediatric neuroblastoma response assessment.

tag.summary: Contrasting uptake of three tracers in a paediatric neuroblastoma patient. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Intradiverticular Bladder Cancer Mimicking a Normal Urinary Bladder Diverticulum on FDG PET/CT.
paper.abstract: Bladder diverticula are predisposed to developing intradiverticular bladder tumors. We describe FDG PET/CT findings in a case of intradiverticular bladder cancer. At FDG PET/CT (62 min), the intradiverticular bladder cancer appeared as an exophytic lesion with similar density to the urine in the bladder‌ and intense activity mimicking a bladder diverticulum. At delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT (275 min), the tumor showed higher density and activity than the urine in the bladder, consistent with malignancy. This case indicates that delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT may be necessary for detecting possible intradiverticular bladder cancer in patient with bladder diverticulum.

tag.summary: Case report of intradiverticular bladder cancer on tracer imaging. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: FDG PET/CT Combined With 3D CT Reconstruction in Diagnosing Inflammatory Granuloma Secondary to Fish Bone Perforation of the Ascending Colon.
paper.abstract: A 71-year-old woman with a 5-week history of right-sided abdominal pain was initially suspected of hepatobiliary disorders. Upper abdominal ultrasound and MRI revealed unremarkable hepatobiliary findings. Although no hepatobiliary lesions were identified, MRI incidentally detected an ascending colon mass highly suspicious for malignancy. The patient underwent FDG PET/CT for differential diagnosis and preoperative staging. PET/CT with 3D CT reconstruction demonstrated a linear hyperdense foreign body within the ascending colon wall, causing focal bowel wall thickening with intense FDG avidity. These imaging findings were consistent with a foreign body-induced inflammatory granuloma, a diagnosis ultimately confirmed by colonoscopy and biopsy.

tag.summary: Case report of inflammatory granuloma after fish bone perforation of the colon. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Preclinical PET Imaging of Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in Tumors with Heterogeneous HER2 Expression.
paper.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has clinical activity in human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-low and -ultralow tumors in addition to HER2-positive tumors. However, no consistent correlation has been observed between traditional HER2 scoring criteria and response to T-DXd in HER2-low and HER2-ultralow tumors. There is a need for complementary approaches to monitor T-DXd delivery in vivo and potentially improve understanding of which tumors may benefit from T-DXd therapy. This study evaluated tumor uptake of radiolabeled T-DXd in tumors with varying HER2 protein levels using PET in treatment-naïve tumors and during T-DXd therapy. Methods: Chelator-conjugated T-DXd or trastuzumab was prepared via conventional lysine conjugation and radiolabeled with 64Cu. The binding and in vitro cytotoxicity of the conjugates were determined in cancer cell lines. PET/CT was performed across 11 tumor models (representing 5 tumor types), including cell xenografts, patient-derived xenografts, and syngeneic models in both subcutaneous and orthotopic models. Image-based tumor uptake of the radiolabeled antibodies was quantified in all models. In the treatment studies, mice bearing CT26-hHER2 tumors that express heterogeneous HER2 with an immunohistochemistry score of 2+ levels received weekly coinjections of therapeutic T-DXd (6 mg/kg) together with imaging-dose [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd (4 mg/kg), corresponding to a total T-DXd administered dose of 10 mg/kg. Results: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd was obtained at a radiochemical purity of at least 98%. Purified [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd bound to cells in a concentration-dependent manner and had a positive correlation between HER2 protein levels and bound T-DXd. Conjugation of T-DXd to NOTA did not affect T-DXd binding or cytotoxicity in cancer cells. [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd mean tumor uptake varied across models (7.45 ± 1.28 to 19.10 ± 2.50 %ID/mL), and the mean uptake was similar to that of the parental antibody 64Cu-labeled trastuzumab. Preimaging doses of either trastuzumab or pertuzumab did not affect [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake in tumors. There was a positive correlation between the change in [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake and the change in tumor volume between weeks 1 and 2 of T-DXd treatment (P < 0.01) in CT26.hHER2 tumors grown in immunocompetent mice. Conclusion: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd PET detects antibody-drug accumulation in tumors with low HER2 protein levels and may provide an early imaging biomarker associated with response. These studies show the potential of using HER2-targeted imaging in preclinical models to noninvasively assess antibody-drug conjugate delivery and explore imaging-based biomarkers associated with T-DXd response.

tag.summary: Preclinical imaging of an antibody-drug conjugate in tumours with heterogeneous HER2 expression. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Clinical Value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT Versus [18F]FDG PET/CT for Primary Staging of Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma: Results from a Prospective Northern European Trial.
paper.abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.

tag.summary: Prospective trial comparing two tracers for staging gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: [18F]DOPA PET Reveals Metabolically Active Transcriptomic States Associated with Clinical Outcome in Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
paper.abstract: [18F]fluorodihydroxyphenylalanine ([18F]DOPA) uptake is dependent on amino acid transport and decarboxylation pathways, including large neutral amino acid transporter 1, encoded by SLC7A5, which are linked to tumor aggressiveness. This study evaluated whether in vivo uptake of [18F]DOPA can serve as an imaging biomarker for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (panNETs), reflecting a tumor's transcriptional status and a patient's clinical course. Methods: This retrospective single-center study was based on a transcriptomic cohort of 74 primary panNETs. A subset of 22 panNETs from patients who underwent preoperative [18F]DOPA PET/CT constituted the discovery radiotranscriptomic cohort. [18F]DOPA tumor uptake was quantified using SUVmax and integrated with matched RNA-sequencing data. Unsupervised clustering, differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment, and tumor microenvironment deconvolution were performed to identify transcriptional programs associated with [18F]DOPA uptake. The prognostic value of SLC7A5 was evaluated in the discovery cohort, the full transcriptomic cohort (n = 74), and an independent external cohort (n = 33). Results: Unsupervised clustering of gene expression profiles identified 2 robust molecular subtypes: cluster 1 and cluster 2. Cluster 1 showed higher [18F]DOPA uptake than did cluster 2, with a median SUVmax of 24.3 versus 5.9, respectively (P = 0.030), and was associated with more advanced clinicopathologic features and shorter event-free survival. This subtype was also characterized by enrichment in extracellular matrix, stromal, vascular, and immune-related components, along with upregulation of amino acid transport and amine metabolism genes, including SLC7A5 As a mechanistic link between tracer uptake and tumor metabolism, SLC7A5 expression significantly stratified event-free survival in the discovery cohort and remained prognostic in the full cohort. Conclusion: [18F]DOPA PET uptake was associated with amino acid-driven metabolic programs in panNETs, including SLC7A5 expression, and adverse clinical features. These findings suggest that [18F]DOPA uptake may provide a noninvasive readout of tumor metabolic activity, although its value as an imaging biomarker requires independent validation.

tag.summary: Tracer uptake related to transcriptomic states in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Prognostic Value of 68Ga-NOTA-AE105 uPAR PET/CT in Resected Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Single-Center Prospective Study.
paper.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer shows wide variability in outcomes after curative-intent resection. 18F-FDG PET/CT is indispensable for staging but primarily reflects glucose metabolism rather than the invasion-related tumor biology that may contribute to recurrence. 68Ga-NOTA-AE105 PET/CT images the urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR), a cell-surface mediator of local invasion and metastatic spread. We assessed whether preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET/CT is prognostic for postoperative recurrence. Methods: We conducted a single-center cohort study of patients with resectable lung adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma who were prospectively enrolled to undergo preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET/CT in addition to standard-of-care 18F-FDG PET/CT. Primary tumor SUVmean and SUVmax were measured for both tracers, and tumor tissue uPAR expression was quantified by immunohistochemistry (H-score). Postoperative recurrence was the primary endpoint and was analyzed in a competing-risks framework with death as a competing event. The primary prognostic analyses evaluated 68Ga-uPAR SUVs, 18F-FDG SUVs, and uPAR H-score as continuous variables using univariable cause-specific Cox models. A 1.5-y horizon was used for exploratory Youden-derived high versus low groups, for which cumulative incidence of recurrence was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method. Trial registration number is NCT02755675 Results: Thirty-seven patients comprised the analysis cohort, of whom 14 developed recurrence during a median follow-up of 2.38 y (interquartile range, 1.97-8.20 y). Four patients died without prior recurrence. 68Ga-uPAR uptake correlated with tumor tissue uPAR expression, whereas 18F-FDG uptake did not. As continuous prognostic factors, higher 68Ga-uPAR SUVmax (hazard ratio, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.34-3.49; P = 0.002) and higher uPAR H-score (hazard ratio, 1.04 per unit; 95% CI, 1.01-1.08; P = 0.017) were associated with recurrence; 68Ga-uPAR SUVmean showed borderline evidence of association (P = 0.053), whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prognostic. Exploratory 1.5-y threshold analyses showed greater early recurrence in the high SUVmean and high H-score groups; the SUVmax comparison did not reach statistical significance. Conclusion: Preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET uptake reflected tumor uPAR expression and was associated with early postoperative recurrence, whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prognostic in this cohort. These findings suggest that uPAR PET captures invasion-related tumor biology that is not fully reflected by glucose metabolism imaging. External validation is required.

tag.summary: Prognostic value of a uPAR tracer in resected non-small cell lung cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Robotic-assisted transduodenal ampullectomy for a neuroendocrine tumour: A step-by-step surgical video.
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND: When endoscopic resection of ampullary neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) is not feasible due to tumour size or location, transduodenal ampullectomy can offer a parenchymal-sparing alternative to a formal pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) [1,2]. We present a robotic-assisted transduodenal ampullectomy (RATA) in a 71-year-old male with an incidental 14 mm ampullary NET found during routine screening. Preoperative 68Ga-DOTATATE PET-CT demonstrated intense somatostatin-receptor avidity (SUVmax 66.8) and absent FDG uptake. The MDT recommended surgical excision due to size and Ki-67 4%. METHODS: Following right colonic flexure mobilisation and a Kocher maneuver, the cystic duct was isolated and cannulated with a 4 Fr catheter to guide biliary identification. After a longitudinal duodenotomy, the ampullary lesion was visualized. Submucosal saline-adrenaline was injected in the submucosal plane. Diathermy scissors were used to perform a circumferential mucosal and muscularis dissection. Biliary and pancreatic ducts were sharply divided and reconstructed using interrupted 5/0 polydioxanone sutures between the pancreatobiliary ducts and the duodenal mucosa after positioning a 6 Fr catheter in the pancreatic duct. The duodenotomy was closed in two layers using a 4/0 absorbable barbed suture, and a methylene blue leak test through the nasogastric tube confirmed duodenal integrity. RESULTS: The procedure was completed successfully with no intraoperative complications. A postoperative contrast-enhanced CT on day 5 demonstrated no collections and no oral contrast extravasation. Oral feeding was gradually reintroduced, the abdominal drain was removed, and the patient was discharged on day 7. Following a brief readmission on day 13 for a pulmonary microembolism successfully treated with medical therapy, the patient recovered fully and remains disease-free 7 months after surgery. CONCLUSION: RATA can represent a safe, feasible, and pancreas-preserving alternative to formal pancreaticoduodenectomy for well-differentiated ampullary NETs in selected patients. The robotic platform enhances three-dimensional visualization and wrist articulation, optimizing the delicate micro-reconstruction of the pancreaticobiliary junction.

tag.summary: Surgical video of robotic transduodenal ampullectomy for a neuroendocrine tumour. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Highly selective depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate plastic via Au/attapulgite dual-site synergy.
paper.abstract: The chemical recycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into high-value terephthalic acid (TPA) under mild conditions remains a significant challenge. Herein, we construct a dual-active-site Au/ATP catalyst via electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) by supporting Au on inexpensive attapulgite (ATP). Under optimal conditions (200 °C, 1 MPa Ar, 4 h), this catalyst achieves near-complete conversion of PET with a terephthalic acid (TPA) yield of 91.76 ± 1.65%, and is also effective for actual waste plastic bottle flakes. The EMSI stabilizes Au nanoparticles, modulates Lewis acidity to suppress side reactions, and enables selective ester-bond cleavage without affecting the benzene ring or CC bonds. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), work-function analysis and density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the EMSI effect drives electron transfer from Au to ATP, generating Auδ+ species. These species can effectively polarize the CO bond to generate an electron-deficient intermediate. Meanwhile, ATP provides an adsorption and activation platform for H2O, promoting the generation of nucleophilic *OH. The synergy of these two sites enables highly performance depolymerization. This work provides a sustainable strategy for polyester chemical recycling and the value-added upgrading of low-grade mineral resources.

tag.summary: A gold and clay dual-site catalyst used to depolymerise PET into terephthalic acid; a catalysis paper.

paper.title: State of the art imaging in ovarian carcinomatosis: how the radiologist can help plan management.
paper.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is the leading cause of gynaecological cancer mortality and is most often diagnosed at an advanced stage due to its subtle early clinical presentation and characteristic peritoneal dissemination. High-grade serous carcinoma represents the predominant epithelial subtype and frequently presents with extensive peritoneal disease, making accurate preoperative evaluation essential. Management of advanced OC (AOC) hinges on the selection of patients for primary cytoreductive surgery vs neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval cytoreduction, with complete cytoreduction remaining the strongest prognostic factor. Radiologists therefore play a critical role in assessing disease distribution, identifying features suggestive of unresectability, and guiding multidisciplinary decision-making. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is the first-line modality for staging AOC, providing comprehensive assessment of peritoneal, nodal, and extra-abdominal disease. Despite its established utility, CT has reduced sensitivity for small-volume implants and involvement in surgically complex regions. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers superior soft tissue characterisation and improves detection of peritoneal disease along the bowel serosa, mesentery, and subdiaphragmatic spaces, particularly through diffusion-weighted and contrast-enhanced techniques. Positron emission tomography (PET)/CT provides complementary metabolic information that can enhance detection of nodal and extraperitoneal metastases in selected cases. Emerging quantitative techniques, including radiomics and machine learning-based analysis, have the potential to extract biologically relevant imaging biomarkers, refine predictions of resectability, and stratify recurrence risk. Integrating these tools with conventional imaging may further support personalised treatment pathways. This review summarises current evidence regarding CT, MRI, and PET in the evaluation of peritoneal disease in AOC and highlights how imaging advances and radiologist expertise can optimise surgical planning and guide management strategies.

tag.summary: Review of imaging in ovarian carcinomatosis to plan management. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Bio-Emulsion Liquid Membrane for Dual-Functional Water Treatment: Microplastic Removal and Antimicrobial Activity.
paper.mesh: Emulsions; Microplastics; Water Purification; Biosurfactants; Membranes, Artificial; Polystyrenes; Polyethylene; Anti-Bacterial Agents; Hexoses; Anti-Infective Agents; Saponins; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Escherichia coli; Microbial Sensitivity Tests
paper.abstract: Microplastics are polymer particles smaller than 5 mm that originate from the degradation of larger plastic debris and persist in the environment. In the present study, polyethylene (PE) and polystyrene (PS) microplastics with particle sizes of 1-5 μm were used as model contaminants. It contaminates water sources, including drinking water, posing a significant risk to human health and the environment. In this study, a biosurfactant-based amphiphilic emulsifier was used in combination with Span 80 to develop a functional bioemulsion liquid membrane (Bio-ELM). The parameter optimization during Bio-ELM synthesis yielded the following optimized emulsification parameters: saponin (1% v/v), Span 80 (1.5% v/v), NaOH (0.2 M), MP: IP ratio (1:0.5), stirring speed 800 rpm, and emulsification time 5 min. The enhanced emulsion stability and membrane integrity are attributed to the interfacial activity of the biopolymer-derived saponin, which contains hydrophilic and hydrophobic functional moieties. They are responsible for improving ELM stability and facilitating selective transport. Emulsion stability was analyzed using the creaming index (CI) and microscopic images during parameter optimization. Two model microplastic samples, polyethylene (PE) and polystyrene (PS), were extracted using Bio-ELM, with extraction efficiencies of 95% and 89%, respectively. Bio-ELM demonstrated microbial growth inhibition, as evidenced by a zone of inhibition (ZOI). Bio-ELM components disrupt bacterial membranes and inhibit bacterial growth in contaminated water. Bio-ELM synthesis offers multifunctional properties, cost-effectiveness, environmental friendliness, enhanced emulsion stability, increased extraction efficiency, and antimicrobial activity.

tag.summary: A bio-emulsion liquid membrane developed for microplastic removal and antimicrobial action; a water treatment paper.

paper.title: High-Resolution Fluorescence Microscopy-Based 3D Encoding Using Polarity-Sensitive Dyes for Rapid Screening of Microplastics in Complex Environmental Samples.
paper.mesh: Microscopy, Fluorescence; Microplastics; Fluorescent Dyes; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Imaging, Three-Dimensional
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs), as emerging pollutants of global concern, urgently require rapid monitoring techniques for effective ecological risk management. Fluorescence microscopy is widely utilized for capturing the morphology of MPs but remains limited in polymer-type discrimination and differentiation from environmental matrices. Herein, we present a novel fluorescence microscopy-based three-dimensional (3D) encoding strategy employing three polarity-sensitive dyes (DNAS, DCM, and MONS) for rapid screening of MPs in complex environmental matrices. Owing to differences in the surface polarity of MPs, the adsorbed polarity-sensitive dyes undergo intramolecular charge transfer (ICT). The polarity-dependent stabilization of the excited charge-transfer state alters the emission energy, resulting in distinct fluorescence colors on different MPs. The three dyes also exhibited varied ICT responses due to hydrogen-bonding and dipole-dipole interactions between the surface groups of MPs and the dyes, facilitating encoding-based discrimination. Stained images were captured with a self-constructed portable fluorescence microscope. The images were converted from RGB values into CIE L*a*b* coordinates to construct a 3D encoding library, where triangular or linear pattern encoding greatly enhanced the spatial separation of MPs and sample matrices. This method enabled rapid identification of 12 common MP types and clear differentiation from ten natural nonplastic matrices. The CIE L*a*b* coordinates exhibited good repeatability, with RSD values of 0.69-4.99% (n = 10). Both "known-as-unknown" spiked sample validation and the analysis of real environmental samples demonstrate that the proposed workflow can rapidly identify polymer types in complex samples, with the results agreeing well with those obtained by FTIR. This low-cost, portable, and spectrometer-free strategy offers a practical tool for rapid screening of MPs in complex environmental samples.

tag.summary: Polarity-sensitive dyes and fluorescence microscopy used to screen microplastics in environmental samples; a method paper.

paper.title: "Imaging Triplets on Two Wheels": 61Cu-, 64Cu-, and 68Ga-labeled Bicyclic Peptides Targeting Nectin-4 Enable High-Contrast PET Imaging of Urothelial Carcinoma and Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
paper.mesh: Humans; Animals; Nectins; Copper Radioisotopes; Female; Triple Negative Breast Neoplasms; Positron-Emission Tomography; Mice; Cell Line, Tumor; Urologic Neoplasms; Peptides, Cyclic; Radiopharmaceuticals; Gallium Radioisotopes
paper.abstract: Nectin-4 is a validated target for theranostic approaches toward urothelial carcinoma, and radiolabeled ligands for PET and SPECT imaging are gaining increasing interest for noninvasive quantification of Nectin-4 prior to a targeted therapy. The goal of this study was to develop bicyclic peptides that allow radiolabeling with three different radionuclides (61Cu, 64Cu, and 68Ga) and to evaluate their suitability for high-contrast PET imaging in urothelial carcinoma (UC) and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). For this purpose, NECT-330, NECT-334, and NECT-346 were designed based on our previously developed ligand NECT-224 but harbor additional linker units between the bicyclic scaffold and the radiometal chelator. Binding kinetics to recombinant Nectin-4 and related isoforms were assessed by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) interaction analysis. Nectin-4-specific cell binding of the radiolabeled probes was determined using UC and TNBC cell lines, and PET/CT imaging was performed in respective tumor xenograft models. All novel ligands showed potent and selective binding to Nectin-4, with improved koff values compared to NECT-224. In small-animal PET/CT imaging studies, the most favorable properties were observed for [64Cu]Cu-NECT-334 (tumor-to-muscle of 20.8 and tumor-to-heart of 11.2) and [64Cu]Cu-NECT-346 (tumor-to-muscle of 15.5 and tumor-to-heart of 8.7) 1-2 h postinjection using a HT-1376 tumor model. Although the novel radioligands provided superior imaging properties to the previously developed radioligand [64Cu]Cu-NECT-224, a first-in-human application of the latter radioligand was initiated to assess the general suitability of PET/CT imaging in humans with a 64Cu-labeled bicyclic peptide directed to Nectin-4. Prospectively, the improved tumor-to-background contrasts achieved with the novel radioligands might further improve diagnostic accuracy and facilitate effective theranostic options in Nectin-4-expressing malignancies.

tag.summary: Radiolabelled bicyclic peptides targeting nectin-4 for tumour imaging. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Hydrolytic-Peroxidatic Cascade on Bifunctional Nanozymes for Specific Fluorescent Profiling of Aromatic Polyester Microplastics.
paper.mesh: Microplastics; Polyesters; Hydrolysis; Fluorescence; Nanostructures; Phthalic Acids
paper.abstract: Aromatic polyester microplastics are derived from a special type of engineering plastic. Therefore, effective management requires reliable qualitative discrimination and accurate quantitative detection, rather than simply measuring total microplastic concentrations. To address this challenge, we developed a cascading fluorescence sensing platform based on the sequential dual-enzyme mimicry of magnesium-iron layered double oxide (MgFe LDO) nanozymes. MgFe LDO first hydrolyzes aromatic polyesters into terephthalic acid (TPA), which is subsequently hydroxylated via its peroxidase-mimicking activity to generate the fluorescent product 2-hydroxyterephthalic acid. Differences in hydrolysis rate and TPA concentration arising from the structural variation among distinct aromatic polyesters are translated into quantifiable fluorescence signals, enabling the precise detection and specific discrimination of multiple polymers. The bifunctional nanozymes combining hydrolase-like and peroxidase-like activities exhibit reliable performance and adaptability in spiked real-world samples, including rainwater, river water, tap water, and seawater. This work provides a basis for constructing integrated laboratory-based screening platforms for aromatic polyester microplastics using rationally engineered nanozymes.

tag.summary: Bifunctional nanozymes used to fluorescently profile aromatic polyester microplastics; a method paper.

paper.title: Prior-Attention-Mechanism-Based Spectral Identifier for Revealing Hazardous Chemical Additives in Commercial PVC.
paper.mesh: Polyvinyl Chloride; Hazardous Substances; Spectrum Analysis, Raman
paper.abstract: Additive components largely determine the environmental and health risks of commercial plastics, but rapid, nondestructive identification of multiple additives in polymer matrices remains challenging. To overcome this challenge, we developed a prior-knowledge-guided triple-scale convolutional neural network (SpecNet) that identified 14 additive classes and two polyvinyl chloride (PVC) types from microconfocal Raman spectra. SpecNet integrated spectral chunking, cross-attention with characteristic peak embedding, and a combined BCE and L1 loss for joint classification and semiquantitative ranking of additive abundances. Trained on 2,200 spectra, the model achieved a 95.03% F1-score on an independent environmental test set (1,000 spectra). Platt scaling reduced the Brier score to 0.03, and Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty was <0.05 when SNR > 10. The model-assisted detection threshold for tris(1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCPP) reached 2.5 wt %, approximately 2-fold lower than the conventional visual detection limit of Raman spectroscopy (∼5 wt %) by leveraging learned multipeak patterns and prior-knowledge attention to extract weak signals below visual detectability. In zero-shot tests on non-PVC polymers, SpecNet correctly identified additives in 82.8% of cases. For additives in microplastic samples after accelerated photoaging (90 days, ∼15 years natural exposure), it maintained 92.48% identification accuracy by dynamically lowering the detection threshold from 0.5 to 0.005. SpecNet offers an interpretable, field-deployable tool for screening hazardous plastic additives in environmental monitoring, recycling, and risk assessment.

tag.summary: A spectral identifier built to reveal hazardous chemical additives in commercial PVC; an analytical paper.

paper.title: Release and Transformation of Polymer-Associated Chemicals from Aged Polypropylene and Polyurethane Microplastics in Freshwater Laboratory and Mesocosm Studies.
paper.mesh: Polyurethanes; Microplastics; Polypropylenes; Fresh Water; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Polymers
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) release polymer-associated chemicals (PACs) into aquatic environments, yet their environmental release, transformation, and persistence remain poorly understood. We applied nontargeted liquid chromatography high-resolution mass spectrometry to characterize PACs released from polypropylene (PP) and polyurethane (PU) MPs in complementary 12-month freshwater wetland mesocosm and 3-month laboratory photolysis and leaching experiments. More leachable compounds were detected from PP (128) than PU (34), reflecting differences in polymer formulations and physicochemical properties. Laboratory studies identified readily mobilized and transformable PACs, including the PP additive bis(2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-4-piperidyl)sebacate (BTMS) and the PU monomer 4-(4-formamidobenzyl)phenyl formamide. Laboratory experiments using higher MP concentrations (10,000 mg L-1) prioritized target PACs for monitoring in lower-concentration mesocosms (50 mg L-1), where ricinine was quantified in PU treatments and BTMS and 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-4-piperidinol (TMPO) were quantified in PP treatments. PAC concentrations increased over time under simplified laboratory conditions but declined in environmentally complex mesocosms, suggesting environmental attenuation through processes such as sorption, sedimentation, and microbial degradation that require further confirmation in future studies. UV exposure minimally affected BTMS hydrolysis but promoted ricinine photodegradation and the formation of additional PU-derived transformation products. These findings identified environmentally relevant PACs and demonstrated the value of integrating simplified laboratory studies with environmentally realistic mesocosms to improve PAC identification and evaluate environmental fate.

tag.summary: Release and transformation of polymer-associated chemicals from aged polypropylene and polyurethane microplastics in freshwater; an environmental fate study.

paper.title: Surface Biogeochemical Regimes Shape Microplastic Abundance in the Eastern Indian Ocean.
paper.mesh: Water Pollutants, Chemical; Microplastics; Indian Ocean
paper.abstract: Open-ocean microplastic (MP) abundance is commonly reported as a contamination metric, but surface concentrations may reflect environmental redistribution, dilution, and retention in addition to source exposure. Here, we investigated surface MPs across 43 stations in the eastern Indian Ocean (EIO) during the late northeast monsoon period using in situ pumped sampling, μ-FTIR identification, and 22 environmental indicators spanning productivity, particle optical properties, hydrography, surface dynamics, mixed-layer structure, and maritime exposure. MPs were detected at all stations, with abundances ranging from 6.67 to 160.00 particles m-3 and a mean of 29.37 ± 26.72 particles m-3. This pronounced spatial heterogeneity is consistent with the intrinsic patchiness of open-ocean surface waters, where hydrodynamic transport, convergence, dispersion, and vertical redistribution can generate strong local variability in particle abundance. The regional MP assemblage was dominated by polyethylene terephthalate (PET), fibers, light-colored particles, and small MPs, with particles <200 μm accounting for 52.1% of the total. Elevated abundance was not explained by maritime exposure alone, but was associated with lower primary production, weaker particulate backscattering, warmer surface waters, and weaker surface-dynamic forcing. Using environmental variables alone to define surface-water regimes, we found that MP abundance was significantly higher in warm, low-productivity waters with weaker surface dynamics than in cooler, more productive waters with stronger surface dynamics (mean: 34.64 vs 17.18 particles m-3; Kruskal-Wallis H = 8.57, p = 0.0034). Particle composition, including polymer/material type, morphology, color, and size class, remained broadly similar across regimes. These findings suggest that environmental conditions modulate the surface abundance of an existing regional MP pool.

tag.summary: Surface biogeochemical regimes related to microplastic abundance in the eastern Indian Ocean; an oceanography study.

paper.title: Oxidative Enhancement of Polystyrene Bioconversion Associated with Bio-Fenton-Type Processes in a Mesocosm-Scale Plastivore System.
paper.mesh: Polystyrenes; Oxidation-Reduction; Animals; Iron; Tenebrio; Larva
paper.abstract: Sustainable plastic waste management calls for mesocosm-scale biological strategies coupling polymer depolymerization with controlled plastic-carbon transformation, yet routes for optimizing plastivore-mediated bioconversion beyond laboratory scale remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a mesocosm-scale plastivore-based platform using Tenebrio molitor larvae and show that moderate Fe supplementation increased the •OH-associated oxidative activity, accompanied by enhanced polystyrene (PS) depolymerization and PS disappearance. Under a simplified incineration-reference scenario, the estimated PS-derived carbon conversion flux corresponded to a gross avoided direct-emission potential of up to approximately 0.31 t CO2 per ton of larvae per month, without representing net life-cycle greenhouse gas mitigation. Molecular analyses showed greater oxidative functionalization, oligomer formation, and chain scission than under regular bioconversion. Quantitative •OH assays and fluorescence imaging further showed stronger intestinal •OH-associated levels, faster signal development, and earlier stabilization in the enhanced bioconversion system. Together, the evidence supports Fe-mediated enhancement of intestinal oxidative processes consistent with bio-Fenton-type reactions and identifies redox modulation as a promising and scalable strategy for plastic depolymerization and bioconversion.

tag.summary: Bio-Fenton-type processes shown to enhance polystyrene bioconversion in a mealworm system; a biodegradation study.

paper.title: Divergent Shifts in Sediment Dissolved Organic Matter Stability and Microbial Carbon Metabolic Potential Induced by Biodegradable and Conventional Microplastics.
paper.mesh: Microplastics; Geologic Sediments; Dissolved Organic Matter; Carbon; Biodegradation, Environmental; Polyesters
paper.abstract: Biodegradable polymers are promoted as alternatives to conventional plastics, but their effects on sediment dissolved organic matter (DOM) and microbial communities remain unclear. Here, we estimated impacts of two nonbiodegradable (low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET)) and two biodegradable (polylactide (PLA) and poly(butylene succinate) (PBS)) polymers on DOM composition and microbial functional profiles using Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS) and metagenomic sequencing. The tested nonbiodegradable polymers shifted DOM toward recalcitrance. In contrast, biodegradable polymers exhibited divergent trajectories: PLA shifted from labile at day 30 to recalcitrant by day 60, whereas PBS showed the opposite trend toward instability. Microbial communities shifted from high-abundance Deltaproteobacteria (∼12%) at day 30 to Alphaproteobacteria (∼16%) and Actinomycetia (∼15%) at day 60. Glycolysis genes were less abundant under LDPE and PET, while fatty acid β-oxidation genes were enriched under LDPE, PET, and PLA. Spearman correlation and Mantel tests revealed that MP-driven DOM changes were associated with microbial community restructuring and bacterial diversity. This study highlights that biodegradable polymers cannot be assumed to have negligible sediment ecological impacts simply because of their degradable classification.

tag.summary: Biodegradable and conventional microplastics compared for their effect on sediment organic matter and microbial metabolism; a biogeochemistry study.

paper.title: Spirocyclic Reconfiguration of the Piperazine Linker Improves Quinoline-Based FAPI PET Tracer Performance.
paper.mesh: Positron-Emission Tomography; Quinolines; Humans; Animals; Piperazines; Fibroblast Activation Protein Alpha; Spiro Compounds; Radiopharmaceuticals; Membrane Proteins; Gelatinases; Serine Endopeptidases; Cell Line, Tumor; Piperazine; Mice; Molecular Dynamics Simulation; Endopeptidases
paper.abstract: Improving the tumor uptake and retention without compromising background clearance remains challenging for fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) radiotracers. Current approaches usually introduce pharmacokinetic modules or reshape molecular scaffolds, increasing structural complexity and synthetic burden. Spirocyclic rigidification offers a distinct strategy by combining conformational constraint and well-defined three-dimensional geometry, yet has not been leveraged for designing FAPI radiopharmaceuticals. Herein, we synthesized FAPI-04 analogues by replacing the piperazine linker with spirocyclic diamines. All analogues were successfully 68Ga-labeled and retained FAP-specific recognition, hydrophilicity and serum stability, but differed in pharmacokinetics and imaging profiles. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-S1 exhibited higher tumor uptake, longer tumor residence, and improved tumor-to-background contrast than [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 in both HT-1080-FAP and U-87 MG models. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed enhanced local protein-ligand interactions without significant changes in overall complex stability. These findings support spirocyclic replacement of piperazine linker as a feasible strategy for local three-dimensional reconfiguration of quinoline-based FAPI PET tracers.

tag.summary: A spirocyclic linker shown to improve a quinoline-based FAPI tracer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: A Biphenyl-Containing Dimeric Sulfonamide PET Tracer for High-Contrast Imaging of Carbonic Anhydrase IX in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
paper.mesh: Carbonic Anhydrase IX; Humans; Carcinoma, Renal Cell; Animals; Sulfonamides; Mice; Kidney Neoplasms; Positron-Emission Tomography; Cell Line, Tumor; Radiopharmaceuticals; Tissue Distribution; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Dimerization; Gallium Radioisotopes; Antigens, Neoplasm
paper.abstract: Carbonic Anhydrase IX (CAIX) is an attractive biomarker for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but small-molecule CAIX radiotracers are often limited by insufficient tumor retention and suboptimal tumor-to-kidney contrast. Herein, we report the rational design of biphenyl-containing bivalent sulfonamide tracers and evaluation of both 68Ga and Al18F-labeled analogues. Guided by a multivalency strategy, [68Ga]Ga-CAIX-D1 and [68Ga]Ga-CAIX-N1 were developed and compared with the monomeric reference tracer [68Ga]Ga-14. In OS-RC-2 xenografts, both dimers showed higher tumor uptake, improved tumor retention, and tumor-to-kidney ratios greater than 1. The lead scaffold was further adapted to generate [18F]AlF-CAIX-N1, which displayed high tumor uptake, excellent tumor-to-muscle contrast, CAIX-specific uptake, and lower liver uptake than its 68Ga-labeled counterpart. First-in-human positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging further supported its translational feasibility. Collectively, [18F]AlF-CAIX-N1 is a promising tracer for ccRCC imaging and highlights the value of integrating bivalency with radiolabel engineering.

tag.summary: A dimeric sulfonamide tracer developed for carbonic anhydrase IX imaging in renal cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: [18F]FPyQCP: A Robust FAP-Targeted PET Tracer Integrating Covalent C-18F Labeling and Radiometal Chelation for Enhanced In Vivo Performance.
paper.mesh: Positron-Emission Tomography; Animals; Fluorine Radioisotopes; Fibroblast Activation Protein Alpha; Humans; Radiopharmaceuticals; Mice; Endopeptidases; Serine Endopeptidases; Gelatinases; Membrane Proteins; Chelating Agents; Pyrrolidines; Cell Line, Tumor; Tissue Distribution; Mice, Nude
paper.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is a validated PET imaging target for the tumor microenvironment. Currently, most 18F-labeled FAP PET agents use Al-F chemistry, with Al18F-FAPI-74 leading clinically, whereas C-18F tracers perform less effectively. Here, we developed (4-quinolinoyl)glycyl-2-cyanopyrrolidine (QCP)-based inhibitors incorporating a 6-fluoronicotinamide prosthetic group for stable C-18F labeling. Chelator incorporation improved hydrophilicity and enabled structurally matched radiometal- and 18F-labeled analogs from a common scaffold. The compounds exhibited high FAP inhibitory capacity (Ki = 9.9-56.7 pM) and favorable physicochemical properties (Log P7.4 = -3.1 ± 0.1). The lead tracer, [18F]FPyQCP, was prepared by a one-pot, two-step radiosynthesis in 50-80% yields, with >99% radiochemical purity and molar activity of 74-200 GBq/μmol. In U87 xenografts, [18F]FPyQCP achieved high tumor uptake (23.3 ± 2.1 %ID/g) and favorable tumor-to-blood ratios (12.0 ± 0.3) at 2 h. This modular labeling strategy establishes a versatile platform for next-generation FAP PET tracers and beyond.

tag.summary: A covalently fluorine-labelled FAP-targeted tracer evaluated in vivo. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Albumin-Binding Modification Improves Tumor Retention of Hydrophilic αvβ6-Targeting Radiotheranostic Tracers.
paper.mesh: Animals; Humans; Hydrophobic and Hydrophilic Interactions; Radiopharmaceuticals; Integrins; Mice; Antigens, Neoplasm; Albumins; Cell Line, Tumor; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Molecular Docking Simulation; Female; Pancreatic Neoplasms; Carcinoma, Pancreatic Ductal; Mice, Nude; Male
paper.abstract: Integrin αvβ6 is an attractive theranostic target for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Existing αvβ6-targeting tracers are limited by relatively low tumor uptake and rapid tumor washout, compromising theranostic efficacy. In this study, a series of αvβ6-targeting ligands with different hydrophilic linkers and/or albumin-binding moiety were designed and evaluated with molecular docking and MD simulations. Among them, NOTA-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L was selected for further theranostic evaluation due to its favorable targeting capability, enhanced tumor uptake and favorable pharmacokinetic properties. NOTA-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L was labeled with 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu, and showed favorable in vitro properties, including high hydrophilicity, αvβ6 affinity, and albumin binding. In PET/CT imaging, [18F]AlF/[68Ga]Ga-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L exhibited enhanced tumor uptake and prolonged retention while maintaining favorable pharmacokinetics, showing favorable diagnostic efficiency. In therapeutic studies, [177Lu]Lu-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L effectively inhibited tumor growth with no apparent toxicity. These results demonstrated [18F]AlF/[68Ga]Ga-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L and [177Lu]Lu-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L as promising radiotheranostic pairs for PDAC.

tag.summary: Albumin binding used to improve tumour retention of integrin-targeting radiotheranostics. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Active surveillance versus standard surgery after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for oesophageal cancer: long-term results of a cluster-randomised controlled trial (SANO).
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Surgery As Needed for Oesophageal cancer (SANO)-trial demonstrated that active surveillance is non-inferior to standard surgery in terms of two-year overall survival in patients with a complete clinical response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). Active surveillance resulted in improved quality of life. Here, we report five-year outcomes. METHODS: From 2017 to 2021, a multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial was conducted. Patients with locally advanced oesophageal cancer who achieved complete clinical response (defined as no tumour detected on endoscopic biopsies, -ultrasound, or PET-CT) underwent active surveillance or standard surgery. Cox regression was used to compare five-year overall and disease-free survival, and the cumulative incidence of distant metastases was estimated using competing risk analysis. RESULTS: A total of 309 patients were included, 198 underwent active surveillance and 111 underwent standard surgery. Median follow-up was 76 months (IQR 67-86). Five-year overall survival was not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery (50%, 95%CI 43-57 vs. 54%, 95%CI 46-64; HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.77-1.77) with similar results across histologic subtypes. Disease-free survival was not statistically significantly different (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.94-2.06). The cumulative incidence of distant metastases at five years was significantly higher in the active surveillance group compared to the standard surgery group (46%, 95%CI 39-53 vs. 29%, 95%CI 21-37; P<.01). Overall, 85 of 198 patients (43%) avoided oesophagectomy, including those with sustained complete clinical response at last follow-up or distant metastases detected within six months after nCRT. CONCLUSIONS: Overall survival at five years is not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery in patients with oesophageal cancer and a complete clinical response after nCRT, despite a higher incidence of distant metastases in the active surveillance group. These findings support active surveillance as a feasible treatment strategy in selected patients.

tag.summary: Long-term results of active surveillance against surgery after chemoradiotherapy for oesophageal cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: PET-Guided Dose Escalation for Stage III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
paper.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
paper.abstract: PURPOSE: Uniform radiation dose escalation has not improved outcomes in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and locoregional failure remains common despite multimodal therapy. We evaluated whether fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET)-guided dose escalation to metabolically active tumor subvolumes reduces locoregional failure compared with standard chemoradiation. METHODS AND MATERIALS: PET-BOOST was a multi-institutional, open-label, phase 2 randomized trial conducted at 7 Canadian centers (January 2017-May 2022). Eligible patients had inoperable, FDG-avid stage IIIA/IIIB NSCLC and an achievable boost dose of at least 65 Gy. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard chemoradiation with 60 Gy in 30 fractions or metabolically adaptive radiotherapy with an integrated boost to FDG-avid subvolumes to a maximum of 85 Gy in 30 fractions. Concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy was planned, and consolidation durvalumab was permitted after 2018. The primary endpoint was 2-year locoregional failure; secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicity, and quality of life (QOL). RESULTS: Seventy-eight patients were randomized: 40 to standard radiotherapy and 38 to dose escalation, with a median follow-up of 5.0 years. Median age was 64.4 years; 53% were male, 62% had stage IIIA disease, and 76% received consolidation durvalumab. Median prescription boost dose was 75 Gy. Two-year locoregional failure was 27.5% with standard radiotherapy versus 18.4% with dose escalation (P=.13). Two-year OS (72.5% vs. 73.7%; P=.91) and PFS (52.5% vs. 57.9%; P=.74) did not differ between arms. Grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicities occurred in 25% versus 37% of patients (P=.26), with one grade 5 pulmonary hemorrhage in the dose-escalation arm. QOL did not differ between arms. CONCLUSIONS: Metabolically adaptive PET-guided radiotherapy dose escalation was feasible in the context of consolidation immunotherapy and resulted in a numerically lower rate of locoregional failure, but did not significantly improve locoregional control or survival. The lower-than-anticipated event rate may have limited statistical power, and larger studies would be required to determine whether selective dose escalation provides a clinically meaningful improvement in locoregional control.

tag.summary: Randomised trial of imaging-guided dose escalation in stage III lung cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Effect of data-driven gating on the quantification of prostate cancer metastases in 68Ga-PSMA- and ¹⁸F-DCFPyL-PSMA PET/CT.
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND: PSMA PET/CT using 18F‑DCFPyL and 68Ga‑labelled tracers is central to prostate cancer staging, but 68Ga‑PSMA may show reduced sensitivity and quantitative accuracy, partly due to respiratory motion and lower spatial resolution. Device-based motion‑correction methods have limitations. Data‑driven gating (DDG) offers a hardware‑free alternative, though its impact on PSMA PET, especially 68Ga‑PSMA has not been systematically evaluated. To evaluate the quantitative and qualitative performance of the DDG motion-correction method in 68Ga-PSMA and 18F-DCFPyL-PSMA PET/CT, focusing on metastatic lymph node, lung, and bone lesions, and to assess its robustness across tracers. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with biopsy‑proven prostate cancer who underwent 68Ga‑PSMA or 18F‑DCFPyL PSMA PET/CT for primary staging or biochemical recurrence and had metastatic disease. Motion correction was applied using the OncoFreeze AI™ data‑driven gating (OFAI‑DDG) method. Metastatic lesions were segmented semi‑automatically, and SUV metrics, image noise, and contrast‑to‑noise ratio were quantified by anatomical site in both OFAI-DDG and static images. Qualitative image quality was independently scored by two experienced readers. Statistical analyses included non‑parametric tests, Bland-Altman agreement, regression analyses, tracer comparison, and inter‑reader reliability assessment. RESULTS: After exclusions, 23 68Ga‑PSMA and 40 18F‑PSMA patients were analyzed, yielding 133 and 192 metastatic lesions, respectively. OFAI‑DDG reconstruction significantly increased SUVmean and SUVmax compared with static imaging for both tracers across bone, lymph node, and lung lesions (p < 0.0001), with the largest gains in lung lesions. CNR improved for most lesion types, and image noise was significantly reduced. Qualitative analysis showed better image quality, sharpness, and noise with OFAI‑DDG, with high inter‑reader agreement. OFAI‑DDG performance was robust across tracers and largely independent of lesion location. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that OFAI‑DDG significantly improves PSMA PET/CT image quality and quantitative accuracy compared with standard static imaging. The improvements were observed for both 68Ga‑PSMA and 18F‑PSMA tracers, indicating tracer‑independent robustness. The OFAI‑DDG simplified the workflow and reduced time used for patient set-up, while enhancing lesion visualization and quantitative reliability without altering lesion detection, supporting its clinical value for metastatic prostate cancer imaging.

tag.summary: Effect of data-driven gating on quantifying prostate cancer metastases. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Three-dimensional multimodal fractal dynamics integrating spatial metabolism, cytoarchitecture, and perfusion for preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in colorectal liver metastases.
paper.mesh: Humans; Colorectal Neoplasms; Liver Neoplasms; Fractals; Female; Male; Middle Aged; Microvessels; Neoplasm Invasiveness; Aged; Imaging, Three-Dimensional; Preoperative Care; Perfusion; Multimodal Imaging; Preoperative Period; Prognosis
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurately predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) preoperatively remains a core challenge for precision surgical decision-making in patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). This study developed and validated a three-dimensional multimodal fractal dynamic model (FRAC-3D) that integrates spatial metabolism, cytoarchitecture, and blood perfusion, aiming to non-invasively identify MVI status preoperatively and evaluate patient prognosis. METHODS: Utilizing a retrospective nested cohort design, stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW) was applied to the derivation cohort (n = 100) for baseline debiasing. A core cohort of 145 patients with complete PET/CT, CE-MRI, and DWI imaging was ultimately included. Spatial metabolic fractal dimension (FD_PET), architectural fractal dimension (FD_ADC), and perfusion fractal acceleration (Afd_MRI) were extracted to construct the FRAC-3D model. The model's discrimination, calibration, and clinical benefit were validated in an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 45). RESULTS: Multivariable analysis confirmed that FD_ADC is the strongest independent predictor of MVI (OR = 3.85, 95% CI: 2.45-6.04, P < 0.001). The FRAC-3D model achieved an AUC of 0.938 and a negative predictive value of 96.2% in the validation cohort. Compared with the dual-modal model, FRAC-3D significantly improved risk restratification (continuous NRI = 0.425, P < 0.001). A "highly chaotic" imaging phenotype, identified based on fractal feature clustering, demonstrated an MVI incidence as high as 96.7% and a median recurrence-free survival (RFS) of only 5.2 months.
