CONCLUSION: Through the cross-validation of multidimensional biophysical features, the FRAC-3D model enables high-precision preoperative prediction of MVI status. This study advances the perioperative assessment of CRLM from traditional 'static anatomical metrics' into a novel dimension of 'microenvironmental dynamic evolution', providing a robust, physics-driven tool for individualized surgical margin planning and the precise stratification of targeted neoadjuvant therapy.

tag.summary: Multimodal fractal dynamics used to predict microvascular invasion in liver metastases. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography with Computed Tomography in Pediatric Non-oncological Conditions: A Comprehensive Review.
paper.abstract: This article examines the expanding role of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography with computed tomography (PET/CT) in pediatric non-oncological conditions, moving beyond its established oncologic use. It outlines radiation dosimetry principles unique to children-emphasizing the As Low as Reasonably Achievable principle, reduced tracer activity, and low-dose CT protocols-given their heightened radiosensitivity. In pediatric neurology, FDG PET/CT aids evaluation of drug-refractory epilepsy (temporal and extratemporal foci) and neuronal migration/proliferation anomalies like focal cortical dysplasia (FCD), polymicrogyria, and hemimegalencephaly.

tag.summary: Review of fluorodeoxyglucose imaging in paediatric non-oncological conditions. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Tumor volume may be a better indicator than diameter for occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinical stage-1 lung cancer.
paper.abstract: Occult lymph node metastasis (OLM) remains a major clinical challenge in patients with lung cancer despite comprehensive preoperative staging efforts. Although several predictors of OLM, including tumor diameter, metabolic activity, molecular characteristics, and radiomics, have been extensively investigated, the predictive role of tumor volume remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate whether tumor volume, quantified semi-automatically using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted Synapse 3D software, could predict OLM in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer. Patients who underwent surgical resection for clinically staged cT1b-cN0M0 lung cancer between 2018 and 2024 were included. Tumor volume was quantified using Synapse 3D software. Associations between tumor volume and OLM were assessed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Because tumor diameter and tumor volume may introduce multicollinearity in multivariable models, separate receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and the corresponding areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. A total of 248 patients were included, of whom 59 (23.8%) were female. The mean age was 65.4 years. OLM were identified in 10.8%, 4.8%, and 2.0% of patients at the N1, N2a, and N2b nodal stations, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified younger age (p = 0.004), greater tumor volume (p = 0.01), and histopathological subtypes other than adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma as independent predictors of OLM. Tumor diameter, extent of resection, surgical approach, and PET-CT metabolic activity were not significantly associated with OLM. ROC analysis demonstrated that tumor volume had significantly greater discriminatory ability for predicting OLM than tumor diameter (AUC: 69% vs. 58%; DeLong test, p = 0.004). AI-assisted tumor volumetry is an independent predictor of occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer.

tag.summary: Tumour volume compared with diameter for predicting occult nodal metastasis in lung cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: A Case of Advanced Basal Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck: Diagnostic Challenges and Sequential Systemic Therapy.
paper.abstract: Advanced cutaneous malignancies with basaloid morphology can present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when pathological interpretations differ and disease progresses during systemic treatment. We describe the clinical course of a 53-year-old woman with an extensive, unresectable cutaneous tumor involving the posterior neck and occipital region, accompanied by bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy and additional clinically suspected cutaneous deposits. The initial diagnosis was trichoblastic carcinoma, whereas expert pathological review favored basal cell carcinoma. The extent of disease precluded surgery and definitive radiotherapy. First-line vismodegib was initiated, and palliative radiotherapy delivering 30 Gy in 10 fractions to the occipital lesions and bilateral cervical lymph nodes was completed one year later. Clinical progression was documented three months after completion of radiotherapy; one month after this, MRI demonstrated extensive infiltration involving the left parotid gland and adjacent pharyngeal spaces. Second-line cisplatin and 5-fluorouracil were subsequently administered. Follow-up MRI six months after the earlier MRI demonstrated substantial tumor volume reduction. PET/CT three months later showed a heterogeneous response compared with a year earlier, including regression at several previously involved sites and newly apparent metabolically active right axillary lymph nodes. A subsequent biopsy was reported as basaloid carcinoma. The patient later experienced clinical deterioration, received one cycle of cemiplimab, and died before further treatment or response assessment. This case illustrates the importance of pathological clarification, longitudinal imaging, and careful interpretation of treatment response during sequential systemic therapy for advanced basal cell carcinoma.

tag.summary: Case report of advanced basal cell carcinoma of the head and neck. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Whole-body MRI for the evaluation of metastatic lobular breast cancer; current uses and future directions.
paper.abstract: Invasive lobular cancer (ILC) metastases are harder to detect radiologically than invasive breast cancer of no specific type due to a unique tumor biology. Metastatic ILC (mILC) spread is also unusual and challenging, favoring sites such as the peritoneum. The sclerotic bone metastases commonly seen with mILC are non-measurable on CT by currently accepted response criteria (RECIST 1.1.) and are frequently fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET-CT non-avid. UK/European guidelines recommend CT +/- bone scan or PET-CT for staging and assessment of treatment response in breast cancer however there is increasing evidence that Whole-body MRI (WBMRI) with its anatomical and functional capabilities (offered by diffusion-weighted imaging) can overcome conventional imaging challenges for breast cancer, especially for ILC subtypes. WBMRI is more accurate at identifying additional sites of disease in mILC and the earlier detection of progressive disease resulting in treatment changes. WBMRI advancements are creating fast, well-tolerated studies, and the use of novel artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques may increasingly help with acquisition and reporting speed. There are WBMRI consensus guidelines for several tumor types, but no published guidelines yet exist for breast. This review article presents the current evidence to support the use of WBMRI in the management of mILC illustrated by cases from clinical practice and discusses the challenges of widespread adoption and potential future applications.

tag.summary: Review of whole-body magnetic resonance imaging in metastatic lobular breast cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Lithium Amide: A Catalyst for Depolymerization.
paper.abstract: The widespread use of plastic materials leads to significant contamination of ecosystems, posing risks to both wildlife and human health. There is an urgent need for efficient, economical, and environmentally friendly catalysts to depolymerize plastic waste into value-added compounds. In this study, we utilized the easily accessible catalyst [Li{N(SiMe3}2]2.2(THF) and pinacolborane (HBpin) as a hydride donor to convert various types of plastic waste, biodegradable/non-biodegradable polyesters, and polycarbonates into respective borylated value-added alcohols under mild conditions without any pre-treatment, up to 99% yield. The borylated 1,4-benzenediol obtained from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization is characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction studies, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and routine spectroscopic techniques. Additionally, the catalyst has been employed for the depolymerization of mixed/contaminated waste plastics, achieving selective and excellent yields of the borylated alcohols. This catalyst facilitated the gram-scale depolymerization of PET into eco-friendly alcohols, such as 1,4-benzene-di-methanol and ethylene glycol, via the depolymerization of PET waste bottles. Furthermore, mechanistic studies supported by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations provide insights into the catalytic pathway. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of alkali metal-catalyzed depolymerization of esters and carbonates containing waste polymers via a homogeneous method.

tag.summary: Lithium amide demonstrated as a catalyst for plastic depolymerisation; a chemistry paper.

paper.title: Augmenting Deep Learning-Based PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation With a Population-Level Spatial Atlas.
paper.abstract: Automated lesion segmentation is increasingly central to PSMA PET/CT interpretation, supporting staging, treatment planning, and response assessment at a scale that outpaces available nuclear-medicine expertise. However, automated PSMA-PET/CT whole-body lesion segmentation models are trained on images alone, with no knowledge of where in the body prostate metastases actually tend to occur. Radiologists use clinical domain knowledge of metastatic spread, but its absence in machine learning models produces false positives in anatomically implausible locations and missed lesions in high-risk sites such as the liver. In this work, we explore whether population-level spatial knowledge of metastatic spread can be used to augment deep learning segmentation predictions, and how such a prior should be fused with a network's output, without additional training. We build a data-driven metastasis atlas from 375 expert-annotated whole-body PSMA PET/CT scans and investigate its fusion with a trained segmentation network under a Bayesian framework, in which prediction probabilities from an nnU-Net-based lesion segmentation model serve as the likelihood and the data-driven atlas as the prior. Because metastases occupy only a small fraction of whole-body voxels, the atlas's peak probability is too low, and standard power-scaled or naive Bayesian pooling references lack the tools to deal with this shortcoming. This causes these standard fusion strategies to fail and, in the naive Bayesian case, to sharply degrade performance. We instead derive a calibrated, background-referenced log-odds fusion, one of many possible approaches to combine a population atlas with a deep learning model's predictions, distinct from classical multi-atlas label fusion in that it fuses a single population prior with a trained network's softmax rather than combining several registered atlases. Furthermore, this approach is neutral outside atlas support by construction, reduces exactly to the baseline network when unweighted, and requires no retraining. This atlas fusion significantly improved mean Dice over the baseline nnU-Net on a disjoint internal test set (+0.011, Holm-adjusted p = 0.021) and on an independent external cohort (+0.0129, Holm-adjusted p = 3.8×10 - 16 ), with lesion sensitivity improving from 0.849 to 0.861 internally and Dice improving over baseline in every stratified anatomic region, including the rare, high-risk sites motivating this work, while naive Bayesian pooling degrades performance sharply and power-scaled pooling underperforms it throughout. Our findings suggest that population-level spatial priors can meaningfully augment deep learning predictions in whole-body oncologic segmentation, provided the fusion rule is calibrated to where the prior actually carries signal.

tag.summary: Deep learning metastasis segmentation augmented with a population-level spatial atlas. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: From task-specific AI to multimodal foundation models in PET/CT: a readiness framework for clinical translation.
paper.abstract: Artificial intelligence in PET/CT is evolving from narrowly optimized systems toward reusable pretrained representations and multimodal models. PET/CT is a demanding test case because clinically meaningful interpretation must preserve quantitative molecular information while integrating anatomic CT, acquisition metadata, longitudinal examinations, and free-text imaging reports. This focused narrative review synthesizes literature reported from January 2021 through July 2026, spanning PET reconstruction and enhancement, attenuation correction, segmentation, outcome modeling, pretrained representations, vision-language systems, and agentic workflows. We distinguish task-specific models, reusable pretrained representations, promptable models, vision-language systems, generalist foundation-model candidates, and agentic systems according to demonstrated capabilities, while separately considering evaluation benchmarks. Task-specific deep learning has demonstrated promising technical performance in low-count imaging and whole-body tumor analysis, but most evidence remains retrospective and restricted by radiotracer, disease, scanner, institution, or endpoint. Emerging PET-native studies demonstrate label-efficient segmentation, image-text grounding, report generation, and modular tool orchestration; however, they do not yet establish broad cross-tracer generalization or prospective clinical benefit. We therefore propose MOSAIC-PET, an author-developed heuristic six-domain evaluation framework for PET/CT foundation models encompassing Molecular fidelity, Organ and anatomic grounding, Semantic faithfulness, Adaptability, Integration and clinical impact, and Continuous governance. MOSAIC-PET has not undergone Delphi consensus or formal validation and is intended to organize PET-specific evidence requirements rather than function as a validated clinical-readiness tool. The near-term translational priority is the development of modular, auditable systems in which validated quantitative tools and evidence-linked language outputs remain under specialist oversight, with progression from external testing to silent evaluation, assisted-use studies, clinical-impact assessment, and continuous lifecycle monitoring.

tag.summary: Readiness framework proposed for multimodal foundation models in clinical imaging. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Cancer of Unknown Primary Presenting as Isolated FDG-Avid Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis: Diagnostic Escalation after a Non-Diagnostic Core Biopsy - A Case Report.
paper.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cancer of unknown primary (CUP) remains a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge, particularly when presenting as isolated cervical lymph node disease. Adequate tissue sampling is crucial, and escalation to excisional biopsy may be necessary when minimally invasive procedures are inconclusive. CASE PRESENTATION: A 62-year-old man with a history of long-term tobacco use presented with a right-sided neck mass. Otolaryngologic examination and fiberoscopy revealed no mucosal abnormalities. Fine-needle aspiration suggested metastatic poorly differentiated carcinoma, while core needle biopsy yielded scant, nondiagnostic material. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated pathological right cervical lymph nodes (level III 29 × 29 mm, level IIa 20 × 15 mm). 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography showed an FDG-avid right cervical nodal package at the level IIB/III border (SUVmax 21.1) and an incidental focal uptake in the left thyroid lobe (SUVmax 4.4), with no other suspicious lesions. Thyroid ultrasound revealed a small, well-demarcated hypoechoic lesion (3.5 × 2.6 × 4.5 mm); repeated ultrasound-guided FNAC was benign (Bethesda II), and calcitonin was within the reference range. The patient underwent excisional lymph node biopsy and comprehensive endoscopic evaluation under general anesthesia (panendoscopy with bilateral tonsillectomy and directed biopsies), without identification of a primary tumor. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed nodal metastasis of undifferentiated carcinoma, most consistent with carcinoma with sarcomatoid features, confined within the lymph node capsule. Because no primary site was identified after imaging, endoscopic evaluation, thyroid workup, and histopathological assessment of the lymph node, the diagnosis remained CUP. The patient was subsequently referred for radiotherapy. CONCLUSION: In cervical lymph node metastasis from CUP, adequate tissue sampling remains essential for definitive diagnosis. When fine-needle aspiration suggests malignancy but core needle biopsy is nondiagnostic, early excisional biopsy should be considered to enable reliable histopathological and immunohistochemical classification. PET/CT may guide the diagnostic pathway and identify incidental findings requiring verification, but imaging should not delay escalation to representative tissue sampling.

tag.summary: Case report of cancer of unknown primary presenting as a cervical node metastasis. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Challenges in Managing Synchronous Advanced Prostate and Pancreatic Cancers: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Prostate cancer (PCa) and pancreatic cancer (PC) are distinct malignancies with diverging epidemiological and prognostic profiles. PCa often mimics benign prostatic hyperplasia, while PC remains asymptomatic until advanced stages, complicating early detection. As cancer survivorship and screening improve, the incidence of synchronous multiple primary malignancies (MPMs) is rising, with emerging data suggesting a potential biological link between PCa and PC. Managing such cases requires a delicate balance of treatment sequencing and toxicity management. Reporting these rare encounters is vital for refining clinical strategies in complex oncologic presentations. CASE PRESENTATION: This report details the clinical course of a 76-year-old male diagnosed synchronously with high-grade ductal PCa and pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Staging via PSMA PET-CT incidentally identified a pancreatic tail mass with an unusually high SUVmax of 5.2. Despite initiating standard androgen deprivation therapy, the aggressive ductal variant exhibited a "PSA escape" following treatment interruption. As the pancreatic lesion progressed metastatically, the patient's refusal of conventional chemotherapy and a lack of genomic profiling prompted a salvage, "last-resort" combination of pembrolizumab and olaparib. While this strategy achieved temporary biochemical stabilization and slowed tumor growth, the patient eventually succumbed to metabolic dysregulation and multi-organ failure. CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of MPM management, specifically rare PSMA-avidity in primary pancreatic tumors which can mimic metastatic spread. While empirical immunotherapy and PARP inhibitor combinations may offer temporary clinical benefit in resource-limited settings, they cannot substitute for biomarker-guided precision medicine. Success depends on strict therapeutic adherence and early multidisciplinary coordination.

tag.summary: Case report of synchronous advanced prostate and pancreatic cancers. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Radiologic Progression of Disease during Neoadjuvant Dostarlimab in Mismatch Repair-Deficient Lynch-Associated Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer Resulting in Pathologic Complete Response: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade has demonstrated unprecedented activity in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), with high rates of clinical complete response and increasing adoption of organ-preservation strategies. However, response assessment during immunotherapy remains challenging as immune-mediated tumor regression may generate radiologic patterns that mimic persistent or progressive disease. CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 40-year-old woman with Lynch-associated dMMR mucinous LARC (cT4N+) treated with nine cycles of neoadjuvant dostarlimab. Early treatment was associated with rapid normalization of carcinoembryonic antigen and nodal regression. Nevertheless, magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated persistent bulky mass with new diffusion-restricted areas, and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography revealed intense metabolic uptake (SUVmax 14.7). A rising carbohydrate antigen 19-9 level further raised concern for residual viable tumor. Surgical exploration confirmed a large, firm pelvic mass with apparent infiltration of adjacent structures, leading to posterior pelvic exenteration. Unexpectedly, final pathologic examination revealed complete pathological response (ypT0 ypN0), with extensive fibrosis and acellular mucin pools and no viable tumor cells in 61 examined sections. CONCLUSION: Radiologic and metabolic findings suggestive of progression during neoadjuvant immunotherapy in dMMR LARC may not necessarily reflect treatment failure. This case underscores the limitations of conventional imaging in the context of immune-mediated tumor regression and highlights the importance of multidisciplinary evaluation when surgical decisions carry major oncologic and quality-of-life implications.

tag.summary: Case report of radiologic progression during neoadjuvant immunotherapy for rectal cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Primary Glomus Tumor of the Inferior Vena Cava Diagnosed by Endovascular Biopsy: A Rare Incidental Finding.
paper.abstract: Glomus tumors are uncommon mesenchymal neoplasms with modified smooth muscle differentiation that classically arise in the subungual region but may occur at extradigital, visceral, and intravascular sites. Although primary intravascular glomus tumors have been reported, apparent primary origin within the inferior vena cava (IVC) represents an unusual presentation and must be distinguished from secondary caval involvement by an extravascular tumor. A 44-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis underwent musculoskeletal imaging for persistent right shoulder and upper back pain following a fall. Imaging incidentally demonstrated a 1.7-cm infrarenal IVC intraluminal abnormality initially interpreted as bland thrombus, while PET-CT showed no 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-avid malignancy. Endovascular evaluation demonstrated an obstructive intraluminal mass, and biopsy revealed uniform round-to-oval cells arranged around branching vascular channels. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong diffuse smooth muscle myosin heavy chain positivity with negative CAM 5.2 and chromogranin staining, supporting the diagnosis of glomus tumor. Subsequent surgical resection confirmed a 2.5-cm glomus tumor with smooth muscle actin (SMA) and caldesmon positivity and a low Ki-67 proliferative index (<1%). This case demonstrates the diagnostic challenge of an indeterminate intraluminal IVC lesion and emphasizes the importance of distinguishing apparent primary caval origin from secondary IVC tumor involvement. Endovascular tissue sampling can provide a minimally invasive means of establishing a diagnosis when imaging findings are inconclusive, and the integration of imaging, histomorphology, immunohistochemistry, and surgical pathology is essential for definitive classification.

tag.summary: Case report of a primary glomus tumour of the inferior vena cava. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Widespread Skeletal Fragility and Progressive Spinal Destruction Associated with Prolonged Tropomyosin Receptor Kinase Inhibitor Therapy: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Tropomyosin receptor kinase (TRK) inhibitors have demonstrated remarkable efficacy in patients with NTRK fusion-positive malignancies; however, their long-term effects on skeletal health remain incompletely understood. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 65-year-old woman with an ETV6-NTRK3 fusion-positive gastrointestinal stromal tumor who achieved sustained disease control during prolonged TRK inhibitor therapy. During treatment, she developed progressive skeletal fragility characterized by multiple atraumatic fractures, delayed fracture healing, and progressive lumbar spinal destruction consistent with Charcot-like neuropathic arthropathy. Neurological deterioration, including loss of ambulation, resulted from structural spinal instability rather than direct neurotoxicity. Although initial imaging findings raised suspicion of metastatic disease, serial CT, MRI, and FDG-PET/CT examinations supported a nonmalignant skeletal process in the setting of continued oncologic remission. Following discontinuation of TRK inhibitor therapy, neurological symptoms stabilized and radiographic evidence of fracture healing was observed. CONCLUSION: This case suggests that TRK inhibitor-associated skeletal toxicity may represent an on-target effect related to disruption of neuro-skeletal interactions. Long-term monitoring of bone health may be warranted in patients receiving prolonged TRK inhibitor therapy.

tag.summary: Case report of skeletal fragility during prolonged kinase inhibitor therapy. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: CD10-Positive Extranodal Marginal Zone Lymphoma of the Thyroid Arising in Hashimoto's Thyroiditis: A Rare Diagnostic Challenge.
paper.abstract: Patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) have an increased risk of developing primary thyroid lymphoma (PTL), with extranodal marginal zone lymphoma (ENMZL) representing a significant subset of these cases. We present the case of a 49-year-old woman with a history of HT, Sjögren's syndrome, and systemic lupus erythematosus who was incidentally found to have fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-avid thyroid nodules on PET-CT. Initial and repeat fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsies were either benign or indeterminate; however, flow cytometry revealed a small kappa-restricted B-cell population with dim CD10 expression. Given the persistent diagnostic uncertainty, the patient underwent total thyroidectomy, and histopathologic evaluation confirmed low-grade ENMZL with plasmacytic differentiation. Staging demonstrated localized stage IE disease. This case highlights important diagnostic challenges, including the potential for thyroid ENMZL to be missed on cytology despite ongoing clinical suspicion and the ability of rare aberrant CD10 expression in marginal zone lymphoma to mimic germinal-center-derived lymphomas.

tag.summary: Case report of extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of the thyroid. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Suspected Scrotal Metastasis Detected by 18F-FDG PET/CT in Recurrent Urachal Adenocarcinoma Associated with Subsequent High-Grade Urothelial Carcinoma: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Urachal adenocarcinoma is a rare and aggressive malignancy arising from persistent urachal remnants and accounts for <1% of bladder cancers. Although the lungs, liver, lymph nodes, bone, and peritoneum are recognized sites of metastatic spread, involvement of scrotal structures is exceedingly uncommon. We report a case of recurrent urachal adenocarcinoma with an unusual pattern of metastatic dissemination identified on 18F-FDG PET/CT. CASE PRESENTATION: A 59-year-old man underwent partial cystectomy with en bloc urachal resection and bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection for a moderately differentiated urachal adenocarcinoma arising from a persistent urachal remnant. Histopathology demonstrated a 6-cm tumor with perivesical extension and perineural invasion, while surgical margins and lymph nodes were negative. Approximately 6 months later, local recurrence was detected, and transurethral resection revealed high-grade urothelial carcinoma with supportive immunohistochemical findings. Restaging 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated a hypermetabolic recurrent bladder mass accompanied by pulmonary nodules suspicious for metastatic involvement, multiple intraperitoneal metastatic deposits, and an FDG-avid lesion within the right hemiscrotum highly suspicious for metastatic involvement. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the aggressive behavior and heterogeneous clinical course of urachal malignancies. In addition to confirming local recurrence, 18F-FDG PET/CT identified a lesion within the right hemiscrotum that was highly suspicious for metastatic involvement. Recognition of atypical metastatic patterns may improve disease staging and influence clinical management in patients with recurrent urachal carcinoma.

tag.summary: Case report of suspected scrotal metastasis in urachal adenocarcinoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: SDHB-Related Carney-Stratakis Syndrome Presenting with a Gastric Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor and a Clinically Suspected Paraganglioma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
paper.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Carney-Stratakis syndrome (CSS) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary tumor-predisposition syndrome characterized by succinate dehydrogenase (SDH)-deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) and paragangliomas. These tumors typically arise in younger patients, may occur synchronously or metachronously, and often show limited sensitivity to conventional tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Given the potential for multifocal disease, recurrence, and familial involvement, accurate clinicopathological assessment, genetic evaluation, and long-term surveillance are essential. CASE PRESENTATION: A 36-year-old woman presented with a 7-month history of visual disturbance. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a hypervascular tumor extending from the left jugular foramen to the carotid sheath, raising clinical suspicion of a paraganglioma and prompting biochemical and functional imaging evaluation. Plasma noradrenaline and dopamine levels were elevated, whereas 123I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scintigraphy showed no abnormal uptake. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography incidentally identified a gastric submucosal tumor. Because placement of a lumboperitoneal shunt for intracranial hypertension was expected to increase the risk of infection and complicate subsequent abdominal surgery, gastric resection was prioritized. Laparoscopic-endoscopic cooperative surgery (LECS) was selected to facilitate local resection of the tumor near the esophagogastric junction while preserving the cardia; an intraoperative perforation necessitated conversion to classical LECS, and complete macroscopic resection was achieved. Histopathological examination demonstrated a multinodular epithelioid GIST positive for KIT and DOG1, with loss of SDHB expression, indicating an SDH-deficient GIST. Germline testing identified a pathogenic SDHB variant, supporting the diagnosis of CSS in the context of the clinically suspected paraganglioma. The jugular foramen lesion, for which no histological diagnosis was obtained, was managed conservatively, and delayed shunt placement improved the visual symptoms. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of considering an SDH-related hereditary syndrome in a young patient with an SDH-deficient gastric GIST and a synchronous lesion clinically suggestive of paraganglioma. It also illustrates the value of genetic evaluation, explicit recognition of diagnostic uncertainty, and multidisciplinary treatment sequencing.

tag.summary: Case report of a hereditary tumour predisposition syndrome with a stromal tumour. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Synthesis and Preliminary Biological Evaluation of a Structurally Modified Niraparib-Based PARP-Targeted PET Tracer for Tumor Imaging.
paper.abstract: Poly-(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) is highly expressed in various malignancies and represents an important therapeutic target. Noninvasive evaluation of PARP expression is therefore of potential clinical significance for patient stratification. In this study, we developed and evaluated [68Ga]-Ga-DOTA-MK-4827, a structurally modified PARP-targeted radiotracer derived from niraparib, featuring a two-carbon linker between the DOTA chelator and the pharmacophore. [68Ga]-Ga-DOTA-MK-4827 demonstrated high uptake in MDA-MB-231 and OE-19 tumors with elevated PARP-1 expression, which was significantly reduced by blocking, supporting a PARP-related component of tumor accumulation. The tracer exhibited favorable pharmacokinetics, including high hydrophilicity and predominantly renal clearance, resulting in low abdominal background activity. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging enabled clear tumor visualization with good contrast, supported by biodistribution findings. Preliminary clinical imaging further showed notable uptake in an esophageal cancer lesion, with immunohistochemical confirmation of PARP-1 expression in the biopsied tissue. These results suggest that [68Ga]-Ga-DOTA-MK-4827 has potential as a PARP-targeted PET tracer for tumor imaging and merits further investigation in larger clinical cohorts.

tag.summary: A modified PARP-targeted tracer synthesised and evaluated for tumour imaging. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Analytical Approaches for Detection, Characterization, and Environmental Significance of Suspended Particulate Matter in Aquatic Systems: A Scoping Review.
paper.abstract: Suspended particulate matter (SPM) represents a component of aquatic systems, acting both as a carrier of contaminants and as a factor shaping ecosystem functioning. This review summarizes recent progress in methods for detecting and quantifying SPM in natural waters. Traditional gravimetric analysis provides a direct mass-based reference, while optical approaches such as turbidimetry and nephelometry enable rapid and automated assessments. Granulometric techniques, including sedimentation and laser diffraction, contribute to understanding particle size distribution and its role in transport, settling, and pollutant interactions. Chemical characterization, based on spectroscopic and spectrometric methods, identifies the composition of SPM and its association with heavy metals, organic pollutants, and microplastics. Particular attention is given to the ecological risks posed by fine particles, which remain suspended longer and enhance contaminant mobility. The review integrates findings from hydrochemistry, analytical chemistry, and environmental monitoring, outlining both the strengths and limitations of existing methods and highlighting directions for improving water-quality assessment and ecological risk evaluation.

tag.summary: Scoping review of analytical approaches to suspended particulate matter in aquatic systems; a methods review.

paper.title: Atypical Type A Thymoma Identified in Slowly Growing Pulmonary Metastases from Type A Thymoma: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Type A thymoma is generally considered a low-risk thymoma subtype with an excellent prognosis and low rates of distant metastasis. Atypical type A thymoma is a recently established entity characterized by more aggressive biological behavior despite retaining the morphology of conventional type A thymoma. Patients with primary conventional type A thymoma who subsequently develop recurrence with atypical histological features are extremely rare. CASE PRESENTATION: A 79-year-old man was referred to our hospital due to gradual enlargement of bilateral pulmonary nodules. Seven years earlier, he had undergone complete resection of an anterior mediastinal tumor, which had been diagnosed as conventional type A thymoma. Retrospective review of preoperative computed tomography images revealed that small pulmonary nodules had already been present at the time of the initial surgery but had yet to be identified. The nodules enlarged slowly from 3 mm to 10 mm and from 3 mm to 7 mm over the 7-year period. Positron emission tomography showed no abnormal fluorodeoxyglucose uptake. After thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left lower lobe lesion, histopathological examination demonstrated pulmonary metastasis of type A thymoma with focal hypercellularity and increased mitotic activity, consistent with atypical type A thymoma. No necrosis was identified. The Ki-67 labeling indices of the primary and metastatic lesions were 7% and 20%, respectively. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that even apparently low-risk type A thymoma may exhibit indolent but metastatic behavior and may develop atypical histological features during a prolonged clinical course. Careful long-term surveillance and detailed pathological evaluation, including assessment of the Ki-67 labeling index, may be important in patients with type A thymoma.

tag.summary: Case report of atypical thymoma with slowly growing pulmonary metastases. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: A scientometric study on research trends and characteristics of lymph node metastasis in oral cancer.
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: Cervical lymph node metastasis (LNM) is the most critical prognostic factor in oral cancer (OC) patients. The purpose of this study was to analyze the scientometric characteristics and research trends of LNM in OC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: All the papers on LNM in OC were comprehensively retrieved from the Scopus database. The years of publication were divided into before 2016 and after 2016 in the analysis of research trends. RESULTS: There were 946 papers on LNM in OC, with total citations of 21,154 and the h index of 70. The trend of clinical aspect including lymph node excision, lymphadenectomy, and sentinel lymph node biopsy has changed to early cancer, extranodal extension, chemoradiotherapy, and distant metastasis after 2016. The trend of diagnostic aspect has highlighted depth of invasion, perineural invasion, deep learning, machine learning, nomogram, and diagnostic imaging by PET-CT, contrast enhancement, and radiomics. Moreover, the trend of laboratory investigation including immunoenzyme techniques, neoplasm proteins, and VEGF-C has changed to tumor microenvironment, tumor differentiation, and signal transduction after 2016. There have always been common keywords such as neck dissection, tongue tumor, metabolism, genetics, risk factor, tumor marker, cancer surgery, cisplatin, and cancer radiotherapy. CONCLUSION: This scientometric study for the first time elucidated the current scenario and research trends of LNM in OC, particularly the comprehensive identification and recognition of the important research topics concerned.

tag.summary: Scientometric study of research on lymph node metastasis in oral cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Isolated Thyroid Metastasis from High-Grade Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma After Radical Nephrectomy: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Thyroid metastasis from clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is uncommon and may occur after radical nephrectomy despite no evidence of residual or metastatic disease at that time. Diagnosis can be challenging because imaging and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) may mimic benign or primary thyroid lesions. Case Presentation: A 55-year-old man underwent left radical nephrectomy for WHO/ISUP grade 3 ccRCC with focal grade 4 differentiation. Two years later, surveillance ultrasonography detected a suspicious lesion involving the thyroid isthmus and left lobe. FNA was interpreted as Bethesda II (benign), but metastatic ccRCC was subsequently confirmed after total thyroidectomy. Histopathology showed focal vascular and capsular invasion. Tumor reached the margin of the main thyroid specimen, whereas separately submitted perithyroidal soft tissue had tumor-free margins, resulting in a final R0 resection. The tumor was positive for CK8/18, PAX8, EMA, vimentin, and CD10 and negative for TTF-1, thyroglobulin, calcitonin, and CD5. Postoperative 18F-FDG PET/CT showed no additional metastatic disease. Conclusions: Benign thyroid cytology should be interpreted cautiously in patients with previous ccRCC when clinical or imaging findings remain suspicious. Diagnosis requires integration of oncological history, imaging, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry. Surgical resection may provide local disease control in selected patients, with surveillance.

tag.summary: Case report of isolated thyroid metastasis from renal cell carcinoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Multiparametric imaging with dynamic 18 F-FDG PET shows increased breast glucose metabolism in patients with breast cancer.
paper.abstract: PURPOSE: Multiparametric PET separates tracer signal into bound and free fractions via reconstructions that reflect the net trapping rate (Ki) and apparent distribution volume (DV). This study aimed to investigate differences in background parenchymal uptake (BPU) between patients with and without breast cancer using multiparametric PET and to evaluate differences in primary tumor uptake according to hormone receptor status. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included female patients (n = 48) with newly diagnosed breast cancer and 146 patients without breast cancer. Patients with breast cancer under or after treatment and patients with bilateral breast cancer were excluded. Enrolled patients underwent whole-body dynamic PET and three quantitative indices representing BPU (maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax], Ki and DV) were calculated. The primary tumor uptake was calculated between estrogen- or progesterone-receptor-positive and -negative groups. RESULTS: The mean SUVmax, Ki and DV of breast cancer cases were 1.39 ± 0.352, 4.88 × 10 - 3 ± 1.61 × 10 - 3 and 24.2 ± 15.4 respectively, whereas in control cases, mean SUVmax, Ki and DV were 1.10 ± 0.320, 3.96 × 10 - 3 ± 1.25 × 10 - 3 and 17.1 ± 10.8 respectively (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.004). The areas under the curve from the ROC analysis for breast cancer presence were calculated as 0.727, 0.681 and 0.653 respectively. In addition, age-stratified analysis showed that SUVmax and Ki were significantly higher in patients with breast cancer than in patients without breast cancer. Regarding the primary tumor uptake, Ki was significantly higher in the estrogen receptor-positive group. CONCLUSION: Multiparametric PET revealed that pure glucose metabolism is significantly elevated in the background mammary glands of patients with breast cancer, and the Ki in the primary tumor is associated with ER status. Dynamic PET imaging may be a useful imaging biomarker for the development of breast cancer.

tag.summary: Multiparametric imaging showing raised breast glucose metabolism in breast cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Coupled sediment and microplastic fluxes revealed by check-dam sediment records.
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as pervasive contaminants in terrestrial environments, yet their redistribution through erosion and accumulation within sediment-retention structures remains poorly quantified. This study quantified MPs in sediments retained behind check dams and examined their relationships with sediment storage and erosion-related sediment yield at the catchment scale. Twenty check dams in a semi-arid mountainous catchment in northeastern Iran were investigated. Sediment storage ranged from 531 to 9828 Mg (mean: 2683 Mg), while specific sediment yield ranged from 16.2 to 855.4 Mg km-2 yr-1 (mean: 247.1 Mg km-2 yr-1). MPs were detected in all sediment samples, with concentrations ranging from 800 to 5240 particles kg-1 dry sediment (mean: 2702 particles kg-1). Estimated MP inventories ranged from 9.0 × 108 to 2.4 × 1010 particles per check dam. Strong positive relationships were observed between specific sediment yield and estimated MP yield (r = 0.99, p < 0.01) and between accumulated sediment mass and estimated MP inventory (r = 0.80, p < 0.01), indicating a close association between sediment dynamics and MP redistribution. Fibrous MPs dominated the assemblage (86.6%), and the 500-1000 μm size class accounted for the largest proportion of detected particles (44.7%). Raman spectroscopy confirmed several polymer types within the analyzed subset. Overall, the findings show substantial accumulation of sediment-associated MPs behind check dams and indicate that erosion-driven sediment mobilization may represent an important pathway for MP redistribution in erosion-prone catchments. However, the persistence of this retention may depend on the stability of accumulated sediments, which can potentially be remobilized during high-energy hydrological events.

tag.summary: Coupled sediment and microplastic fluxes reconstructed from check-dam records; an environmental fate study.

paper.title: Radiopharmaceuticals for Melanoma Theranostics.
paper.mesh: Humans; Melanoma; Radiopharmaceuticals; Theranostic Nanomedicine; Animals; Receptor, Melanocortin, Type 1
paper.abstract: Malignant melanoma (MM) remains a formidable clinical challenge due to its high metastatic potential and the eventual emergence of resistance to current BRAF/MEK and immune checkpoint inhibitors. To address these limitations, the theranostic strategy integrating diagnostic imaging with targeted radionuclide therapy to enable personalized treatment has gained significant traction. Current research primarily exploits the overexpression of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R), very late antigen-4 (VLA-4), and melanin as primary molecular targets for radiopharmaceutical development. For MC1R, α-MSH peptide analogs have been engineered with β-emitters such as 177Lu and 90Y for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT), as well as α-emitters like 225Ac and 212Pb (β- decay to 212Bi and then emit α particles) for targeted alpha therapy (TAT), showing high specificity and rapid clearance. Concurrently, VLA-4-targeted platforms utilizing high-affinity LLP2A ligands have been optimized through PEGylation and albumin-binding strategies to enhance bioavailability and tumor retention. Beyond these primary receptors, this review evaluates alternative strategies, including copper transporter (CTR1) targeting with 64CuCl2 and the use of gold nanocages for multimodal applications. Together, these advancements represent a critical shift toward image-guided, dosimetry-driven radionuclide therapies that may work synergistically with existing immunotherapies to improve survival in metastatic melanoma.

tag.summary: Overview of radiopharmaceuticals for melanoma theranostics. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: PET Imaging of Melanoma Using a Melanocortin 1 Receptor-Targeted Probe.
paper.mesh: Receptor, Melanocortin, Type 1; Animals; Humans; Melanoma; Positron-Emission Tomography; alpha-MSH; Mice; Radiopharmaceuticals; Cell Line, Tumor; Gallium Radioisotopes; Tomography, Emission-Computed, Single-Photon
paper.abstract: The melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) is overexpressed in more than 80% of melanoma cells but is expressed at low levels in normal tissues, making it an important target for melanoma imaging and therapy. Recently, MC1R has attracted the interest of numerous researchers as a target for melanoma. Radiolabeled alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) peptides bind specifically to MC1R and internalize into tumor cells, enabling melanoma diagnosis and therapy. Several radiolabeled α-MSH peptides have been developed. Among those, a cyclized α-MSH peptide produced via an alternative click chemistry cyclization strategy offers faster and more specific bindings to MC1R. It could be labeled with ²0³Pb/²¹²Pb (VMT01) for melanoma single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging and therapy and also could be labeled with 68Ga (VMT02) for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Preliminary clinical imaging showed highly sensitive and specific melanoma detection. This chapter describes the synthesis of VMT02 and PET/CT imaging procedures in both mouse models and patients.

tag.summary: A melanocortin-1 receptor-targeted probe used for melanoma imaging. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: First Presentation With Impending Cardiac Tamponade Leading to a New Diagnosis of Mediastinal Lymphoma: A Shared Learning Case on the Atypical Presentation of Pericardial Effusion and Cardiac Tamponade.
paper.abstract: Cardiac tamponade is a life-threatening emergency classically associated with Beck's triad of hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and elevated jugular venous pressure; however, incomplete or atypical presentations may delay diagnosis. We report the case of a previously healthy 28-year-old woman who presented with progressive dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, orthopnoea, peripheral oedema, fever, and fatigue. Examination revealed mild tachycardia, soft heart sounds, reduced basal air entry, and ankle oedema, while the patient remained normotensive. Initial investigations demonstrated cardiomegaly with pleural effusions on chest radiograph, low-voltage QRS complexes on electrocardiogram, and markedly raised inflammatory markers. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography identified a large anterior mediastinal mass encasing the great vessels, a significant pericardial effusion with features of cardiac tamponade, and bilateral pleural effusions. Emergency pericardiocentesis resulted in immediate clinical improvement. Histopathological analysis confirmed high-grade B-cell lymphoma, most consistent with primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma. The patient was treated with immunochemotherapy, achieving complete metabolic remission on end-of-treatment PET-CT. This case highlights the importance of recognising atypical presentations of cardiac tamponade and considering mediastinal malignancy in young patients presenting with unexplained cardiorespiratory symptoms.

tag.summary: Case report of cardiac tamponade leading to a diagnosis of mediastinal lymphoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Valorisation of PET-rich mixed plastic waste using a cascading concept involving selective ammonolysis and catalytic pyrolysis.
paper.abstract: We report a cascading valorisation strategy for real polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-rich waste streams, combining selective ammonolysis of PET with catalytic pyrolysis of the non-PET residue. In this approach, PET-rich packaging waste is treated with ammonia in ethylene glycol to produce terephthaldiamide (TDA), while the remaining polyolefin (PO)-rich residue is subsequently upgraded to benzene, toluene, xylene (BTX), and light olefins over H-ZSM-5 catalyst. TDA is a valuable aromatic diamide and a potential precursor to p-phenylene diamine, a monomer used in the production of poly(p-phenyleneterephthalamide) (PPTA). For post-consumer PET trays, ammonolysis at 5 bar NH3, and 100 °C for 8 h, followed by a downstream separation procedure, resulted in an almost quantitative conversion of PET, yielding pure TDA as small crystals in 74 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content in the feed. The residue (mostly polyolefins) was converted to BTX (5 wt% on residue), and propene/butenes (19 wt%, on residue) using a catalytic in situ pyrolysis approach with H-ZSM-5 at 550 °C. The same strategy was applied to a PET-enriched, DKR-350 mixed-plastic packaging fraction, affording TDA in 71 wt% (87 mol%) yield based on the PET content, while catalytic pyrolysis of the residue produced BTX (3 wt%) and propene/isobutene (4 wt%) based on the residue. These results demonstrate that real PET-rich mixed plastic waste streams can be selectively upgraded into valuable aromatic diamide while retaining the non-PET fraction as a feedstock for petrochemical intermediates.

tag.summary: Cascading ammonolysis and pyrolysis applied to PET-rich mixed plastic waste; a recycling paper.

paper.title: Unified alcoholysis-GC-MS/MS for simultaneous differentiation and quantification of polyester microplastics in water.
paper.abstract: Environmental waters now carry complex mixtures of polyester microplastics that vary in origin and biodegradability, including fossil-based and biodegradable polyesters, yet no method can simultaneously distinguish and individually quantify them. We present a unified alcoholysis method coupled with GC-MS/MS to quantify four polyester microplastics (PEMPs) in a single workflow. By selectively cleaving ester bonds in an alcohol medium, the method converts polylactic acid, polyethylene terephthalate, polyhydroxybutyrate and polybutylene succinate into four distinct, stable monomers. These monomers are directly determined by GC-MS/MS without derivatization. Under unified conditions (190 °C, 5 h), depolymerization efficiencies range from 15% to 90%. We calibrate directly between polymer mass and monomer signal intensity. Detection limits are 0.0462 μg/L for polylactic acid (PLA), 0.103 μg/L for polyethylene terephthalate (PET), 2.92 μg/L for polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), and 0.695 μg/L for polybutylene succinate (PBS). Spiked recoveries in lake water are 90-115%. In six lake samples, PLA constitutes over 75% of total PEMPs. This fingerprint points to consumer packaging as the dominant source. By circumventing particle morphology constraints and delivering polymer-specific mass concentrations, the method opens a direct route for source apportionment of coexisting fossil-based and biodegradable polyester microplastics.

tag.summary: An alcoholysis GC-MS method developed to quantify polyester microplastics in water; a method paper.

paper.title: GATA3-positive primary ductal adenocarcinoma of the lacrimal gland with calcification: a case report.
paper.abstract: Primary ductal adenocarcinoma of the lacrimal gland (PDALG) is a rare epithelial malignancy of the ocular adnexa. A man in his 50s presented with painless swelling of the right upper eyelid and was found to have a right lacrimal gland mass with punctate hyperdense foci on computed tomography (CT) and low signal intensity on both T1- and T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging. Histopathology of the tumor revealed nest-like, cribriform, and tubular proliferation of atypical epithelial cells, with fibrotic and hyalinized stroma, comedo necrosis, and calcification. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for androgen receptor, HER2, and GATA3, while GCDFP-15 was negative. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography showed no systemic lesions, supporting the diagnosis of PDALG. Elastica van Gieson staining demonstrated venous invasion, and adjuvant radiotherapy was performed after complete excision. This case illustrates the diagnostic value of correlating punctate hyperdensity on CT with pathologic calcification and integrating GATA3/HER2 findings with the systemic exclusion of metastatic breast carcinoma. At 1 year of follow-up, no local recurrence or distant metastasis had been detected; however, given the potential for late metastasis in this pathology, long-term close observation is required.

tag.summary: Case report of primary ductal adenocarcinoma of the lacrimal gland. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Comparative diagnostic accuracy of PSMA-PET versus conventional imaging for Initial T/N/M staging of intermediate- to high-risk prostate cancer: a patient-level paired bivariate meta-analysis.
paper.mesh: Humans; Male; Prostatic Neoplasms; Neoplasm Staging; Positron-Emission Tomography; Tomography, X-Ray Computed; Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging; Antigens, Surface; Sensitivity and Specificity; Glutamate Carboxypeptidase II; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography
paper.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the patient-level diagnostic accuracy of PSMA-PET with multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), computed tomography (CT), and bone scintigraphy (BS) for initial T, N, and M staging of newly diagnosed intermediate- to high-risk prostate cancer using paired studies. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to December 1, 2025, for paired studies in which the same patients underwent PSMA-PET and conventional imaging, with histopathology or predefined composite criteria as the reference standard. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 and QUADAS-C. Pooled sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using bivariate composite-likelihood models. Modality effects were tested by meta-regression and likelihood ratio tests, and absolute between-modality differences with 95% CIs were estimated using the delta method. RESULTS: Forty-three studies including 4,023 patients were analyzed. For local T staging, PSMA-PET did not show uniform superiority over mpMRI. For extraprostatic extension, PSMA-PET/CT did not differ significantly from mpMRI in sensitivity (absolute difference, -7.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -16.1 to 0.9; p = 0.08) or specificity (-7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -14.7 to 0.8; p = 0.08); no significant differences were observed for seminal vesicle invasion. In an exploratory six-study comparison, PSMA-PET/MRI had higher sensitivity than mpMRI for extraprostatic extension (+ 12.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.9 to 22.2; p = 0.02). For regional lymph node staging, PSMA-PET/CT sensitivity was 69.3% (95% CI, 56.6-79.7) versus 45.3% (95% CI, 33.0-58.3) for mpMRI (difference, + 24.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.0-40.3; p = 0.009), whereas specificity did not differ (difference, + 3.2 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.6 to 11.8; p = 0.41). For bone metastasis staging, PSMA-PET had greater sensitivity than BS (95.8% [95% CI, 92.8-98.7] versus 76.2% [95% CI, 68.7-83.8]) and greater specificity (92.8% [95% CI, 89.9-95.7] versus 77.4% [95% CI, 71.3-83.5]; both p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: PSMA-PET/CT was more sensitive than mpMRI for regional lymph node staging, while specificity was comparable. PSMA-PET had greater sensitivity and specificity than bone scintigraphy for bone metastasis staging. For local T staging, PSMA-PET did not show uniform superiority over mpMRI.

tag.summary: Meta-analysis comparing prostate-specific membrane antigen imaging with conventional staging. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: AI-based automated body composition analysis from whole-body MRI and (PET-) CT: an intermodal comparison from same-day examinations.
paper.mesh: Humans; Magnetic Resonance Imaging; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Whole Body Imaging; Male; Female; Body Composition; Multiple Myeloma; Retrospective Studies; Aged; Middle Aged; Fluorodeoxyglucose F18
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND: To determine intermodal agreement of AI-derived volumetric body composition metrics between [18 F]FDG-PET/CT-derived low-dose CT and whole-body MRI (wb-MRI). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed same-day whole-body low-dose CT, obtained from [18F]FDG-PET/CT, and wb-MRI from consecutive multiple myeloma patients from the prospective GMMG-HD7- and GMMG-HD8-/DSMM-XIX-trials. An automated deep learning pipeline based on the TotalSegmentator model, and its MRI variant were used to segment skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous- (SAT) and abdominal visceral adipose tissue (VAT) from CT and MRI, respectively. Volumetric measures and single-slice estimates were derived. Agreement between CT- and MRI-based metrics was assessed using Pearson r, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland-Altman analyses. RESULTS: Forty-two multiple myeloma patients with same-day PET/CT and wb-MRI were included. For AI-based volumetric body composition metrics, CT and MRI demonstrated high agreement (ICC > 0.95) across all SM, SAT and VAT. However, Bland-Altmann plots revealed systematic modality-related differences between MRI and CT: both SM (bias: -2582 ml, p < 0.0001) and VAT (bias: -211 ml, p < 0.0001) were significantly lower when extracted from MRI compared to CT, while for SAT, the difference was not statistically significant (bias: -263 ml, p = 0.1629). For AI-based single slice analysis, agreement remained high for SAT and VAT (ICC > 0.97), while being lower for SM (ICC 0.87). Bland-Altman plots showed that SM was systematically and significantly lower when obtained from MRI than from CT (bias: -18.4cm2, p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: Automated body composition measures from (PET-)CT and wb-MRI are highly concordant but show consistent intermodal biases that should be considered when pooling multimodal data or applying modality-agnostic thresholds. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

tag.summary: Artificial intelligence body composition analysis compared across imaging modalities. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Pancreatic Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasm in a Carrier of a Reported Pathogenic BRCA2 Variant: Diagnostic Considerations and Management Using European and International Guidelines.
paper.abstract: Pathogenic germline variants in BRCA2 are associated with increased susceptibility to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and may prompt pancreatic surveillance in selected high-risk individuals. Whether BRCA2 status increases the prevalence or alters the biological behavior of intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) remains uncertain. We report a 71-year-old Latin American woman with a reported heterozygous pathogenic BRCA2 variant and a remote history of stage IA hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast carcinoma. The original molecular genetics report was unavailable; therefore, the exact variant designation, testing platform, laboratory classification, and American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG)/Association of Molecular Pathology (AMP) evidence could not be independently verified. In June 2025, during long-term oncologic follow-up, positron emission tomography-computed tomography incidentally identified a 21×21 mm pancreatic tail cyst. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) in July 2025 demonstrated a 22×20 mm cyst communicating with the main pancreatic duct (MPD), which measured 5 mm. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) demonstrated a 20×23 mm septated cyst without mural nodules or a solid component. Serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA 19-9) was 21.4 U/mL. Cyst fluid glucose was 12 mg/dL, amylase 316 U/L, and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) 247 ng/mL. Cytologic examination and an adequate cell-block specimen obtained by EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) demonstrated papillary mucinous epithelium with gastric-type features, favoring a low-grade IPMN. No immunohistochemical studies were performed, and the specimens were evaluated by a gastrointestinal pathologist. The case was reviewed by a multidisciplinary team in August 2025. The 5 mm MPD represented a relative indication for surgery under the 2018 European evidence-based guidelines and a worrisome feature under contemporary international criteria, but no absolute or high-risk indication for resection was identified. Surveillance was selected. Computed tomography (CT) in December 2025 showed a stable 22×20 mm cyst and a 5 mm MPD; serum CA 19-9 was 24.7 U/mL. In May 2026, the cyst measured 22×21 mm, and the MPD remained 5 mm. The patient remained clinically stable and asymptomatic without pancreatitis, obstructive jaundice, abdominal pain, weight loss, or other symptoms attributable to the lesion. This case illustrates the integration of lesion-specific morphology, ductal anatomy, pathology, longitudinal imaging, and hereditary-risk context without using reported BRCA2 status alone as an indication for pancreatic resection.

tag.summary: Case report of a pancreatic neoplasm in a BRCA2 variant carrier. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis mimicking seronegative rheumatoid arthritis: a case report of destructive erosive arthritis with partial response to Upadacitinib.
paper.abstract: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis (MRH) is a rare non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis that can mimic seronegative rheumatoid arthritis through destructive inflammatory arthritis and papulonodular skin lesions. We report a 44-year-old woman with progressive polyarthritis, purplish papulonodular lesions and destructive erosive disease of the hands and feet. Rheumatoid factor, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody and antinuclear antibody were negative. Radiographs showed sharply demarcated erosions with prominent distal interphalangeal involvement, and skin biopsy confirmed MRH. Available malignancy screening, including oncology review, mammography, cervical screening and blood tests, was reassuring, although planned PET-CT was not completed due to loss to follow-up. Methotrexate and corticosteroids were not tolerated, certolizumab produced partial response, and upadacitinib led to modest cutaneous improvement but persistent active synovitis at four months. This case highlights MRH as a diagnostic mimic of seronegative rheumatoid arthritis and illustrates discordant treatment response to JAK inhibition.

tag.summary: Case report of multicentric reticulohistiocytosis mimicking rheumatoid arthritis. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Preoperative 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography maximum standardized uptake value is independently associated with overall survival in surgically resected undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma.
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS) is the most common adult soft tissue sarcoma subtype, with heterogeneous survival despite optimal surgery. We evaluated whether the preoperative maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) on 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) is independently associated with overall survival (OS) in surgically resected UPS. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 79 patients with localized UPS who underwent curative resection between 2015 and 2023. Preoperative SUVmax, tumor grade (French Federation of Cancer Centers Sarcoma Group), tumor size, and Ki-67 index were assessed. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors for OS. RESULTS: The median age was 59 (range: 18-92) years; 53.2% of patients were male, and 59.5% of tumors were high grade. The median tumor size, Ki-67 index, and SUVmax were 60 mm, 60%, and 10, respectively. At a median follow-up of 58.9 months, median OS was not reached. In univariable analysis, tumor size (P = 0.007), Ki-67 (P = 0.001), SUVmax [hazard ratio: 1.08 per unit, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.04-1.10, P = 0.001], and high grade (P = 0.003) were associated with worse OS. In multivariable analysis, only SUVmax remained independently associated with OS (adjusted hazard ratio: 1.06 per unit, 95% CI: 1.02-1.10, P = 0.002), whereas grade, size, and Ki-67 did not retain significance. CONCLUSION: Preoperative 18F-FDG PET/CT SUVmax is independently associated with OS in surgically resected UPS and provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinicopathological parameters.

tag.summary: Preoperative tracer uptake associated with survival in resected pleomorphic sarcoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: A Comprehensive Review of PET Chemical Depolymerization: Mechanisms, Catalyst Design, and Process Intensification Toward Closed-Loop Recycling.
paper.abstract: The massive accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste necessitates efficient recycling technologies to mitigate environmental pollution. Chemical depolymerization converts PET into high-purity monomers, offering a promising route for closed-loop plastic circularity. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in catalytic PET depolymerization, emphasizing reaction mechanisms, catalyst design, and process intensification. We analyze major depolymerization routes, namely hydrolysis, methanolysis, glycolysis, and aminolysis while highlighting fundamental mechanistic insights such as nucleophilic transesterification and emerging β-cleavage pathways. Furthermore, we evaluate catalyst design principles for active sites (e.g., Brønsted and Lewis acids, bridged bimetallic centers, and defect-engineered structures) across various homogeneous and heterogeneous systems, including ionic liquids, metal-organic frameworks, and zeolites. Finally, we highlight recent progress in process intensification strategies, such as interfacial catalysis, microwave-assisted reactions, and tandem one-pot processes. By integrating mechanistic understanding with catalyst engineering, this review provides a comprehensive perspective and outlines future directions for sustainable, industrially viable closed-loop PET recycling.

tag.summary: Comprehensive review of PET chemical depolymerisation mechanisms and catalyst design; a recycling review.

paper.title: Personalized Management of Erdheim-Chester Disease: The Pivotal Role of Molecular and Cross-Sectional Imaging from Staging to Targeted Therapy Monitoring.
paper.abstract: Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD) is a rare, clonal non-Langerhans cell histiocytic neoplasm driven by activating mutations in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway, most notably the BRAF-V600E mutation. The discovery of these molecular alterations has shifted the therapeutic paradigm from non-specific immunosuppression to personalized targeted therapies, such as BRAF and MEK inhibitors, dramatically improving patient outcomes. Given its protean and insidious systemic manifestations, imaging plays an indispensable role in the personalized diagnostic and therapeutic pathway of ECD. Metadiaphyseal symmetrical osteosclerosis represents the skeletal hallmark, while extraskeletal involvement typically affects the cardiovascular, retroperitoneal, pulmonary, and central nervous systems, yielding pathognomonic imaging signatures such as the "coated aorta" and "hairy kidney." Advanced cross-sectional techniques-including CT, MRI, and organ-specific mapping protocols-are crucial for baseline phenotype characterization, risk stratification, and guiding biopsies toward hypermetabolic sites for biomarker detection. Furthermore, molecular imaging with 18F-FDG PET/CT has emerged as the cornerstone for baseline systemic staging and quantitative metabolic response monitoring via PERCIST criteria, enabling early assessment of targeted treatment efficacy long before morphological changes occur. This review illustrates the multimodality imaging spectrum of ECD based on our institutional experience, emphasizing how precision imaging integrates with molecular profiling to guide personalized patient management.

tag.summary: Review of molecular and cross-sectional imaging in Erdheim-Chester disease. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Self-Monitoring Theranostic Nanomaterials for Biomedical Imaging and Cancer Therapy: Real-Time Visualization of Biodistribution, Payload Release, and Therapeutic Response.
paper.abstract: Theranostic nanomedicines integrate therapeutic delivery with diagnostic imaging, but many conventional platforms primarily visualize nanocarrier localization and provide limited information on whether the therapeutic payload has been released, the intended treatment mechanism has been activated, or a meaningful biological response has occurred. Self-monitoring theranostic nanomedicines have emerged as functionally informative platforms capable of reporting their own biodistribution, biological fate, payload release, therapeutic activation, and downstream response in real time or through longitudinal imaging. This review summarizes the conceptual framework and design principles of self-monitoring nanomedicine, including always-on and activatable probes, Förster resonance energy transfer, self-quenching and dequenching mechanisms, ratiometric sensing, environment-responsive contrast agents, and multimodal imaging. Major imaging modalities, including fluorescence, magnetic resonance, photoacoustics, positron emission tomography, single-photon emission computed tomography, computed tomography, and ultrasound imaging, are discussed with emphasis on their respective capabilities and limitations for monitoring nanomedicine performance. Representative studies demonstrate the visualization of systemic biodistribution, target-site accumulation, carrier disassembly, drug and nucleic-acid release, photothermal and photodynamic activation, gene and RNA activity, oxidative stress, immune modulation, apoptosis, and pathogen clearance. Particular emphasis is placed on cancer theranostics, where self-monitoring nanomaterials can integrate tumor imaging with the assessment of intratumoral delivery, payload release, therapeutic activation, and early treatment response. Broader applications in inflammatory and immune-related diseases and infectious diseases further illustrate the general applicability of these monitoring principles beyond cancer. Despite substantial progress, clinical translation remains limited by ambiguous signal interpretation, insufficient quantitative validation, biological safety concerns, manufacturing complexity, and regulatory challenges. Future development should prioritize mechanistically defined and clinically actionable signals, orthogonal validation, standardized reporting, biodegradable and clearable materials, reproducible manufacturing, and compatibility with established imaging workflows. Self-monitoring theranostic nanomedicines may ultimately enable the transition from image-guided drug delivery to feedback-guided, adaptive, and personalized precision therapy.

tag.summary: Review of self-monitoring theranostic nanomaterials for imaging and cancer therapy. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Occurrence of Microplastics and Potentially Toxic Elements in Red Sea Crab (Portunus pelagicus) and Squid (Uroteuthis spp.): Contamination and Food-Safety Concerns.
paper.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and potentially toxic elements (PTEs) are co-occurring marine contaminants, yet integrated assessments of Red Sea seafood remain limited. This study evaluated MP contamination, PTE bioaccumulation, and dietary health risks in Portunus pelagicus (n = 281) and Uroteuthis spp. (n = 159) from Yanbu, Rabigh, and Umluj. A standardized subset of 180 specimens was examined for MPs using stereomicroscopy, yielding 508 suspected particles. All 508 particles were examined by FTIR, of which 260 (51.2%) were spectroscopically confirmed as polyethylene (PE), while 248 (48.8%) remained unconfirmed. Crabs showed approximately 10-89-fold higher suspected-particle burdens than squid (0.742-1.683 vs. 0.008-0.167 particles/g wet weight). Eleven PTEs were quantified in edible muscle by ICP-MS. Squid contained approximately 17-24-fold higher Fe and 5-7-fold higher Cd, whereas crabs contained 11-13-fold higher total As and higher Zn. Non-carcinogenic risk remained below the conventional threshold (HI < 1) across all scenarios, whereas estimated arsenic-related carcinogenic risk exceeded 1 × 10-4 in some crab-consumption scenarios under the assumed 7% inorganic-As fraction. Exploratory MP-PTE associations were strongly influenced by species identity and cannot establish MP-mediated PTE transfer.

tag.summary: Microplastics and toxic elements measured in Red Sea crab and squid; a food contamination survey.

paper.title: Organ-specific depth of response to CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in B-cell lymphomas.
paper.mesh: Humans; Female; Male; Retrospective Studies; Middle Aged; Aged; Antigens, CD19; Immunotherapy, Adoptive; Lymphoma, B-Cell; Receptors, Chimeric Antigen
paper.abstract: BACKGROUND: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CART) has transformed treatment of relapsed or refractory (r/r) large B cell lymphoma (LBCL); however, organ-specific response patterns and depth of response (DoR) remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated organ-specific imaging response and the impact of spatial disease patterns on progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 109 consecutive patients with r/r LBCL treated with CD19-directed CART between January 2019 and May 2025 were included. Baseline and follow-up CT or PET/CT was analyzed using structured lesion tracking. Up to six target lesions per patient were assessed according to Lugano criteria, and the sum of the products of diameters (SPD) was calculated. DoR was defined as percentage change in SPD from baseline. Associations with PFS and OS were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. RESULTS: Among 109 patients (median age, 65 years [IQR, 57-71]), 65 (59.6%) had extranodal disease at baseline. Baseline tumor burden was higher in patients with extranodal than nodal disease (median SPD, 3573 mm2 [IQR, 1314-9708] versus 1998 mm2 [IQR, 1347-2921]). DoR was comparable between nodal and extranodal lesions at both time points (- 62.1% vs. - 65.6% and - 77.9% vs. - 78.1%); this comparability at the second follow-up may partly reflect differential attrition, as extranodal patients were more likely to be lost to follow-up before this timepoint. Despite similar tumor reduction, median PFS was 306.5 days in nodal versus 90 days in extranodal disease. Baseline tumor burden (SPD) was independently associated with both PFS and OS (HR per doubling of SPD 1.17 and 1.21, respectively). Pleural, hepatobiliary, and adrenal involvement showed the strongest associations with adverse outcomes in this exploratory, hypothesis-generating organ-level analysis; pleural involvement remained independently associated with PFS and OS, though organ-specific subgroups were small (n = 7-19) and estimates should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: Tumor reduction occurs in nodal and extranodal disease after CART, but outcomes depend on anatomical disease distribution. Pleural and hepatobiliary involvement emerged as candidate high-risk imaging phenotypes in this exploratory analysis, warranting confirmation in larger, multicenter cohorts. Organ-specific assessment may provide information beyond global tumor burden.
