DISCUSSION: Foreign-body reaction against sutures and meshes employed in abdominal surgery has been widely analysed in experimental models. Lymphocytes and histiocytes are the main inflammatory cells responsible for this reaction. In the literature there are few reports of foreign-body reaction mimicking peritoneal seeding of carcinomas, and all of them were diagnosed with a biopsy of suspicious nodules. A thorough review of the literature has not revealed any similar case in which FNAC allowed diagnosis of foreign body reaction avoiding the need of surgical exploration and unnecessary systemic therapy. CONCLUSION: We herein report a unique case in which FNAC led to the correct diagnosis of a foreign body reaction, avoiding aggressive measures in an oncologic patient.

tag.summary: Cytology of a postoperative foreign body reaction mimicking peritoneal metastasis. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Unveiling the heterogeneity: PD-L1 expression and metabolic activity in primary vs. metastatic NSCLC, a retrospective single-center analysis.
paper.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression was different in primary tumors (PT) and metastatic tumors (MT). Total-body positron-emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) comprehensively visualizes primary lesions and metastases. We aimed to explore the heterogeneity of PD-L1 high expression and metabolic activity between primary and metastatic lesions in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: Immunohistochemistry analysis (IHC) was conducted for PD-L1 expression on tumor cells (TC) and tumor-infiltrating immune cells (IC) with 22C3 antibody. PD-L1 positive scores on TC no less than 50% or IC no less than 10% was defined as high expression. Total 598 (456 adenocarcinoma (ADC) and 142 squamous cell lung carcinoma (SCC)) primary diagnosed NSCLC patients who underwent 18F-FDG-PET/CT imaging were collected retrospectively. The statistic methods included chi-square test, Mann Whitney test and multivariate regression. RESULTS: 598 patients included 441 with PD-L1 low expression and 157 high expression. In all subtypes and ADC, MT had higher PD-L1 high expression (P = 0.023 and P = 0.010, respectively). The maximum standard uptake value (SUVmax) of PD-L1 high expression was significantly higher than that of PD-L1 low expression, no matter in PT or MT (15.23 (8.85) vs 9.42 (8.34), P<0.001; 13.36 (5.55) vs 8.52 (6.93), P<0.001). The squamous-cell-carcinoma metastatic-lesion analyses were exploratory owing to the very small sample size and risk of type-II statistical error. Multivariate regression indicated that SUVmax was independently associated with PD-L1 high expression. In all metastatic sites, we compared the SUVmax of MT and paired PT and found SUVmax was higher in PT than MT in PD-L1 low expression subgroup (11.39 (8.12) vs 8.52 (6.93), P = 0.002). For lymph node metastases, SUVmax was significantly elevated in PT compared to MT in PD-L1 low expression (13.71 (7.95) vs 8.54 (7.30), P = 0.002), whereas no correlation was observed in PD-L1 high expression. DISCUSSION: Both PD-L1 expression and metabolism exhibited heterogeneity between primary tumors and their metastases. Compared to the primary tumors, different types of metastatic tumors showed variations not only in PD-L1 expression but also in their metabolic parameter. Utilizing whole-body PET/CT imaging facilitates the selection of optimal biopsy sites by providing metabolic reference data pertinent to clinical practice.

tag.summary: PD-L1 expression and metabolic activity compared in primary and metastatic lung cancer. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Distant Cutaneous Metastasis as the First Sign of Recurrence After R0 Resection of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: A Case Report.
paper.abstract: Cutaneous metastasis from cholangiocarcinoma is rare and typically occurs at surgical incision sites or along drainage tracts due to tumor implantation, whereas distant cutaneous metastasis unrelated to surgical procedures is extremely uncommon and generally indicates a poor prognosis. We report the case of a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma after a low-density lesion was detected in the left lateral liver segment during postoperative surveillance following nephrectomy for renal cell carcinoma. He underwent left hepatectomy with caudate lobectomy and hepatoduodenal ligament lymphadenectomy, and pathological examination revealed pT2N0M0, stage II disease (AJCC 8th edition). No adjuvant chemotherapy was administered. Eight months after surgery, a painless, mobile subcutaneous mass appeared on the right posterior trunk and was clinically diagnosed as a lipoma. At 14 months postoperatively, the lesion became painful, and partial excision at another hospital revealed a metastatic cutaneous tumor. Subsequent FDG-PET/CT demonstrated uptake in the cutaneous lesion as well as in the right iliac and left femoral bones. Immunohistochemical findings supported cutaneous metastasis from intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The patient received radiotherapy for bone metastasis and systemic chemotherapy, but despite temporary disease control, his condition gradually deteriorated, and he died 56 months after surgery. This case highlights that distant cutaneous metastasis from intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma may initially present as a benign-appearing postoperative subcutaneous mass and can be easily overlooked. Because cutaneous lesions are readily accessible for diagnostic evaluation, newly developed postoperative subcutaneous masses should be carefully assessed even when serum tumor markers and imaging studies show no evidence of recurrence.

tag.summary: Case report of cutaneous metastasis after resection of cholangiocarcinoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: High-Resolution Imaging via UHF-US-Based 3D Reconstruction in a 3D In Vivo Tumor Model.
paper.abstract: The chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model resembles a preclinical in vivo platform for the engraftment of different tumors and is especially well-suited for the development and evaluation of novel cancer therapies. Due to the CAM's extensive vascular network, it can sustain engrafted human tumor tissue, which can be used for therapy testing and analysis throughout the experimental process. Although numerous studies have demonstrated successful tumor engraftment and vascular integration into the CAM's blood vessel network, the accurate and sequential measurement of tumor volume remains a significant challenge. Current imaging modalities, such as positron emission tomography/computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging or three-dimensional (3D) digital microscopy are limited by cost, complexity, and potential harm due to injected agents or radiation. This study introduces an innovative imaging approach by utilizing ultrahigh frequency (UHF) ultrasound combined with 3D ultrasound reconstruction of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) on the CAM. By utilizing ultrasound frequencies of up to 71 MHz, two-dimensional (2D) imaging of PDAC tumors was transformed into comprehensive 3D reconstructions. This innovative approach provides a more detailed tissue resolution and enables noninvasive, longitudinal volumetric monitoring of tumor growth in vivo, and in principle provides a platform for future studies assessing angiogenesis and therapy response. In this study the accuracy of 3D UHF ultrasound was tested by comparing it with established imaging techniques such as 3D digital microscopy. In summary, the 3D ultrasound reconstruction resembles a more versatile noninvasive alternative for in vivo tumor volume measurement. This advanced imaging approach adds a valuable methodology for the investigation of tumor biology in the CAM model by providing noninvasive volumetric and morphological characterization of engrafted tumor tissue, thereby linking preclinical research and clinical applications.

tag.summary: High-resolution ultrasound reconstruction demonstrated in a tumour model. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Role of PET/CT in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Review).
paper.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and its diagnosis and management are moving steadily toward personalization and precision. As a functional imaging modality, positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET/CT) plays an irreplaceable role in the management of DLBCL. For diagnosis and staging, PET/CT corrects staging errors made with CT alone and improves the detection of bone marrow involvement; baseline metabolic parameters [metabolic tumor volume (MTV) and total lesion glycolysis] and measures of disease dissemination (Dmax) are independent prognostic factors, and MTV in particular refines the risk stratification provided by the International Prognostic Index. During therapy, an interim ΔSUVmax reduction of ≤66% indicates high-risk patients, while a negative interim Deauville score (1-3) and a negative end-of-treatment PET/CT both predict favorable long-term survival. Before chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy and autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, metabolic parameters also carry predictive value for both outcome and toxicity. In addition, radiomics combined with multiparametric data improves prognostic accuracy, and novel tracers and PET/MR offer complementary advantages for distinguishing tumor from inflammation and for assessing extranodal disease. Taken together, PET/CT provides a precise evaluation platform that spans the entire course of diagnosis and treatment. The present study systematically reviews the application of PET/CT to the diagnosis, prognostic prediction, response assessment and special clinical scenarios of DLBCL.

tag.summary: Review of imaging in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Machine Learning Regression-Enhanced Property Prediction of Brush Particle Solids.
paper.abstract: The development of advanced hybrid materials such as polymer-grafted nanoparticles (aka "brush" or "hairy" particles) hinges on the ability to accurately predict suitable compositions to realize desired functionalities. Such systems are characterized by expensive synthesis, sparse data, and large parameter spaces that often render physics-based modeling or experimental exploration of structure-property relationships expensive and impractical. Regression models provide a versatile data-driven alternative to establish empirical structure-property relations. However, the implications of sparse data availability and method of training on the predictive capability of regression models outside of the respective range of training data is poorly understood. This work presents a comparative analysis of widely used linear and nonlinear models versus machine learning regression models to evaluate their ability to predict the elastic modulus of brush particle solids formed by poly-(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) and polystyrene (PS) tethered silica nanoparticles with systematic variation of the degree of polymerization, dispersity, and grafting density. The methods investigated include k-nearest neighbors, multilayer perceptron, and XGBoost regression. The performance of each model is assessed on a consistent set of training and testing data. Within the experimental certainty, the k-nearest neighbors regressor and XGBoost were found to provide the most reliable property prediction. Combining data sets of disparate polymer systems (PMMA/PS) was found to increase the accuracy of prediction and to enable models to forecast previously reported unexpected behavior outside of the range of the original training data. This supports the use of trained regression models as capable exploratory tools to reveal structure-property relations for systems that are controlled by multiple parameters with unknown interactions.

tag.summary: Machine learning regression used to predict properties of polymer-grafted particle solids; a materials paper.

paper.title: Spatial organisation of microplastics in road runoff across an urban network.
paper.abstract: Road runoff is a major pathway by which microplastics are transported from urban surfaces to aquatic ecosystems, yet the spatial scales over which measurements represent road networks remain unresolved. This constrains source attribution, monitoring design and urban emission inventories. Using high-resolution µFTIR imaging, we quantified microplastic abundance, particle-size distribution and polymer composition in runoff across an interconnected urban road network following a rainfall mobilisation event, characterising twenty-one polymer types across four particle-size fractions. Concentrations spanned more than an order of magnitude (18-544 particles L⁻¹), varying sharply even between road only 114 m apart. Compositional dissimilarity showed no significant relationship with inter-site distance, instead revealing a mosaic of locally distinct polymer assemblages, with significantly greater heterogeneity in the urban core. Cellulose acetate, polyurethane, polymethyl-methacrylate and polypropylene dominated, reflecting diverse sources. In contrast, 25-50 µm particles consistently dominated, accounting for ∼84% of particles, indicating a common fine-particle transport signature despite pronounced spatial variability in polymer composition. These reveal for the first time, that fine-scale spatial heterogeneity, rather than geographic distance, is the defining characteristic of microplastic distributions in road runoff. Resolving this is therefore fundamental to establishing the representativeness of urban microplastic measurements, without which risk assessments remain inherently uncertain.

tag.summary: Spatial organisation of microplastics measured in road runoff across an urban network; an environmental survey.

paper.title: Silver nanodot embedded waste PET nanofibres for efficient multifunctional air filter.
paper.abstract: This study focuses on conversion of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into ultrafine nanofibres with silver nanodots (AgND) (diameter 3.49 ± 0.94 nm) embedded within via electrospinning. Ultrafine PET (diameter 74 ± 15 nm) or PET-AgND (diameter 68 ± 17.4 nm) nanofibre-based membranes (basis weight 0.5 ± 0.02 g/m2, thickness 20 ± 1.4 μm), sandwiched between two spun-bond nonwoven layers, achieved a remarkable particle filtration efficiency (PFE) of 99.24-99.93% against 10-1000 nm particles, while maintaining pressure drop (ΔP) of 13 Pa at a face velocity of 5 cm/s. Such 3-ply filters demonstrated PFE > 99.5% against 350 nm particles with ΔP between 13-27 Pa over 28 consecutive filtration cycles. The PET-AgND membranes also demonstrated antibacterial efficacy of 99.78 ± 0.18% against Escherichia coli and 99.92 ± 0.02% against Staphylococcus aureus, respectively. Washability assessments showed reduction of PFE from 99.7% to 57.6% with increment in pressure drop from 13 to 79 Pa, from unwashed till 9 washing-drying trials. The 3-ply filters also exhibited significant air permeability (64.4 ± 0.25 cm3/cm2-s), water vapor transmission rate (82.45 ± 2.7 g3/m2-h) coupled with prominent UV protection (79.5%). This study highlights a sustainable route for converting waste PET into high-performance, multifunctional, filter media.

tag.summary: Waste PET converted into silver-embedded nanofibres for air filtration; a materials paper.

paper.title: 0The long-term burden: Chronic exposure to nylon-6 microfibres alters the growth of Lumbriculus variegatus (Oligochaeta).
paper.abstract: Microplastics (<5 mm) (MP) are a complex group of emerging contaminants. Their origin (e.g., custom made MP for certain applications) can play a crucial role in their distribution and toxicity in biota. To address this gap, we investigated the chronic effects of nylon-6 microfibres (Ø = 14 μm, length = 500 μm) on the endobenthic oligochaete Lumbriculus variegatus, a model freshwater species which is present in a wide variety of habitats in most continents. Experimental vessels consisted of natural lake sediment (70 g), spiked with the fibres at concentrations of 0.01, 0.1 and 3% of sediment dwt and 150 mL of artificial freshwater (AFW). Additional controls (n=3) without fibres were also set. Ten worms were added per replicate and two timepoints (28 d and 30 w) were assessed. Furthermore, the burrowing behaviour after 30 w was assessed by photographing the lateral profiles of sediments. Results after the 28 d of exposure indicated no effect on the reproduction and growth of the worms with any of the concentrations of microfibres used. However, after 30 w, while the reproduction was not affected, worms exposed to the highest concentrations showed a significantly lower dry weight compared to those in all the other treatments. Furthermore, a reduction in the burrowing patterns of worms was observed at the highest concentrations of microfibres, however, due to the methodology used, this is only a semiquantitative estimation. Overall, in addition to the important information on the environmental toxicology of nylon-6 microfibres, this study highlights the importance of introducing long term exposures in ecotoxicology tests, also for other anthropogenic chemicals. This would improve the environmental significance of the existing data that could be used to enhance environmental risk assessment.

tag.summary: Chronic exposure to nylon-6 microfibres altered growth in the freshwater oligochaete Lumbriculus variegatus.

paper.title: Vehicle interiors as mobile reservoirs of urban microplastics: seasonal accumulation, polymer composition and occupant exposure inferred from car wash vacuum debris.
paper.abstract: Vehicle cabins are enclosed, plastic rich spaces that people occupy daily, yet the microplastics that accumulate inside them are rarely measured. Debris removed by car wash vacuum cleaners offers a direct and largely unexploited window on that accumulation and is itself an unmanaged urban waste stream. We quantified the abundance, morphology, colour and polymer composition of microplastics in vacuum debris from 15 formal car wash facilities in Mbombela (formerly Nelspruit), South Africa, spanning three land use zones (low density residential, central business district and industrial) and three seasons (hot-wet, cool-dry and hot-dry) in 2025, with 100 samples per season. Samples were density separated in zinc chloride (1.7 g cm-3), vacuum filtered, enumerated by stereomicroscopy (×80) and confirmed by Fourier transform infrared micro-spectroscopy. Microplastics were detected at every facility, although the proportion of individual samples with no detectable particles rose sharply in the hot-dry season, from 2.9 % to 74.3 % in the low density zone. Abundance peaked in the hot-wet season and was highest in the low density zone (4 480 ± 3 260 particles kg-1). Fragments dominated, followed by fibres, foams, films and beads, and both morphotype and colour composition shifted with season and land use. Fourier-transform infrared micro-spectroscopy identified a polymer suite consistent with vehicle interior materials and occupant-derived debris, led by polydimethylsiloxane, poly (vinyl chloride) and poly (methyl methacrylate). Season explained substantially more variation in estimated occupant exposure than land use zone (partial η2 = 0.265-0.280 versus 0.014-0.019), and ingestion of settled dust accounted for 94-96 % of estimated annual fibre exposure against 4-6 % for inhalation. Car wash vacuum debris therefore functions both as an integrative indicator of the microplastics urban residents encounter inside vehicles and as an overlooked point source of secondary microplastic release where it is disposed of without containment.

tag.summary: Microplastics accumulating in vehicle cabins quantified from car wash debris with occupant exposure estimates; an exposure survey.

paper.title: Cutaneous clues: Malignant acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms as first signs of recurrent endometrial carcinoma.
paper.mesh: Humans; Female; Endometrial Neoplasms; Aged; Acanthosis Nigricans; Neoplasm Recurrence, Local; Carcinoma, Endometrioid; Paraneoplastic Syndromes; Lymphatic Metastasis
paper.abstract: OBJECTIVE: 'Tripe palm' is a rare cutaneous paraneoplastic syndrome characterized by velvety thickening of the palms with a ridged or rugose appearance. The condition, either on its own or in combination with acanthosis nigricans, is strongly associated with internal malignancies, particularly gastric and lung cancers. Reports linking malignant acanthosis nigricans to endometrial cancer are scarce. Even more uncommon is its presentation as an initial sign of recurrent disease. CASE REPORT: We report a rare case of acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms in a 73-year-old woman who had completed treatment for stage IB endometrial endometrioid adenocarcinoma and remained disease-free for six years. She was referred by a dermatologist for evaluation of potential underlying malignancy. Chest CT, panendoscopy, and colonoscopy showed no significant findings. However, a PET/CT scan revealed a suspicious lymph node metastasis in the portocaval region. Laparoscopic excision of the retroperitoneal lymph nodes was performed, and pathological examination confirmed metastatic endometrioid adenocarcinoma with microscopic features consistent with the original endometrial carcinoma. CONCLUSION: Acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms are rarely linked to endometrial cancer, especially as indicators of recurrence. Gynecologic oncologists should recognize these cutaneous clues during patient surveillance, even if the patient has been disease-free for many years following treatment.

tag.summary: Case report of paraneoplastic skin signs heralding recurrent endometrial carcinoma. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.

paper.title: Companion animal nuclear medicine: A translational evidence map for dogs and cats.
paper.abstract: Companion animals occupy an increasingly important clinical and societal space, with dogs and cats often managed as family members and receiving advanced diagnostic and therapeutic care. Many veterinary nuclear medicine procedures are adapted from human practice, while naturally occurring canine and feline diseases provide opportunities for comparative and translational insight. This review mapped and synthesised the literature on nuclear medicine imaging and radionuclide therapy in dogs and cats, with emphasis on clinically mature applications and relevance to human nuclear medicine. A PRISMA-aligned systematic evidence map with focused narrative synthesis were undertaken. MEDLINE via PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection were searched, with supplementary Google Scholar searching, reference-list screening and citation mining. Because of heterogeneity in species, indication, radiopharmaceutical, protocol, comparator and outcome reporting, formal meta-analysis was not performed. A total of 228 articles were included. The literature was predominantly imaging-focused, with 176 articles addressing imaging alone, 34 therapy alone and 18 both imaging and therapy. Feline nuclear medicine was dominated by thyroid disease, particularly thyroid scintigraphy and radioiodine therapy for hyperthyroidism. Canine nuclear medicine was broader, including oncology PET/CT, osteosarcoma imaging and therapy, renal and hepatobiliary functional scintigraphy, portosystemic shunt imaging, neurology/behavioural imaging, thyroid carcinoma and radiosynoviorthesis. PET/CT was most prominent in canine oncology, while conventional scintigraphy remained important where functional information could not be replaced by structural imaging. Companion animal nuclear medicine is clinically useful and translationally relevant. Its most mature model is feline thyroid scintigraphy and radioiodine therapy, while its most dynamic future directions lie in canine oncology, molecular imaging and radiotheranostics. Closer collaboration between veterinary specialists and human nuclear medicine professionals may improve companion animal care while informing broader development of molecular imaging and targeted radionuclide therapy.

tag.summary: Evidence map of nuclear medicine in companion animals. PET here is positron emission tomography, not polyethylene terephthalate.
